### BD-Matter-CASEServer-ResumedSessionBeforeSigma2Resume — the controller's CASE responder registers a resumed session before Sigma2_Resume

matter.js `CaseServer.ts` at `db021da0` creates the resumed session before
Sigma2_Resume with `delayManagerRegistration` (`:175-188`, `:187`;
`NodeSession.ts:153-155` skips the manager) and adds it to the manager
only after the send (`:211`); a message for it before then is dropped as
one of an unknown session (`ExchangeManager.ts:331-342`).
`handshake.CASEServer.resume` registers it before the send and closes it
when the send fails (`client/handshake/server.go`), the order matter.js
takes after the pin: at `c41eb7da` the session is registered from its
construction (`NodeSession.ts:163-165`), created establishing before the
send (`CaseServer.ts:177-190`) and receives messages in every state
(`NodeSession.ts:223-225`). connectedhomeip drops a message on the
session until the initiator's Success activates it
(`CASESession.cpp:2315-2340` → `PairingSession.cpp:62-66`,
`SessionManager.cpp:1007-1012` at `6170af84`). Reasoning: the initiator sends its first request right after
its Success, and the controller's manager reads it on another goroutine
than the responder's, so a session registered after the send lost that
request over TCP, where nothing retransmits it (release v0.23.0, the
camera tests' "expected message missing after 35s"); only a holder of the
record's shared secret can send on the session (`CaseServer.ts:162-182`
at `db021da0`). Reconciled at the pin lift: the order is matter.js's then,
and `c41eb7da` also closes a resumed session whose Success does not
arrive (`CaseServer.ts:205-211`), which ends the resume half of
`BD-Matter-CASEServer-CloseOnUnfinishedEstablishment`. Pinned by
`TestCASEServerRegistersTheResumedSessionBeforeSigma2Resume`.

At `b25ed960` (pin lift; text final in pin-lift unit P1-A) the claims hold:
the session is registered from its construction (`NodeSession.ts:163-165`),
the resume creates it with `establishing: true` (`CaseServer.ts:177-190`,
`:189`) before `sendSigma2Resume` (`:197-202`), and a message for it is
accepted in every state (`NodeSession.ts:223-225`; the exchange manager looks
sessions up in the registered set, `ExchangeManager.ts:330-340`). The order
mirrors matter.js; the entry stays as a record of the order. The
establishing state is mirrored since pin-lift unit P1-A: the resumed
session is created establishing (`exchangeseam.NewEstablishingSecureSession`,
responder form), listed by `SessionsFor` and its messages processed, not
counted by the per-peer cap, and established on the initiator's Success
(`CaseServer.ts:204-206`).

### BD-Matter-CASEClient-SessionBeforeSigma3 — the CASE initiator registers its session before Sigma3 and holds it until the Success

matter.js `CaseClient.ts` at `db021da0` sends Sigma3 and awaits the
responder's Success (`:335-336`), then creates the session with
`delayManagerRegistration` (`:343-358`, `:356`) and adds it to the
manager (`:369`); a message for the session before then is dropped as one
of an unknown session (`ExchangeManager.ts:331-341`). connectedhomeip
activates the initiator's session when the Success arrives
(`src/protocols/secure_channel/CASESession.cpp:2315-2339` at `6170af84`,
`OnSuccessStatusReport` ending in `Finish()`; the activation is
`PairingSession.cpp:42-66`) and drops a message on a session not yet active
(`src/transport/SessionManager.cpp:1007-1012`); neither holds one.
`handshake.CASE`'s full handshake (`client/handshake/case.go`) registers
the session before Sigma3 goes out, establishing (through
`internal/exchangeseam`): what decrypts on it is held, in order and at
most 16 distinct messages — one beyond that is dropped undecrypted, so its
retransmission is taken; a retransmission of a held message takes no
place — and `exchange.Manager.SessionsFor` does not list it,
until the Success activates it; then the held messages are delivered
before any that follows, and the caller gets the session. A Sigma3 that
cannot be sent, a failure StatusReport and a Success that does not arrive
(timeout, cancellation) close it. Reasoning: a responder can send on the session as soon as its Success is out
— matter.js's has it in the manager before it sends the Success
(`CaseServer.ts:316`, `:332`, `NodeSession.ts:153-155`), connectedhomeip's
activates right after sending it (`CASESession.cpp:2138`, `:2150`) — and the
manager reads that message on its listener goroutine while the handshake's
goroutine still waits for the Success; registered after it,
the message met no session and was dropped — for good over TCP or for a
message sent without an acknowledgement asked. The keys are final once
Sigma2 is processed, so only the responder the handshake authenticated
can send on the session early. The resumption branch is unchanged: its
session is registered before our Success goes out. The row closes when
matter.js's initiator registers the session before Sigma3. Pinned by
`TestCASEInitiatorReceivesTheResponderMessageBeforeSuccess` and
`TestCASEInitiatorClosesTheEstablishingSessionWithoutSuccess`, and in
`client/exchange` by `TestEstablishingSessionHoldsUntilActivated` and
`TestEstablishingSessionClosedDeliversNothing`.

### BD-Matter-CASEServer-NoReportOnShutdown — a handshake the responder's Close cut short reports nothing

matter.js `CaseServer.ts:68-77` logs a `ShutdownError` at info and still
sends InvalidParam unless the exchange is closing (`:84-93`).
`CASEServer.Close` cancels the handshakes in flight and `Serve` sends no
StatusReport for one its context ended. Report AI.

By design. Close precedes the manager's own close; a report sent into a
socket about to close would only fail with a flow error, the case `:84-86`
skips for an exchange already closing.

### BD-Matter-Controller-Sigma1OnSecureSessionIgnored — a Sigma1 on a secure session is acknowledged and dropped

matter.js's full `SecureChannelProtocol` takes every session
(`requiresSecureSession = undefined`, `SecureChannelProtocol.ts:34`) and
hands a Sigma1 to the CaseServer wherever it arrived (`:146-148`).
`exchange.Manager.handlerFor` consults the installed Secure Channel
handler only on an unsecured session; on a secure one a Sigma1 is
acknowledged and dropped as any unhandled message. Report AI.

By design. Session establishment runs over the unsecured session; a
Sigma1 inside an established session is a peer error the controller does
not reward with a second session.

### BD-Matter-Controller-EmptyListsNotEncoded — client requests omit an optional list that is empty

matter.js writes an optional list whenever the field is set, an empty
array included: `#encodeReadingRequest` (`InteractionMessenger.ts:1143-1168` at
`db021da0`) that dropped every DataVersionFilter still sends
`dataVersionFilters: []`. `im.ReadRequest.MarshalTLV`,
`SubscribeRequest.MarshalTLV` and `WriteRequest.MarshalTLV` write a list
only when it has members; the request's space budget still counts the
empty array's three bytes, so what fits is what fits matter.js. Report AI.

By design. Go's nil and empty slice are one value; an empty optional
list carries no information the receiver reads.

### BD-Matter-Controller-NoIMServer — a first Interaction Model message other than a report is answered InvalidAction

matter.js's controller is a ServerNode whose InteractionServer serves a
Read or Invoke a peer opens (`InteractionServer.ts:240-262` at `862ad75f`);
only a ReportData reaches the `ClientSubscriptionHandler`.
`interaction.Subscriptions.HandleExchange` answers any other first IM
message with StatusResponse InvalidAction. Report AI.

By design. The controller of ADR 0020 is not a node and serves no
attributes; InvalidAction is what an InteractionServer answers an
unsupported message (`InteractionMessenger.ts:415-419` at `862ad75f`).

### BD-Matter-Controller-ListIndexPastEnd — a list index past the end of a chunked list makes the entry malformed

matter.js assigns `list[index] = value` (`TlvArray.ts:150` at `0ceb202d`),
which in JavaScript extends the array with holes. The report assembler of
`client/interaction` treats such an entry as malformed and skips it,
as it skips every other malformed entry (`InputChunk.ts:229`, `:352` at `862ad75f`). Report AI.

By design. Go slices do not hold holes; a report whose set-at-index
exceeds the list the peer sent is the peer's defect.

### BD-Matter-Controller-MergedReports — `Updated` receives a report with its chunks merged

matter.js hands a subscription's consumer an iterator of `InputChunk`s
(`ClientSubscriptionHandler.ts:129-138`, `processReports :155-190` at
`862ad75f`). `interaction.SubscribeRequest.Updated` is called once per
report, after its last chunk was assembled and before that chunk's
acknowledgement — the point matter.js's iterator has drained. Report AI.

By design. A Go callback that receives the whole report is the iterator's
equivalent surface; the order of acknowledgement is matter.js's.

### BD-Matter-Controller-InvokeRevision12 — the client's InvokeRequest stamps InteractionModelRevision 12

matter.js's `Invoke()` defaults the request's revision to
`SessionParameters.fallbacks.interactionModelRevision`, 11 (`Invoke.ts:102`,
`SessionParameters.ts:160` at `db021da0`), the value assumed for a peer
whose revision is unknown; its Read and Subscribe stamp
`Specification.INTERACTION_MODEL_REVISION`, 12
(`action/request/Read.ts:40`, `Specification.ts:124`).
`im.InvokeRequest`'s client encoder stamps 12, as every message this
module sends (`BD-Matter-InteractionModelRevision`). Reports AH and AI.

By design. One revision per module; the fallback is not the controller's
own.

---

### BD-Matter-ClientNode-NoGeneratedTypes — the client node carries the shape analysis, not a generated behaviour class

matter.js builds a TypeScript behaviour class per discovered cluster shape
(`PeerBehavior.ts:105-139`, `:169-285` at `0ceb202d`), memoised by a
fingerprint of revision, features, attribute and command ids
(`:290-378`), and installs it on the endpoint so the remote cluster reads
as a typed `state`. Go has no run-time types: `controller/client.Cluster`
carries the analysis those classes are built from (`:422-467` — revision,
features, supported and extra attributes and commands) and its values stay
`spec.Node`, decoded on access through the generated `Attribute.Decode` or
`spec.DecodeValue`. The fingerprint cache is not ported; the shape is
recomputed when its inputs change (`ClientStructure.ts:750-752`, `#invalidateOnDefinitionChange`, at `862ad75f`), which is
what the cache keyed on. Report AK.

By design (brief AK, D2). The same decisions, one struct instead of one
class per shape.

### BD-Matter-ClientNode-UnknownEventsDelivered — every event reaches the host

matter.js drops an event of a cluster or event its model does not know,
with a one-time notice (`ClientEventEmitter.ts:38`, `:143-161` at `b25ed960`),
because it has no generated observable to emit on; the notice's set is
module-wide (`:38`). `controller/client` delivers every event through
`Hooks.Event` with its path and its decoded value, or the raw node when no
definition decodes it; the one-time notice stays as an `Info` line,
remembered per node. Nothing a host could observe in matter.js is lost;
the host sees more. Report AK.

By design (brief AK, D4).

### BD-Matter-ClientNode-WriteNotThroughCache — the image changes when the peer reports, not when the host writes

matter.js sends a client behaviour's write through `RemoteWriter.ts` as
commit phase one of the behaviour's transaction and settles the values the
peer accepts in the cache right away; a declined attribute fails phase one,
which rolls back every participant
(`packages/node/src/storage/client/RemoteWriteParticipant.ts:28-37` at
`862ad75f`; `DatasourceCache.ts:73-130` at `0ceb202d` wrote locally first
and compensated).
`controller/client.Node.Write` forwards to the interaction's Write and
leaves the image alone: the value changes when the peer reports it, which
the default subscription delivers. A host that reads the image right
after a write sees the old value until the report arrives, where matter.js
shows the new one at once; the image never shows a value the peer did not
confirm. Report AK. The write-through, transaction and `RemoteWriter`
cases of ClientNodeTest.ts:1137-2853 (at `862ad75f`, about 60) are
`missing` under this entry; report BI (phase 16, 2026-10-19).

At `b25ed960` the class doc still says this (`RemoteWriteParticipant.ts:28-37`;
`set` queues one prepared write per cluster, `commit1` sends them in one
request and settles the accepted values through `receiver.settleAccepted`,
`:59-96`), and a client write of a fabric-scoped list follows new rules:
`RemoteWriter.prepare` sends only our entries, with our fabric index on the
peer, refuses the whole write with CONSTRAINT_ERROR when that index is
unknown or an entry of another fabric matches no cached entry
(`packages/node/src/storage/client/RemoteWriter.ts:89-142`,
`FabricScopedListWrite.ts:16-30`, `:59-70`), and merges the accepted list into
the cache so that other fabrics' cached entries stay (`RemoteWriter.ts:124-125`,
`:212-215`). This module's side was not compared: whether
`controller/client.Node.Write` filters or refuses a fabric-scoped list as
`FabricScopedListWrite` does was not read (unverified). The entry's reason
covers only the cache, not this entry selection.

By design (brief AK, D6). The compensation machinery is the price of
optimistic local state; the port takes the pessimistic one.

### BD-Matter-ControllerNodeIDRandom — the controller draws a peer's node id at random, never sequentially

matter.js's controller hands out node ids from a stored counter by default
— `ControllerBehavior.allocatePeerAddress` with `nodeIdAssignment:
"sequential"`, `nextNodeId` from 1, skipping an id in use and never
handing one out twice
(`packages/node/src/behavior/system/controller/ControllerBehavior.ts:139-181`,
`:285-295` at `db021da0`) — and draws a random operational id only with
`nodeIdAssignment: "random"` or in `ControllerCommissioner.#determineAddress`
(`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioner.ts:569-582`).
`controller/commissioner.Commissioner.determineAddress` always draws a
random operational node id no peer of the fabric holds; a caller's id
(`commissioner.Options.NodeID`) is taken as given and refused when in
use. ClientNodeTest's four allocator cases ("assigns an unused node ID
when commissioning after a restart with existing peers", "refuses to
allocate a peer address whose NodeId is already in use", "skips the
controller's own node ID", "skips a previously allocated node ID",
`packages/node/test/node/ClientNodeTest.ts:537-567`, `:3024-3033`,
`:4147-4192`) are `left` under this entry. Owner decision 2026-11-03
(phase 32).

By design: several administrators on one fabric collide when each counts
from 1, while a random 64-bit draw does not, and a host's records keyed by
node id stay stable across a controller that loses its counter.

### BD-Matter-ClientNode-EndpointInstalledOnce — an installed endpoint's clusters are not emitted again

matter.js emits an installed endpoint through `emitEndpoint`, which emits
each of its clusters and recurses into its parts
(`ClientStructureEvents.ts:101-120` at `862ad75f`), and then emits every
cluster of the endpoint once more (`ClientStructure.ts:1696-1703`, "a
minor optimization" for cluster-level listeners). `Hooks.EndpointInstalled`
is called once per installed endpoint; its clusters come with it and no
`ClusterInstalled` follows for them. Report AK.

By design. One typed hook per fact; a host that wants the clusters reads
`Endpoint.Clusters()` in the hook.

### BD-Matter-ClientNode-SettingsInStore — the node's settings are stored beside its image

matter.js persists a client node's settings (`autoSubscribe`,
`defaultSubscription`, `isDisabled`, the event cursor) as the state of its
`NetworkClient` behaviour through the node's own storage: the state
fields of quality "N", the event cursor `maxEventNumber` among them
(`NetworkClient.ts:501-529` at `b25ed960`; at `0ceb202d` the cursor was
`ClientEventEmitter`'s). `controller/client` keeps them in the same `Store` as the
image, as endpoint 0's cluster `0xFFFF_FFFF`, an id no Matter cluster can
take. One store interface, one erase. Report AK.

By design. A second store seam for a few settings would be a second thing
to implement for every backend.

---

### BD-Matter-ClientRegistry-RestoreSkipsFailedNode — a node that fails to restore is skipped, not kept unavailable

matter.js's `Peers.initialize` creates every stored node and adds it;
one whose construction fails stays in the container as unavailable, its
error logged (`Peers.ts:133-160` at `db021da0`). `client.NewRegistry`
logs the failure with the node's id and does not add the node; its
stored data stays for the next start. Report AL.

By design. A Go node has no "crashed" lifecycle state to hold; a host
sees the id in the log and the data in the store.

### BD-Matter-ClientRegistry-ReactionsInBackground — the BasicInformation reactions and the label reconciliation run as registry work

matter.js runs `#onLeave` as a mutex task and `#onShutdown`/`#onStartUp`
as async event handlers (`Peers.ts:824`, `:876`, registered `:754-756`
at `862ad75f`), and `#reconcileFabricLabel` from the `subscriptionAlive`
reactor (`NetworkClient.ts:60`). The Go registry runs each as background work
it starts from the node's `Event`/`SubscriptionAlive` hook and that
`Close` cancels and waits for: a leave that deletes the node must not
run on the goroutine of the subscription that delivered it. Report AL.

By design. The same order of effects; the hook returns at once.

### BD-Matter-ClientRegistry-CommissionAddressesOverride — the commissioner's address option overrides the record's addresses

matter.js's `commission` takes the addresses from the node's record only
(`CommissioningClient.ts:254-257` at `862ad75f`). `Registry.Commission`
uses `CommissionOptions.Addresses` when given and the record's otherwise,
so a host that knows the address can commission without a prior
`ForDevice`. Report AL.

By design. An extension of the surface; the record's path is matter.js's.

---

### BD-Matter-WiFiHost-NetworkCommissioningEthernet — a Wi-Fi host advertises NetworkCommissioning as Ethernet and states the WiFi condition

matter.js's `NetworkCommissioningServer` is the empty generated class
(`packages/node/src/behaviors/network-commissioning/NetworkCommissioningServer.ts:18`
at `0ceb202d`); a Wi-Fi node there specialises it with the WI feature and
supplies the scan/connect commands itself. `node/` keeps
`NetworkCommissioning` Ethernet-only (concept v2 0.4, §B.4): a host with a
`Network.WiFi` reporter gets `WiFiNetworkDiagnostics` on its root and the
root states the Base conditions `Ethernet` and `WiFi`
(`RootDeviceConditions`), which is what the RootNode requirements'
`[WiFi]` and `[Ethernet]` conformance evaluates; the FeatureMap of
NetworkCommissioning stays `ET`. Report AM.

By design. A bridge host does not scan or join networks through Matter;
the diagnostics tell the truth about the link, the commissioning cluster
says what the host can do. Since wave 28b (2026-11-11) the entry holds for
a host without a Wi-Fi driver only: `Network.WiFi.Driver` is the host's
Wi-Fi commissioning port, and a node that sets it serves
NetworkCommissioning with the `WI` feature in place of `ET`
(BD-chip-WiFiNetworkCommissioningServer, BD-chip-WpaSupplicantDriver); the
test seam of review 2026-11 W5-api-11 (`internal/nodeseam.UseWiFiCommissioning`)
is gone. A reporter alone leaves the cluster on Ethernet, as before.

On Ethernet the one network's Connected is InterfaceEnabled
(`cluster/core/network_commissioning.go:214`): a write that changes
InterfaceEnabled changes Networks with it, advances the DataVersion once and
reports both (`:147`, `:165-166`). matter.js's `NetworkCommissioningServer`
is the empty subclass
(`packages/node/src/behaviors/network-commissioning/NetworkCommissioningServer.ts:18`
at `b25ed960`), so Networks is state of its own there that an
InterfaceEnabled write does not touch — inferred from the empty class, not
run. This module's rule (review II, R2-P4-cert-03): an interface the
controller disabled is no connected network.

---

## Removed (built, tested, never wired)

`cluster/doc.go` cites this table. It records code that existed and was
deleted, so a later reader does not re-add it thinking it was an oversight.
The code itself is in Git history.

### BD-Matter-LevelControl-LenientDecoders — LevelControl's omitted request fields take a fallback

The bridge decodes every LevelControl request through the generated
definition (`cluster/spec/levelcontrol`, ADR 0013; since brief BX1 the
definition decodes first, gate 1 G1-2), but a mandatory field that is
absent from the payload decodes as its fallback instead of failing:
TransitionTime (MoveToLevel, Step and their WithOnOff forms) and Rate
(Move, MoveWithOnOff) as null, OptionsMask and OptionsOverride (all eight)
as 0 (`bridge/fields_definition.go` `requestFallbacks`). The raw decoders
`cluster/wire` `DecodeMoveToLevel` / `DecodeStep` read an absent
TransitionTime as null the same (owner decision 168). matter.js refuses the
shape: decode leaves the member unset (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvObject.ts:205-251`
at `db021da0`), then `requestTlv.validate`
(`packages/protocol/src/action/server/CommandInvokeResponse.ts:486`) throws
`ValidationMandatoryFieldMissingError` (`TlvObject.ts:257-261`), answered
INVALID_COMMAND (`CommandInvokeResponse.ts:529-535`); matter.js has the mechanism — after decoding, a mandatory field that is
missing takes its field's fallback when one is declared
(`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvObject.ts:236-249` at `db021da0`), and
`TlvField` takes one 'to initialize the field value when devices omit
providing a value' (`:398-404`) — but the schema built from the model
declares none for any field: `TlvField(id, schema)`
(`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvOfModel.ts:267`). connectedhomeip accepts it: its generated
decoder has no presence check
(`zzz_generated/app-common/clusters/LevelControl/Commands.ipp:44-73` at
`6170af84`) and the cluster reads the field with a fallback
(`src/app/clusters/level-control/LevelControlCluster.cpp:371`, Step `:517`);
that the absent field is null is inferred. This module follows chip here. No
capture of a controller that omits the field is on record (the Google Home
claim came with the extraction commit `f2f65e6a`). `levelcontrol.Server`
reads the fallbacks as a null TransitionTime and zero options. A missing
Level, MoveMode, StepMode or StepSize still answers INVALID_COMMAND. Pinned
by `TestDecodeMoveToLevelOmitsTransitionTime`,
`TestDecodeStepOmitsTransitionTime` and the lenient column of
`TestRawDecodersRefuseWhatTheGeneratedOnesRefuse` (cluster/wire),
`TestDecodeMoveToLevelRequest_AbsentTransitionTime`,
`TestCommandFieldsReader_MoveToLevelVariants_AbsentTransitionTime` and
`TestCommandFieldsReader_LevelControlStepAbsentTransitionTime` (bridge).
Retire when a decision to follow matter.js's refusal is taken. Review II,
R2-P6-wire-1209, owner decision 168.
### BD-Matter-AdminCommissioning-OpenWindowParams — OpenCommissioningWindow keeps its hand-written decoder

`cluster/wire.AdministratorCommissioning` is built on its generated
definition (`cluster/spec/administratorcommissioning`, ADR 0013), but the
bridge decodes OpenCommissioningWindow with its own
`decodeOpenCommissioningWindowRequest` (`bridge/fields_reader_admincomm.go`)
into `cluster/wire.OpenWindowParams`, ahead of the definition. Two reasons:
the `WindowController` port a host implements takes `OpenWindowParams`, and
matter.js extends the request schema before it validates — its
`AdministratorCommissioningServer.ts:38-43` (at db021da0) relaxes the
PakePasscodeVerifier, Iterations, Salt and Discriminator constraints to
"none" so the behavior answers PakeParameterError (cluster status 0x03) for
the PAKE parameters and INVALID_COMMAND for a discriminator above 0xFFF
(`:92-97`) rather than the interaction layer answering CONSTRAINT_ERROR. Since
2026-11-14 (review II, owner decision 64) the generated definition carries
that extension: the four fields are entries of the relaxation table
(`script/clustergen/relaxed.go:71-79`), written into the definition as
`spec.Field.Relaxed`, and the request is held to the definition's request
check before the hand-written decoder reads it (`heldByDefinition`,
`bridge/fields_reader.go:88-101`) — a missing mandatory field is
INVALID_COMMAND — and the PAKE and discriminator checks stay with the
server. The server also
accepts the generated `OpenCommissioningWindowRequest` in process. What is
left of this entry is the first reason, the port's `OpenWindowParams`. Retire
when the `WindowController` port takes the generated request.

### BD-Matter-Commissioning-HandDecoders — the commissioning and group requests keep their hand-written decoders

GeneralCommissioning, the core Groups and ScenesManagement servers are
built on their generated definitions (ids, revisions, FeatureMap, lists,
privileges, write statuses — ADR 0013), but their requests still decode
through the bridge's hand-written readers into the `cluster/core` request
structs (`ArmFailSafeRequest`, `SetRegulatoryConfigRequest`,
`AddGroupRequest` …, `AddSceneRequest` with its `SceneRef` and extension
field sets), which run ahead of the generated decoders in
`bridge/fields_reader.go`. Those structs are what the fail-safe, the group
table and the scene table are written against; re-pointing the servers at
the generated structs is a rewrite of the commissioning and scene logic,
not a codec swap, and the CGEN, G and S families hold the readers' statuses
as they are. Every request they define is still decoded by a hand-written
reader, but since 2026-11-14 (review II, owner decision 64, R2-P4-coresec-04,
-07) each is first held to its definition's request check (`heldByDefinition`,
`bridge/fields_reader.go:103-155` at `1a0d8ba9`), so the statuses are those of matter.js's
request schema — a field outside its constraint is CONSTRAINT_ERROR, a missing
mandatory field INVALID_COMMAND, before the server runs
(`packages/protocol/src/action/server/CommandInvokeResponse.ts:484-487` at
`db021da0`) — with the servers' relaxations of `script/clustergen/relaxed.go`
(OperationalCredentials' nonces, OpenCommissioningWindow's PAKE fields and
Discriminator, Groups' AddGroup fields, ScenesManagement's SceneId,
TransitionTime and SceneName; `:65-98`). One hand reader departs:
SetRegulatoryConfig's hands the server an empty CountryCode whatever was
sent, kept after an Apple Home pairing regression
(`decodeSetRegulatoryConfigRequest`, `bridge/fields_reader.go:357-391` at `1a0d8ba9`), so the server sees none although the
definition has checked the one on the wire. Pinned by
`bridge:TestHandDecodedRequestsAreHeldByTheirDefinition`. Retire per server
when its logic is moved onto the generated request structs.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-wire-0440, R2-P6-test-0811): each hand-read request is held to its definition's request check (`cmd.DecodeRequest`) and the hand reader then reads that checked tree, restricted to the command's defined top-level fields (`bridge/fields_reader.go` `heldByDefinition`, `definedFields`) — a member the definition does not know is skipped whole, as matter.js skips an unknown field (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvObject.ts:215-217` at `b25ed960`), so the request checked is the request executed. A known command without a decoder is INVALID_COMMAND, and a command the definition does not know never reaches a hand reader. KeySetWrite no longer has a hand reader (it decodes into the generated request). The readers' own type, width, length and mandatory checks were unreachable behind the check and are deleted; a TLV list where the definition expects an array is now INVALID_COMMAND for every request decoded through a definition, as matter.js refuses any type but Array (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvArray.ts:73-74`).

### BD-Matter-FixedWidthStructs — DeviceTypeList and BasicCommissioningInfo keep their fixed-width encoders

The generated codecs encode every integer at its smallest TLV width, as
matter.js's `TlvNumber` does, and the measurement, BasicInformation,
GeneralDiagnostics and DiagnosticLogs values now encode through them. Two
hand-written encoders in `bridge/reply.go` stay: Descriptor's
`DeviceTypeList` (`[]core.DeviceTypeStruct`, now an alias of the generated
struct) writes DeviceType as a 4-byte and Revision as a 2-byte integer, and
GeneralCommissioning's `BasicCommissioningInfoStruct` writes both fields as
2-byte integers. Both record controller-side findings — Apple Home's
topology decoding and a typed decoder rejecting a narrowed width — that no
run of this round re-verified, and both are read by every controller during
commissioning. The wire values are the same; only the widths differ from
matter.js's. Retire after a commissioning run against Apple Home with the
generated encoders.

### BD-Matter-Media-HostPorts — the fourteen media servers are the generated definitions plus typed host ports and a state transaction

matter.js's media behaviours at `0ceb202d` are the generated
`extends XBehavior {}` stubs (fourteen; `low-power/LowPowerServer.ts:13-25`
is the one with logic, `sleep()` emitting `enterLowPowerMode`): the
application's subclass implements each command against `this.state`,
and a command throwing rolls its transaction back. `cluster/media` wraps
each definition in `spec.NewServer` behind one host port per cluster:
a port command receives the attribute state as a pointer, the server
commits the copy on success and drops it on failure; optional commands
are optional Go interfaces (accepted only when implemented,
`ProtocolService.ts:548-552` at `862ad75f`), a mandatory one the port lacks is
`ErrNotImplemented` (`ValidatedElements.ts:357-371`); the two list
defaults the model does carry (`channel.element.ts:31`,
`content-launcher.element.ts:34`, both `[]`) are applied by the servers
because `defaultValue` renders no list defaults. LowPower's `Sleep`
calls the port where matter.js emits its event. Report AR.

By design (ADR 0022). A host owns what plays; the server owns the wire
shape and the transaction.

### BD-chip-Messages-CoreHeld — Messages answers a ninth message with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, cancels per fabric and lets the host report presentation

matter.js has no Messages logic (`MessagesServer.ts`, an empty class at
`0ceb202d`); chip's `messages-server.cpp` at the harness pin checks the
request (Responses without RESP → INVALID_COMMAND, `:359-363`) and the
tv-app's `MessagesManager.cpp` replaces an existing id, completes a
presented message on cancel and drops a queued one. `core.Messages`
mirrors both and adds what neither says: a ninth message is
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (the list's `max 8`, `messages.element.ts:32`), a
cancel touches only the accessing fabric's messages (the list is `R F V`),
the presentation lifecycle is the host's (`Presented`, `Complete` with
a `MessageOutcome`), and MessageComplete's ResponseId/Reply are null
with RESP/RPLY and absent without. chip's per-option rules — at most 4
options, a MessageResponseID from 1, a label of at most 32 — are held by
the generated request decoder (`cluster/spec/messages/definition_gen.go:150-151`,
`:250`; chip `messages-server.cpp:365-367`, `:379-385`,
`messages-delegate.h:33-35` at `6170af84`), an option without id or label
is INVALID_COMMAND as there (`:375-377`), and chip's SpokenMessage and
AudioMessage checks (from `:293`) have no counterpart: the snapshot's
MessageControlBitmap has neither bit (`definition_gen.go:92-96`). Pinned by
`cluster/core:TestMessagesResponseOptionRules` (review II, W3-clucore-09).
Report AR.

By design (ADR 0022). The list bound and the fabric scope come from the
model; the lifecycle has no reference and is the host's.

The fields' fabric sensitivity is matter.js's and is applied on every read:
each field of MessageStruct but FabricIndex is access "S"
(`packages/model/src/standard/elements/messages.element.ts:121-133` at
`b25ed960`), and matter.js withholds such a field from a session of another
fabric and from one without a fabric (`mayRead`,
`packages/protocol/src/action/server/AccessControl.ts:342-356`). A read
without a fabric filter therefore serves another fabric's message as its
FabricIndex alone (`cluster/core/messages.go:176-196`; review II, phase 4).
Pinned by `cluster/core:TestParityMatterJS_MessagesEntryOfAnotherFabricWithoutSensitiveFields`
and, for every fabric-scoped list a node serves, by
`node:TestFabricSensitiveFieldsWithheldFromOtherFabrics`.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): the tv-app's `MessagesManager.cpp` of
connectedhomeip is outside the exports the review read and was not re-read;
what this entry says of it is unverified.

### BD-Matter-DCL-OptIn — the DCL is reached only through a host-built client; development certificates from GitHub stay off; one trust-store blob; the CRL cache expires on use

matter.js's `DclCertificateService` (`packages/protocol/src/dcl/DclCertificateService.ts`
at `0ceb202d`) is constructed by the controller with the production
ledger, fetches GitHub's development certificates whenever test
certificates are enabled unless explicitly disabled (`:1103-1119` at
`db021da0`),
stores PAAs and CD signers as per-certificate entries, and sweeps its
CRL cache with an hourly timer after an hour of disuse (the cache at
`:362-367`, its timer and sweep at `packages/general/src/util/Cache.ts:36-40`
and `:153-156`, all at `b25ed960`). `controller/dcl` (the ledger client in `dcl` since review II, decision 553) mirrors the GETs, the 5 s timeout
(`DclClient.ts:39`), the daily refresh and the §6.2.6.1 checks, with four
surface differences: a `CertificateStore` without a `Client` is offline
and fetches nothing; the GitHub fallback is an option that defaults to
off; the trust store persists as one JSON value under the host's
`Store`; a CRL entry's hour is checked when it is used, with no timer.
The reference daemon's `--dcl` defaults to `off`, as
`eligibility/vendor_name.go:5-25` keeps vendor names embedded. Report AS.

By design (ADR 0020 stage 6a). No request leaves a host that did not
construct a client; the stored shape and the sweep are private to the
store and change no answer.

### BD-chip-CommissionerControl-RandomWindow — the reverse commissioning window is minted at random; the client check includes the fabric; approval may time out

chip's CommissionerControl server (`src/app/clusters/commissioner-control-server/CommissionerControlCluster.cpp`
at the harness pin) delegates the window's parameters, and the only
delegate — `examples/fabric-sync/bridge/CommissionerControlDelegate.cpp:33-36`
— uses the fixed passcode 20202021 and discriminator 3840 with 1000
iterations; `CommissionNode` hands the client's node id and the request id
to the delegate to compare (`CommissionerControlCluster.cpp:207`,
`Delegate.h:67-78` at `6170af84`), and a TODO to include the fabric stands at
no line of the cluster's directory — the delegate under `examples/fabric-sync`
was not read (unverified); an approval has no timeout. `core.CommissionerControl`
mints passcode, discriminator and salt from `crypto/rand` per request,
compares node id *and* accessing fabric index, and takes
`ApprovalTimeout`/`ApprovalValidity` (0 = chip's wait-forever and
never-expire); the TIMEOUT and FAILURE result codes for a timed-out or
denied approval are this module's choice. The vid/pid of the request is
not checked by the server, as chip checks it at discovery
(`src/controller/SetUpCodePairer.cpp:690-707`): the port exposes
`CommissioningApprovalRequest.Matches` for the host's commissioner.
Report AS.

By design (ADR 0020 stage 6b). A fixed passcode on a reverse window is
an example's convenience, not a protocol rule; the fabric comparison is
what chip's TODO asks for.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): connectedhomeip's
`examples/fabric-sync/bridge/CommissionerControlDelegate.cpp` is outside the
exports the review read and was not re-read; what this entry says of it is
unverified.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-sup-1009, owner decision 150): the node holds one request slot, freed only by the approving client's CommissionNode — used, or past `ApprovalValidity` — or by a restart; neither the clock nor a fabric's removal frees it, as chip's example delegate: the idle check (`examples/fabric-sync/bridge/CommissionerControlDelegate.cpp:77` at `6170af84`), the validation of a CommissionNode (`:139-147`), the slot freed at the end of `HandleCommissionNode` (`:201`, `ResetDelegateState`) and when the event cannot be generated (`:126`); the file has no clock and no fabric-removal path (read `:45-203`). Mirrored though a request nobody approves keeps the slot until a restart.

### BD-Matter-ControllerFabric-OneRecord — the controller keeps one fabric per database, with its key and NOC, and resumes sessions from memory only

matter.js's `FabricManager.ts:187-200` at `db021da0` persists a list of
`Fabric.Config` records under `"fabrics"` with a `nextFabricIndex`
counter (read back at `:68-73`); each record carries the fabric id, root node id, IPK, operational
certificate and key pair (`Fabric.ts:714-733`), and `FabricAuthority.ts:136-141`
mints a random root node id, a random IPK and vendor 0xFFF1 (`:47`) on first use.
`controller/ca`'s `SettingStore` and `commissioner.FabricConfig.Store`
keep one record of the same fields in the host's settings table — no list,
no counter — so a second run of the reference controller is the same
identity every paired node trusts; session resumption stays in
`peer.MemoryResumptionStore` (a restart re-runs Sigma1–3). Report AT.

By design (ADR 0020). A controller daemon has one fabric; the list form
returns when a second is wanted.

### BD-chip-ControllerCLI-JSON — the JSON value codec extends chip-tool's conventions by names, and leaves a struct's FabricIndex to the server

chip-tool's argument parser at the harness pin
(`examples/chip-tool/commands/clusters/JsonParser.h`, `CustomArgument.h`,
`examples/chip-tool/commands/common/CustomStringPrefix.h`) takes numbers, `hex:`/`base64:`/`str:` strings,
`null`, nested objects by field name and arrays. `spec.EncodeJSON`/`DecodeJSON`
(`cluster/spec/json.go`) take the same and also an enum by its value name,
a bitmap as an object of member names, struct keys without regard to
case or by field id, and let a fabric-scoped struct omit `FabricIndex`
(the server stamps the accessing fabric, `AttributeWriteResponse.ts:466-471` at `862ad75f`).
Signed integers are JSON numbers only, as in chip-tool. Report AT.

By design (ADR 0020). chip is the authority for tool input; the names
are a convenience the definitions make exact.

### BD-chip-ControllerCLI-GroupsAndOTA — the reference controller sends to groups and serves OTA images from the controller's own identity, asks OTA consent at offer time, and sets a group up the pre-1.5 way where Groupcast is absent

`group send` and `ota serve` run on the controller's own identity:
`Controller.Groups` sends with the key set `group create` keeps through
`Controller.SetGroupKey`, and `controller.Config.OTA` serves the provider
at the controller's provider endpoint (phase 37; until then the tool
commissioned a second `node.Node` of its own for both). OTA
consent is asked when an image is offered, not through the provider's
consent hook: with the hook, matter.js's requestor cancels the update at
apply time for a device that consents itself (`BD-Matter-OTAProvider-HostPorts`,
findings "OTA provider, mirrored"). `group create` reads the node's
ServerList and, without Groupcast (0x0065), follows chip's
`src/app/tests/suites/TestGroupMessaging.yaml` at the pin — KeySetWrite
TrustFirst (`:84-102`), a GroupKeyMap entry (`:122-132`), Groups AddGroup
per endpoint (`:134-168`), an ACL entry for the group subject (the bare
16-bit group id, which `cluster/core/access_control.go:1168-1170` accepts as
matter.js does; chip stores its 64-bit group node id in that form,
`src/app/server/AclStorage.cpp:162-171`) granting Operate on those
endpoints where the YAML's own entry (`:188-211`) grants any group Manage.
Report AT.

By design (ADR 0020). The controller sends through its own socket;
the narrower ACL is what the group needs; a device before Matter 1.5 has
no Groupcast.

### BD-Matter-LevelControl-NativeSource — the native-ramp source switches off when the level arrives and couples no colour temperature

matter.js's `LevelControlServer` runs the ramp itself and, for a
`*WithOnOff` command, moves OnOff on every step of its own transition
(`LevelControlServer.ts`, `transition`/`setLevel` as cited in
`cluster/levelcontrol/native.go`). `levelcontrol.NewNativeSource` hands
the ramp to the device (`NativeRamp.Ramp(level, duration, withOnOff)`):
it switches the light on before a ramp up from off in matter.js's order,
and switches off when the level reaches the minimum — at once for a
ramp without duration, on the device's change notification, and at the
latest when the ramp is due to end, reported or not (v0.5.2, v0.5.3,
#129, #131); a later command cancels the pending switch-off. It reports
RemainingTime 0 and couples no colour temperature (the engine's
`Transitions.ColorTemperature` has no hand-off counterpart). The plain
Stop is gated by ExecuteIfOff and StopWithOnOff is not
(`LevelControlServer.ts:481-500` at `b25ed960`). Report AV (#120).

By design. A device that ramps natively reports its level when it gets
there; the server cannot step what it does not drive.

### BD-Matter-SqliteStore-WrapOrder — after a wrap the store takes the lowest free number and starts at 2

matter.js `ServerEndpointStores.ts:170-183` at `0ceb202d` continues from
the number after the last assigned one after wrapping to 1, and skips
the preset numbers an application reserves. `endpoint/sqlitestore`
lifts its persisted counter past the highest stored number on every
allocation, so once 0xFFFE is in use it walks from the first bridged
number (2 — 1 is the Aggregator) and takes the lowest free one; there is
no preset-number set because the bridge reserves nothing beyond the
Aggregator. `ErrEndpointsExhausted` only after a full pass. Report AV
(#121).

By design. Matching matter.js's order after a wrap would need a second
persisted cursor for a case that needs 65 533 allocations to occur.

### BD-Matter-LevelControl-NativeSwitcher — a device that writes On/Off and level together takes "with On/Off" commands as one call

matter.js couples On/Off and the level transition in one transaction
against local state (`LevelControlServer.ts:529-550`, `couple` →
`#turnOnForLevel` → the transition; the switch-off on commit, `:624-633`
at `b25ed960`),
so a device sees one consistent change. A bridged device that takes
"start at level X" and "stop" as one write each would see two writes —
on at the old level, then the new level — and an audible or visible
moment in between. `levelcontrol.NativeSwitcher` (optional on a
`NativeRamp`) receives `SwitchOn(level, d)` when a "with On/Off" command
turns the device on and `SwitchOff(d)` when one ends at the minimum,
instead of the source's SetOnOff + Ramp sequence; the source then leaves
the OnOff attribute to the host's OnOff, which reflects the device. A
device without the interface keeps matter.js's order; `NativeMover`
still takes Move. Issue #131.

By design. No matter.js behaviour changes for a device that does not
opt in; the interface only lets a bridged device express the one
transaction matter.js runs locally.

### BD-Matter-CommissioningBlocked — a host can refuse every new commissioning while paired controllers keep working

matter.js opens a commissioning window whenever its rules allow one —
the node's own window while uncommissioned, AdministratorCommissioning
for an administrator (`AdministratorCommissioningServer.ts`: Busy only
for an armed fail-safe or a window already open, `:213-221` at
`db021da0`) — and has no policy refusal. A bridge
host that was configured with a vendor attestation chain it cannot load
must not let a new controller pair against the CSA test chain, yet must
keep serving the controllers already paired.
`bridge.CommissioningWindow.SetBlocked(ctx, err)` / `Node.SetCommissioningBlocked`
refuse both window open paths (`OpenOwnWindow`, `OpenWindow`) with an
error wrapping `bridge.ErrCommissioningBlocked` and the host's cause,
revoke a window that is open (withdrawing the CM record), and lift with
nil — the facade then reopens an uncommissioned node's own window. An
AdministratorCommissioning command refused this way answers FAILURE
(general status): none of the cluster's statuses means "refused by
policy". Issue #133.

By design. A host extension with no matter.js behaviour to mirror; it
only removes ways to commission, never adds one.

### BD-Matter-AttestationPolicy-ZeroProceeds — the zero attestation policy lets commissioning proceed with a warning

matter.js's `ControllerCommissioningFlow.#resolveAttestationFindings`
(`ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:1359-1386` at `db021da0`) logs each
attestation finding as a warning and proceeds when the controller set no
policy; only `false` or a deciding function rejects. `attestation.Policy`'s
zero value is that undefined policy (`controller/attestation/policy.go:14-17`,
`:42-61`), so a host that drives `controller/commissioner` itself and sets
nothing commissions a device whose chain does not verify
(`controller/commissioner/commissioner.go:168-175`). The facade does not
pass the zero value on: `controller.Pair` turns a zero
`OnAttestationFailure` into `attestation.Reject()`
(`controller/controller.go:904-906`, `:1086-1088`;
`BD-Matter-Controller-PairRejectsFailedAttestation`). Hosts on the
commissioner set `attestation.Reject()` for production; the security
page and the controller guide say so. Raised in brief AW's report.

By design. The zero value mirrors matter.js; a Go-only stricter default
would change what a matter.js-shaped host expects, and the reference
controller asks on a terminal and rejects otherwise.

### BD-Matter-LastFabricReopenWithoutErase — after the last fabric goes the node reopens its window when idle, without a factory reset

matter.js `CommissioningServer #resetWhenIdle` (`CommissioningServer.ts:179-202`
at `b25ed960`) waits until no fail-safe is armed and no session remains,
cancels if a fabric exists by then, and erases the node
(`ServerNode.erase()`), which restarts it commissionable. The facade waits
the same way (`Node.reopenWhenIdle`) and then reopens its own window, but
erases nothing: a bridge host's endpoint numbers, labels and settings are
the host's model of its devices, and the fabric-scoped state (ACL, group
keys, bindings, scenes of the fabric) already left with the fabric.
Findings wave 2026-10-17.

By design. A reset of the host's device model is the host's decision, not
a side effect of a controller removing itself.

Review II, run 4 (R4-par-4051): AccessControl reports a fabric drop's shrink of Acl and Extension also when the removed fabric was the last one; matter.js skips the strip then (`packages/node/src/node/server/ServerEnvironment.ts:189-192` at `b25ed960`: `if (fabricIndices.length > 0)` `:190` before `limitNodeDataToAllowedFabrics` `:191`). The module keeps the node at its last fabric's removal (above), so the list does shrink and is reported: one version step that no fabric is left to read. GroupKeyManagement's drop report (decision 614) has the same shape; that it fires at the last fabric too was not measured (unverified). Pinned by `cluster/core:TestAccessControlFabricDropReportsWhatShrank`.

### BD-Matter-FactoryResetEndsTheNode — a factory reset stops the node; the host builds the one that comes back

matter.js `ServerNode.erase` (`packages/node/src/node/ServerNode.ts:159-200`
at `862ad75f`) takes the node offline, resets its in-memory state, erases its
storage (`resetStorage`, `:242-256`) and brings the same object back online
when it was; a controller's erase also drops its peers and CA material
(`ServerEnvironment.eraseCredentials`, `server/ServerEnvironment.ts:72-89`)
and the same instance commissions again (ServerNodeTest.ts:1488-1498). A Go
node and controller are single-use — `Node.Stop` and `Controller.Close` end
them (`node.ErrStopped`) — so `Node.FactoryReset` removes the fabrics
through the RemoveFabric fan-out, stops the node and erases its credential
store (`store.Eraser`) and endpoint records, and `Controller.Erase` closes
the controller and erases its database; the host builds the node or
controller that comes back on the same store (fabrictest's
`Device.FactoryReset` restarts a device that ran). One consequence: the
endpoint allocation counter of `endpoint.Store` is not rewound (the
interface has no reset; a freed number is reissued only after the wrap).
The erased store gets a fresh random UniqueID pin, as matter.js draws one
(phase 32). Phase 31.

By design. Rebuilding is how every in-memory state a reset erases — the
root servers' values, Wi-Fi networks, scenes, the validator — goes for
certain, without a reset path in each server.

The order of the reset follows connectedhomeip (review II, R2-P4-cert-06):
the fabrics leave while the node is still online — each through the
RemoveFabric fan-out, which sends what the fabric's subscriptions owe, the
Leave event included, and tells the fabric's sessions with a CloseSession
(`node/factory_reset.go:61-75`; `bridge/bridge.go:1679-1722`) — and the node
stops after, as connectedhomeip deletes all fabrics, "and emit[s] Leave
event", before the server shuts down (`src/app/server/Server.cpp:893-902` at
`6170af84`). matter.js goes offline first ("Go offline before performing
reset", `packages/node/src/node/ServerNode.ts:165-173` at `b25ed960`) and
clears the sessions and fabrics then (`resetStorage`, `:243-257`). Who sees
it: a controller subscribed at a factory reset gets the Leave event and a
CloseSession here before the node goes; what reaches it from matter.js on
that path was not traced (unverified). By design: a controller that is told
its fabric left does not have to find the node gone by its timeouts.

### BD-Matter-EndpointNumberAfterWrap — after the wrap the store takes the lowest free number on every allocation

matter.js `ServerEndpointStores.assignNumber` keeps its counter after the
number it assigned last and walks on from there after a wrap
(`packages/node/src/storage/server/ServerEndpointStores.ts:169-183` at
`862ad75f`; ServerNodeTest.ts:1153-1176 expects the endpoint after the
wrapped one to take the next number, not the one a deleted endpoint freed).
`endpoint/sqlitestore` lifts its counter past the highest number a row holds
on every allocation (`allocate`), so once a row holds 0xFFFE every
allocation wraps and takes the lowest free number, a just-freed one
included. `endpoint:TestEndpointNumberWrapParityMatterJS` pins it. Phase 31.

By design. The lift is what keeps a number a row placed above the counter
from being reissued (BD-Matter-EndpointNumber-Monotonic); the reuse begins
only after 65 533 allocations.

### BD-Matter-OTA-MirroredQuirks — consent reset, userConsentNeeded and TC-SU-2.7 follow matter.js

Mirrored as matter.js has them at `db021da0`: the provider's
`directConsentObtained` defaults to false on every state change
(`OtaSoftwareUpdateProviderServer.ts:596-603`, `:627`); `userConsentNeeded`
is set from `consentRequired` also after the provider obtained consent
(`:399`); the requestor treats a failed provider connection as "no update"
with reason Success (`OtaSoftwareUpdateRequestorServer.ts:630-641`) and a
BDX failure's DownloadError carries no byte count (`:924-930`, `:993-1002`),
where chip's TC_SU_2_7.py expects otherwise (manual at the pin). Report AX §8.

By design. Each is a matter.js behaviour with an upstream question; the
module changes when matter.js does.

### BD-Matter-DCL-MirroredScope — an expired CRL still revokes; the unported DCL parts; context-less seams

`DclCertificateService.ts:1964-1989` (at `b25ed960`) parses a CRL's `nextUpdate` and never
reads it, so an expired CRL still revokes — mirrored, pinned by a test.
Of the parts this entry listed as not ported, these are ported now:
out-of-band revocation sets (`CertificateStore.InstallRevocations`,
`controller/dcl/revocation.go:770-777`), seed data (`controller/dcl/snapshot`;
the vendor seed, `dcl/vendorinfo.go:60-67`), the on-demand
certificate fetch by subject key id (`GetOrFetchCertificate`,
`controller/dcl/certstore.go:396-401`), the compliance endpoint
(`Client.ComplianceInfo`, `dcl/client.go:466-472`) and OTA image
storage (`controller/softwareupdate/images.go:26-30`). Not ported: ML-DSA
PAAs in the ledger stores (the attestation validator admits them
behind PQC Phase 1, wave 27-A). `attestation.PAAStore` and
`Revocations` take no context (a change would break the API before the
freeze); on-demand CRL fetches are bounded by the client timeout. Reports
AS, AX §10.

By design until a host needs one of them.

### BD-Matter-GroupKeyEpochStartTimeUnits — the group sender compares the key's epoch start as matter.js does

`KeySets.ts:83`, `:126-133` read `epochStartTime` (Matter epoch, µs since
2000) through `Timestamp.fromMicroseconds` and compare it with Unix ms; a key
whose start is in the past in either reading counts as started.
`groups/sender.go:132-173` mirrors it. Report AX §6.

By design. Controllers write current values, which read as started either
way; a fix belongs upstream.

### BD-chip-EVSE-TargetsServerHeld — an eleventh ChargingTarget in a day is the EnergyEvse server's RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, not the decoder's CONSTRAINT_ERROR

matter.js validates a SetTargets request against the model before the
invoker runs (`CommandInvokeResponse.ts:484-487`) and refuses an eleventh
ChargingTarget of a day at `ChargingTargets`' `max 10`
(`energy-evse-cluster.element.ts:254`, `TlvArray.ts:111-113`) with
CONSTRAINT_ERROR; its `EnergyEvseServer.ts:14` has no logic. chip's
generated decoder does not enforce the list bound and its handler counts
the targets: `EnergyEvseCluster.cpp:564-565` answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
which TC-EEVSE-2.3 step 19 expects (`TC_EEVSE_2_3.py:411-439`). The
generated `ChargingTargetScheduleStruct` decoder drops the bound
(the relaxation table of `script/clustergen/relaxed.go`, section
`cluster/energy EvseServer`, `:116-123`, written into the definition as
`spec.Field.Relaxed`; the definition keeps `max 10` verbatim), so `cluster/energy/evse.go`'s
`evseMaxTargetsPerDay` check answers on the wire; pinned by
`bridge/fields_evse_targets_test.go`.

By design (owner decision 2026-11-03): the CSA case expects chip's status
and matter.js serves no EnergyEvse logic of its own to mirror.

### BD-chip-Harness-ModelOverCase — CountdownTime and two chipdm (ii) entries follow the model, not chip's case or XML

CountdownTime is reported as matter.js reports it (QuietEvent), not by the
specification's list, which matter.js does not implement either.
TC-EEVSE-2.3 left this entry for `BD-chip-EVSE-TargetsServerHeld`
(owner decision 2026-11-03). GroupKeyMulticastPolicy stays as the snapshot gates it.
ColorControl's XY → HS conversion departs from matter.js, which hands x and y
to `hsvToXy` (`ColorControlServer.ts:1493` at `b25ed960`); the module converts
with `xyToHsv` (`BD-Matter-ColorControl-XYToHS`). The FanMode a speed maps to
is left to the device (`BD-Matter-FanControlCouplingInServer`): neither chip's
33/66 split (`FanControlCluster.cpp:84-166`) nor a matter.js mapping, of which
there is none — matter.js's `FanControlServer` only defaults FanMode to Off
(`FanControlServer.ts:13-19`). Corrected 2026-11-14 (review II,
R2-P4-applight-09): the entry called both mirrored from matter.js.
Report AY §2, §5, §9, §12.

By design. matter.js is the gold standard where a case and the model
disagree; the harness classifies the cases accordingly.

### BD-chip-RvcRunMode-InvalidInMode — RvcRunMode without DIRECTMODECH refuses a change between two running modes

matter.js's RvcRunModeServer accepts any supported mode. chip's RVC example
and TC_RVCRUNM_2_2 step 6b (`src/python_testing/TC_RVCRUNM_2_2.py:228-232`
at `6170af84`) expect InvalidInMode for a change between two
non-Idle modes when DIRECTMODECH is not set; the server answers it itself.
RvcCleanMode's companion rule needs RvcRunMode's state and stays with the
host. Report AY §4.

By design. A rule matter.js leaves to the application, taken from chip where
the server can see everything it needs.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): connectedhomeip's RVC example
(`examples/rvc-app`) is outside the exports the review read and was not
re-read; what this entry says of it is unverified.

### BD-Controller-KeysBehindSigner — the controller's CA and operational keys may live behind `crypto.Signer`

matter.js keeps the fabric's operational key pair in the fabric itself
(`Fabric.ts:50-76` at `0ceb202d`, `#keyPair: Key`) and the CA's root key in
`CertificateAuthority`'s state; there is no seam for a key the process
cannot read. This module adds one: `ca.Config.RootSigner` / `ICACSigner`,
`commissioner.FabricConfig.OperationalSigner`, `sigma.Identity.Signer`
(a P-256 `crypto.Signer`); with a signer the stored record keeps the
certificates, the public key and a `KeyRef`, no private scalar. Without
one the record and its JSON are what they were. The wire shape is
unchanged: ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256, `r ‖ s` in Sigma2 / Sigma3
(`signTranscript` parses the signer's ASN.1 and range-checks the
components). Concept v3 §A.3, report AZ §2 (phase 11, 2026-10-17).

By design. Go's standard key seam, needed by an operator with an HSM, a
TPM or a KMS; the device side (the node's NOC key) is a later item.

### BD-Controller-DclSnapshotLayered — the embedded DCL snapshot is a trust layer, and the CD signers are named

matter.js feeds an offline seed into its `DclCertificateService`
(`DclCertificateService.ts:344-349`, `#consumeCertSeed` :1466-1537 at
`b25ed960`) and has no query for the ledger's CD-signer set. This module
keeps the snapshot (`controller/dcl/snapshot`: 74 production PAAs and 5 CD
signers from `on.dcl.csa-iot.org`, `SOURCE` manifest, refreshed only by
`make update-dcl-snapshot` as a review step) a separate `attestation.PAAStore`
beneath the online `dcl.CertificateStore` (`attestation.Trust`, `Layered`;
`TrustMode` Development / Production / None), because consuming it into
`controller/dcl` would import `attestation` from both sides. The CD-signer
set is named by key id after chip's
`src/credentials/attestation_verifier/DefaultDeviceAttestationVerifier.cpp:146-256`
(harness pin `6170af84`; the five ids equal the ledger's child listing of
the CSA root, checked 2026-10-17). Revocation is never answered from the
snapshot (`TestSnapshotIsNoRevocationSource`; Matter PKI CP §1.4.5,
§4.9.6). Concept v3 §A.2, report AZ §3,
`notes/reference/dcl-data-terms-2026-10-17.md`.

A CD signer the snapshot does not name is fetched from the ledger by
subject key id and trusted only when the CSA CD root issued it for that
key identifier (`attestation.VerifyCDSignerCertificate`), as matter.js
b25ed960 trusts CD signers like chip (`CdSigners.ts:90-136`,
`dcl/DclCertificateService.ts:901-970` at `b25ed960`): the five CSA keys
are built in (`attestation.KnownCDSigner`), the snapshot's and the store's
certificates count only if they verify, and a CD whose signer is none of
these is `CdSignerUnknown` (`BD-Matter-Attestation-CDSignerTrust`). This
replaces the earlier trust-as-fetched parity (owner decision 2026-11-02,
review W4-ctlint-09), which matter.js left at #4871 (pin lift wave P2,
#431).

By design. Same trust decision as matter.js's seed, a different place in
the graph; the named signer set is chip's own.

### BD-Controller-NetworkStepsOverIP — the network steps also run over IP when credentials are given

matter.js registers the NetworkCommissioning steps of the commissioning
flow only on a BLE channel (`ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:595-620` at
`db021da0`: "Care about Network commissioning only when we are on BLE,
because else we are already on IP network"). This module runs the same
steps (:1555-2008; Wi-Fi :1595, Thread :1776) over any channel when, and
only when, the operator passes credentials (`commissioner.Options`,
`pair --wifi-ssid/--wifi-credentials`, `--thread-dataset`); without them
the IP flow is matter.js's. Report BA §3 (phase 12, 2026-10-17).

By design. The steps are provable against the reference daemon's simulated
Wi-Fi interface without a radio, and a device reached over Ethernet that
should also join Wi-Fi can be provisioned.

### BD-chip-WiFiNetworkCommissioningServer — the device-side Wi-Fi NetworkCommissioning server follows chip, TESTING ONLY

matter.js's `NetworkCommissioningServer.ts` is an 18-line generated stub at
`0ceb202d`; the command semantics the flow expects of a Wi-Fi device
(`ScanNetworks`, `AddOrUpdateWiFiNetwork` with the credential length rule,
`RemoveNetwork`, `ConnectNetwork`, `ReorderNetwork`, `Networks`,
`LastNetworkingStatus`, `LastNetworkID`, `LastConnectErrorValue`) are
taken from chip's
`src/app/clusters/network-commissioning/NetworkCommissioningCluster.cpp`
(harness pin `6170af84`), as the parity contract allows where matter.js has
no behaviour. `core.WiFiNetworkCommissioning` sits behind
`contract.WiFiDriver` and — since wave 28b (2026-11-11) — the public
`node.Network.WiFi.Driver`, no longer a test seam (the heading keeps its
words for the links to it); `wifi/wpasupplicant` is the Linux driver
(BD-chip-WpaSupplicantDriver). The reference daemon mounts it only with
`--wifi-sim`, so the FeatureMap and the composition the harness certifies
do not move. Report BA §4. The
committed networks — SSID and credentials — are kept in the node's
`store.Settings` (`WiFiNetworkCommissioningConfig.Store`), as the Linux
driver keeps its network in the KVS (`NetworkCommissioningWiFiDriver.cpp`
`CommitConfiguration` :135-167, `Init` :77-128), and `Start` rejoins the
first one when the node starts, recording the result as chip's
`OnNetworkingStatusChange` does when the link returns
(`NetworkCommissioningCluster.cpp:283-307`); a network is connected while
the link is on it (`WiFiNetworkIterator::Next`, driver :275-310): after a
failsafe revert the committed network reads connected once the link is back
on it, which the rejoin brings about (`BD-chip-WiFiRejoinBackoff`), and after
a failed join none does. The revert and the rejoin are
reported to subscriptions (`OnAttributeChange`), and a Breadcrumb a
NetworkCommissioning command writes is reported by GeneralCommissioning's
own notifier, as chip marks both dirty where they change. TC-CNET-4.1, 4.4
and 4.9 run on the restarted daemon since phase 30.

By design. A real Wi-Fi driver is roadmap milestone 7.

Review II, phase 6b (N4-d4wifi-1): ConnectNetwork on a switched-off interface switches it on before the join, whatever the network id, without starting the committed network's rejoin, as connectedhomeip's Thread driver: `MatchesNetworkId` is not consulted before `if (!GetEnabled()) { Delete(kInterfaceEnabled) }` (`src/platform/OpenThread/GenericNetworkCommissioningThreadDriver.cpp:205-213` at `6170af84`), the one chip driver that models the switch (`SetEnabled(bool)` overridden only there and in the cluster's test fakes); a driver that does not switch on fails the command. matter.js's `NetworkCommissioningServer.ts:18` is an empty class.

### BD-Controller-BleReliableExchange — one reliable exchange manager per BLE channel

matter.js marks a BLE channel reliable (`Ble.ts:38` `isReliable = true`)
and a session then does not use MRP (`Session.ts:368-370` `usesMrp`, at
`db021da0`). This
module expresses the same as `exchange.Config.Reliable` on an exchange
manager created per BTP channel with a synthetic peer address, since the
UDP/TCP managers key their peers by network address. Report BA §2.

By design. The idiom differs, the rule (no retransmission, no MRP
parameters over BTP) is matter.js's.

### BD-Go-BtpRejections — BTP refusals that exist only on the Go side

`transport/btp` refuses a message longer than 0xFFFF (the BTP length
field), a segment with no room for payload after the header, and a
truncated packet (`ErrTruncated`) with named errors; matter.js's
`BtpCodec.ts` / `BtpSessionHandler.ts` reach the same outcomes as thrown
exceptions without these distinctions. Timers and window sizes are
`BleConsts.ts`'s verbatim (15 s / 15 s / 5 s / 60 s, window 255, thresholds
1 and 2, segment 20–244). Report BA §1.

By design. Go's error surface; the wire behaviour is identical.

### BD-Matter-BtpInboundMessageBounded — an inbound BTP message is held to the datagram bound

Inbound BTP messages above 2048 bytes (`udp.MaxDatagramSize`) end the channel on the controller (`controller/ble/channel.go` `maxInboundMessage`) and the session on the device (`transport/btp/session.go`, the beginning segment's declared length), as connectedhomeip refuses an inbound BTP message larger than its buffer (`src/ble/BtpEngine.cpp:305`, `:312-314`, `:329-331` at `6170af84`); matter.js accepts up to the declared length (`packages/protocol/src/ble/BtpSessionHandler.ts:314`, `:323-331` at `db021da0`) and states a BLE channel's payload bound as 1232 bytes (`packages/protocol/src/ble/Ble.ts:37`, `BleConsts.ts:79`, `packages/general/src/net/udp/UdpSocket.ts:12`). Pinned by `controller/ble:TestInboundMessageAboveTheDatagramBoundEndsTheChannel`, `transport/btp:TestBtpSessionRefusesAMessageAboveTheDatagramBound`.

By design, as connectedhomeip. Review II, TM R5 5a.5.

### BD-Controller-BluezWithoutNobleRetries — `ble/bluez` ports the sequence, not noble's recovery

matter.js's node platform drives BLE through noble/bleno over raw HCI
(`packages/nodejs-ble/src/NobleBleClient.ts`, `NobleBleChannel.ts` at
`0ceb202d`); this module's `ble/bluez` drives BlueZ over D-Bus. The
sequence and the timeouts are noble's (`NobleBleChannel.ts:203` connect
2 min, :220 interview 1 min, :38 stop 5 s); not ported are the reconnect on
a disconnect during connect (:273-297), the 2 s MTU settle wait (:526-560)
and the `connectable` check (`NobleBleClient.ts:184-187`), which BlueZ
either does itself or has no property for. Report BB §1 (phase 13,
2026-10-18).

By design. A different stack under the same seam; what BlueZ guarantees is
not re-implemented above it.

### BD-Controller-BleNodeLocatedByChannel — a BLE-found node is located by its commissioning channel

matter.js records a peripheral as a `NetworkAddress` of type `"ble"` in the
node's addresses (`CommissioningClient.ts:910-945` at `862ad75f`), which passes the
"has the node been located" check (:254-257). `client.Record`'s addresses
are IP only; `Registry.Commission` therefore accepts a node without
addresses when `Options.Channel` (the BTP channel) is set, and the
operational address arrives through DNS-SD after the network steps as it
does in matter.js. Report BB §2.

By design. The record keeps one address type; the channel carries the
BLE case.

### BD-chip-CnetWifiProvisionedAfterIP — the CNETWIFI harness run provisions the Wi-Fi network after IP commissioning

chip's test harness commissions a Wi-Fi DUT over BLE and configures the
network in the flow (`AutoCommissioner.cpp:780-797` at `6170af84`: no
network is configured when commissioning over IP). The harness here
commissions the reference daemon (`--wifi-sim`) over IP and then adds the
cases' PIXIT network (`zigbeehome` / `password123`) with the same commands
the flow would send (`testdata/provision_wifi.py`, four chip-tool commands
for the YAML cases), so the CNET Wi-Fi cases see the state a BLE-Wi-Fi
commissioning leaves. Report BB §4.

By design. The harness image has no CHIPoBLE; the DUT state, not the
transport, is what the cases judge.

### BD-Controller-BleOverEsphomeProxies — `ble/esphome` commissions through ESPHome Bluetooth proxies; matter.js and chip reach BLE only through a local adapter

matter.js's `packages/nodejs-ble` reaches BLE through noble on a local
adapter and names proxies only as a reason for `isPeripheralReachable`
(`BleScanner.ts:46-52` at `862ad75f`); connectedhomeip has no ESPHome
transport either — what it has at `6170af84` is a proxy of Matter's own,
the Commissioning Proxy cluster (0x0455,
`src/app/clusters/commissioning-proxy-server/README.md:1-9`), through which
a commissioner tunnels its commissioning packets to a device the proxy
node reaches (`src/transport/raw/ProxyTransport.h:19-32`,
`src/transport/raw/PeerAddress.h:60`,
`src/controller/AutoCommissioner.cpp:788-797`). `ble/esphome` (brief BP1, ADR 0024 decision 3 amended
2026-10-27) runs the BlueZ platform's sequence — scan for the Matter
service data, connect, C1 write-with-response, C2 indications, C3 read —
over the ESPHome native API after aioesphomeapi (`api.proto`,
`_frame_helper/noise.py` at 3b2a4a2d) and ESPHome's `bluetooth_proxy`
behaviour (at 1cc6c9d1): the client writes C2's CCCD itself (the firmware
registers locally only, `bluetooth_connection_bluedroid.cpp:325`), parses
the raw advertisement bytes, takes the ATT MTU from
`BluetoothDeviceConnectionResponse`, and implements `isPeripheralReachable`
from the proxies' free connection slots. A proxy has one API subscriber;
the central logs `ble.esphome.proxy_taken`, reconnects once after 30 s of
silence and reports `ErrProxyBusy` on a second silence, cleared by the
next fresh scan. The silence counts advertisements of any kind, so in a
BLE-quiet environment (a shielded lab, a remote site) a proxy nobody else
uses is presumed taken too — a false positive the host answers by raising
`Options.SilenceTimeout` (`ble/esphome/central.go`, `DefaultSilenceTimeout`;
documented in the package doc and `docs/guides/ble-proxies.md`,
W4-ctlint-13). Reasoning: a host without a Bluetooth adapter commissions
through the proxies a Home Assistant site already has; neither reference
speaks ESPHome's protocol, so there is no behaviour to mirror and no marker
to watch.

**Discovery (brief BP2, 2026-10-27).** The proxies are found over DNS-SD
(`_esphomelib._tcp.local.`, the service ESPHome's `mdns_component.cpp`
advertises with the TXT keys `version`, `mac`, `config_hash`, `board`) and
keyed per device by name or MAC (`esphome.Keys`, `ParseKey`); whether a
device is a Bluetooth proxy is learned after connecting, from its
capability flags, not from the record. matter.js's DNS-SD ingress admits
Matter's three service types only (`MdnsService.ts:27, :90-94` and
`CommissionableMdnsScanner.ts:100-105` at `862ad75f`), so
`client/discovery.Names.Browse` widens the filter for the requested type
while a browse runs. The central re-browses every five minutes and on every
proxy loss, follows a moved address and drops a discovered proxy only when
it is unadvertised and idle; a given proxy always stays. matter.js has no
counterpart (it reaches BLE through a local adapter only), so the discovery
is this module's own, pinned by `ble/esphome`'s discovery tests and
`fabrictest.Device.BLE()`.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): aioesphomeapi at `3b2a4a2d` and ESPHome at
`1cc6c9d1` are outside the exports the review read and were not re-read;
what this entry says of them is unverified.

Review II, phase 6b: a discovered proxy is used only with a key, unless `DiscoverOptions.AllowPlaintext` (owner decision 196). The test kit (`ble/esphome/esphometest`) ends the earlier link when a second connect arrives for its address; that is the kit's own rule, and the firmware's answer to it is not modelled (R2-P6-test-2055).

Review II, run 3 (R3-sec-3303): a keyed proxy is trusted for its own statements: a key holder that states another keyed device's MAC keeps that device out of the set, as before R2-C2-bound-2003 it could attract every connect through the RSSI it reports (`ble/esphome/central.go`, the RSSI pick). A MAC stated over the plaintext API identifies nothing to a keyed connection: a keyed newcomer whose MAC a plaintext holder states is admitted beside it, and `Discover` prefers the keyed entry. Pinned by `ble/esphome:TestPlaintextMACDoesNotShadowAKeyedProxy`, `TestDiscoverPrefersTheKeyedEntry`.

### BD-Controller-BluezScanWithoutUuidFilter — `ble/bluez` scans LE without a `UUIDs` discovery filter

matter.js scans with noble's `startScanningAsync([MatterBle.SERVICE_UUID_SHORT],
true)` (`packages/nodejs-ble/src/NobleBleClient.ts:84` at `0ceb202d`).
noble's hci-socket binding keeps that list in user space
(`@stoprocent/noble` 2.8.0, `lib/hci-socket/bindings.js:105`) and matches
it against the advertisement's service UUIDs **and the UUIDs of its service
data** (`:273-286`), so a Matter advertisement — Flags and Service Data 16
only — passes. BlueZ's `SetDiscoveryFilter` with `UUIDs` instead becomes the
kernel's service discovery (MGMT Start Service Discovery), which passes only
advertisements carrying the UUID in a UUID16/32/128 field; the `ble-virtual`
run 39100460695 shows hci0 receiving the peripheral's ADV_IND and reporting
no device. connectedhomeip's Linux scanner sets `Transport "le"` alone for
this reason (`src/platform/Linux/bluez/ChipDeviceScanner.cpp:227-236` at
`6170af84`). `ble/bluez` therefore filters on `Transport "le"` and
`DuplicateData` and selects the device by the Matter service data in the
discovery callback, which is what noble's user-space match amounts to.
Report BC (phase 13b, 2026-10-18).

By design. The same selection as matter.js, placed where BlueZ lets it
run; the kernel filter would never see a Matter advertisement.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): `@stoprocent/noble` 2.8.0 is outside the
exports the review read and was not re-read; what this entry says of it is
unverified.

### BD-Matter-SessionParams-ZeroIsUnset — a zero session parameter means "not stated"

`secure/sessionparams/sessionparams.go:44-48`: a zero field is omitted on
the wire and read as the spec default. matter.js checks a stated value at
run time — a zero, fractional or untyped maxPathsPerInvoke takes the
fallback (`session/SessionParameters.ts:75-87`), a local one is refused
(`session/SessionManager.ts:75-81`, called at `:296-298` and `:412-414`;
all at `db021da0`). Those inputs cannot reach the Go
type, so the cases that feed them are `missing` with this entry as the
reason. Report BH (phase 16, 2026-10-18).

By design. Go's zero value is the absence matter.js spells `undefined`;
the one real gap (an oversized wire value masked) is in the findings
register.

### BD-Matter-MonotonicClockTests — session and peer-loss time runs on the monotonic clock

matter.js stamps a session's creation and a peer-loss `asOf` on
`Time.nowUs`, "not a wall-clock time" (`session/Session.ts:59-60`,
`session/SessionManager.ts:671-672`, `:678`, at `db021da0`), and its tests step the wall
clock apart from it to prove that. Go's `time.Time` comparisons use the
monotonic reading, and `clocktest.Fake` has one reading, so a wall-clock
step is not expressible; the step cases of SessionManagerTest,
ExchangeManagerTest and BleScannerTest are `missing` with this entry as
the reason. Report BH (phase 16, 2026-10-18).

By design. The guarantee matter.js tests for is the one Go's clock gives;
a second reading in `clocktest` would test the fake, not the module.

### BD-Matter-EventNumberEpoch — the event-number epoch is chip's 0x10000

`im/eventlog.go` (the epoch default in the log's constructor): an epoch of 0 selects chip's
`CHIP_DEVICE_CONFIG_EVENT_ID_COUNTER_EPOCH` and the ceiling is persisted
inclusive. matter.js reserves in blocks of 1 000 by default, counts a block
size of 0 as 1 (`events/BaseEventStore.ts:43-51`) and stores the exclusive
next number (`:153-162`). Neither reuses a number across a restart; the
gap a restart leaves differs. Report BH (phase 16, 2026-10-18).

By design. The chip-tool families judge the numbering a device shows after
a restart against chip's epoch; the register keeps the block-size cases
as `missing` under this entry.

### BD-Matter-AttestationDERAsReceived — attestation certificates are kept as received

DAC, PAI and PAA are parsed with `crypto/x509` from the DER as received
and never re-encoded; matter.js decodes them into its own structure, reads
the issuer DN as it reads the subject (`certificate/kinds/Certificate.ts:729`,
`:740` at `b25ed960`) and re-encodes. The recode and round-trip cases of
CertificatesTest are `missing` under this entry. Report BH (phase 16,
2026-10-18).

The vendor and product id are read from the parsed name by matter.js's rule
at `db021da0` since review II (owner decision 33, R2-P1-sec-02); until
`0a1d4e6d` they were read more leniently — hex digits in either case and of
any length, the commonName fallback whenever both attributes read as absent
— a difference no row or finding had recorded. The rule
(`certificate/kinds/Certificate.ts` and `kinds/DistinguishedName.ts`): a
matter-oid-vid or matter-oid-pid attribute is exactly 4 uppercase hex
digits (`parseMatterRdnHex`, `Certificate.ts:242-249`, `:341-345`) and
occurs once (`DistinguishedName.ts:261-270`), else
`CertificateProfileError` (`Certificate.ts:346-349`); the `Mvid:`/`Mpid:`
commonName fallback is read only when the DN carries neither attribute, a
malformed one counting (`:343`, `:377-381`), from the first commonName that
carries a value, in its first 64 bytes (`DistinguishedName.ts:345-346`,
`:364-374`); a prefix without 4 uppercase hex digits is a
`CertificateError` (`:63-72`). `controller/attestation` (`matterIDsOf`)
reads it strictly, issuer before subject, and the validator answers
`DacFormatInvalid` or `PaiFormatInvalid` as matter.js's does
(`DeviceAttestationValidator.ts:181-188`, `:263-264`). `secure/attestation`
(`productIDsOf`, behind `ValidateProduct`) reads a malformed or repeated
attribute as absent, as the device's read of its own DAC and PAI does with
`acceptMalformedVidPid` (`DeviceCertification.ts:116-120`,
`Certificate.ts:350-351`, `DistinguishedName.ts:318-320`): an id the
certificate does not state readably is not judged against the product —
matter.js's behaviour, pinned there by "starts a device whose own DAC has
a malformed VendorID" (`AttestationCertificateProfileTest.ts:610-624`),
not a gap. Two copies of one rule, one per layer; what `crypto/x509` makes
of a DN value before either reads it is in
`BD-Matter-Attestation-ProfileOnCryptoX509`. Ported:
`controller/attestation:TestProfileVendorProductIDInTheDN`,
`secure/attestation:TestProductIDsAcceptMalformed` and
`TestValidateProductOverAMalformedVendorID`.

By design. A re-encoded attestation certificate has no consumer here; the
vendor-id read happens on the parsed name. The operational-certificate
side is different: there the TBS is rebuilt from every DN attribute the
TLV carries (the X.520 gap closed after PR #164).

### BD-Matter-Attestation-ProfileOnCryptoX509 — the DAC and PAI profile is read beside crypto/x509, which refuses more

The DAC and PAI profile is matter.js's (`kinds/AttestationCertificates.ts:92-196`
at `db021da0`), read from the DER by `controller/attestation/profile.go`
beside `crypto/x509`, which parses the rest. `crypto/x509` refuses a
certificate that carries any extension twice and a critical flag that is
not DER (`0x00`/`0xFF`); matter.js parses both (`Certificate.ts:390-397`
at `b25ed960` reads any non-zero byte as true) and refuses a duplicate only
of basic constraints, key usage, SKID or AKID, in the profile. A DAC or PAI
that carries one of those four twice is still `DacFormatInvalid` or
`PaiFormatInvalid` (the profile reads the DER when `crypto/x509` refuses
it); one that repeats another extension, a PAA that repeats any, or a
non-DER critical flag is `CertificateUnparseable` here. The commissioner's
DAC key after a policy accepted a failed attestation is read by
`crypto/x509` too (`controller/commissioner/flow.go` `dacKeyOf`), the
