### BD-chip-CameraAvStream-DefaultsWhereTheModelHasNone — attributes without a model default start at chip's values

The matter.js model names no default for most CameraAvStreamManagement
attributes, and matter.js refuses to serve a mandatory attribute without
a value. Requiring every camera host to set them would put chip's member
defaults into each host; the server starts them at chip's values instead
(`CameraAVStreamManagementCluster.h:405-445`, `:740-764`: NightVision On,
the maximum levels 254, StatusLightBrightness Medium, the rest zero or
false) and keeps the model's default where it names one
(MicrophoneAGCEnabled and StatusLightEnabled `true`, chip `false`), since
schema values come from matter.js verbatim. Owner decision 2026-10-27.

### BD-chip-CameraAvStream-SnapshotBound — the capture size bound is the TCP message size less chip's margin, configurable

chip bounds a captured snapshot by its platform packet buffer
(`CameraAVStreamManagementCluster.h:53-55`), which the module does not
have. `DefaultMaxSnapshotSize` is matter.js's MaxTCPMessageSize fallback
(64000) less chip's 100, and `Config.MaxSnapshotSize` overrides it; the
bound is not read from the session's negotiated size at invoke time.
Owner decision 2026-10-27.

### BD-chip-FailSafeOfTheAccessingFabric — a command under the fail-safe needs the window of its own fabric

matter.js's `OperationalCredentialsServer.ts:602-604` at `862ad75f` reads the
DeviceCommissioner's one `failsafeContext`, so CSRRequest, AddNOC and
AddTrustedRootCertificate pass under a window any fabric armed (or one armed
over PASE). connectedhomeip asks `IsFailSafeArmed(accessingFabricIndex)` —
armed and `MatchesFabricIndex` (`FailSafeContext.h:76-79, :92-96` at
`6170af84`) — and answers FAILSAFE_REQUIRED otherwise
(`OperationalCredentialsCluster.cpp:341, :472, :760`; Thread Border Router
Management `:212`; Joint Fabric Administrator `:325, :369`; Network
Commissioning's AddOrUpdate, RemoveNetwork and ConnectNetwork through
`EnsureFailsafeIsArmed`, `NetworkCommissioningCluster.cpp:155-172, :380,
:568, :609, :644`). This module follows chip (owner decision 2026-11-01, review
W3-clusec-03, W3-club1-02, W3-clua2-01, and the W3 PR for the Thread and
Wi-Fi NetworkCommissioning servers): the node's fail-safe port is
`core.GeneralCommissioning.FailSafeFabric` (armed, and for which fabric), the
servers test it with `core.FailSafeArmedFor`; the two NetworkCommissioning
servers take it through `AttachFailSafe` / `Config.FailSafe` and keep the
fabric-blind `IsFailSafeArmed` port for a host without one, deprecated
since review II (R2-C2-sec-1006, decision 515) and removable in v0.28.0: a
server wired with that port alone gates on any fabric's window, and logs
`netcomm.failsafe_blind_port` once when it does — a decided exception to
README §The deprecation window, rule 2 (decision 522: the blind port opens
network commissioning to a foreign fabric's window); UpdateNOC keeps
matter.js's own answer for another fabric's window, ConstraintError
(`OperationalCredentialsServer.ts:355-360`). Reasoning: another fabric must
not consume or roll back the commissioning state of a window it did not arm.
Pinned by `TestParityOpcreds_FailSafeOfAnotherFabricIsNotArmed`,
`TestThreadBorderRouterManagementCluster_FailsafeOfAnotherFabric`,
`TestICACCommandsNeedTheAccessingFabricsFailSafe`,
`TestThreadNetworkCommissioningFailSafeOfAnotherFabric`,
`TestWiFiNetworkCommissioningFailSafeOfAnotherFabric`,
`TestWiFiNetworkCommissioningBlindFailSafePortLogsOnce` and
`TestThreadNetworkCommissioningBlindFailSafePortLogsOnce`.

### BD-chip-ClosureControl-RulesInServer — the ClosureControl command rules are connectedhomeip's; matter.js has none

matter.js's `ClosureControlServer` is the empty subclass
(`packages/node/src/behaviors/closure-control/ClosureControlServer.ts:17` at
`862ad75f`), so `cluster/closure.ControlServer` follows connectedhomeip's
`ClosureControlCluster.cpp` at `6170af84` behind the `Mover` port. MoveTo
(`HandleMoveTo` `:554-639`): none of Position, Latch and Speed is
INVALID_COMMAND (`:558`), a Position outside the advertised set
CONSTRAINT_ERROR, and in any MainState other than Moving, WaitingForMotion
or Stopped INVALID_IN_STATE before the mover is called (`:599-605`;
W3-club1-01, `TestClosureControlMoveToMainStateChip`); the server starts in
SetupRequired until the host reports a state. The CONSTRAINT_ERROR for a
Position whose feature is not advertised is this server's, from the enum
value's conformance and before the mover (`cluster/closure/closurecontrol_server.go:444`,
`:662-672`, ahead of the mover call at `:551`;
`TestMoveToTakesTheGeneratedRequest`): connectedhomeip answers
CONSTRAINT_ERROR for a value outside the enum only (`:574`) and, for a
defined position whose feature it lacks, FAILURE after the delegate ran and
MainState moved, because `SetOverallTargetState` refuses it (`:222-238`,
`:435-436`, `:622-637`; review II, W3-club1-10). chip's null-OverallCurrentState
gate (`:560-562`) has no counterpart: this server reads OverallCurrentState
as a struct whose fields are null until observed. Stop (`HandleStop`
`:531-551`): only Moving, WaitingForMotion and Calibrating stop, SUCCESS
always (with `BD-Matter-ClosureControl-StopObserver`), and OverallTargetState
is left as it was (W3-club1-05). One addition chip does not make — of its command
handlers only MoveTo writes OverallTargetState (`:637`): a reported CurrentPosition
that is the target's own position clears the target, a position on the way
(PartiallyOpened) keeps it, so a target reads only while it is outstanding.
The fallback target
and the ignored Latch and Speed of features the server does not serve are
the specification text matter.js carries (`closure-control.resource.ts`).
Reasoning: chip is the only reference with rules (W3-club1-06). Retire when
matter.js's server gains them.

Phase 38 serves MotionLatching, Instantaneous, Speed and Calibration after
the same file, behind the row (`closure.Ahead`, surface yes). A declared
LT, SP or CL needs the `Mover`'s optional `closurecontrol.Latcher`,
`SpeedMover` or `Calibrator` (`cluster/spec/closurecontrol/server_gen.go`),
else `ErrFeatureMap` names the interface; IS is a declaration fact, and SP
with IS is the definition's conformance refusal (chip's constructor dies
on it, `:49-53`). LatchControlModes is the Latcher's, fixed (`:81`); Stop
with IS is UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND (`:535`) and IS withdraws Stop and
MovementCompleted from the lists (`:107`, `:680`); Calibrate is
UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND without CL, SUCCESS without a call while Calibrating,
INVALID_IN_STATE outside Stopped and SetupRequired, and MainState
Calibrating after the Calibrator's success (`:642-665`). MoveTo's Latch
needs RemoteLatching / RemoteUnlatching or is INVALID_IN_STATE
(`:579-590`), an unknown Speed is CONSTRAINT_ERROR (`:592-597`), a Position
change of a latched closure without Latch false INVALID_IN_STATE
(`:607-620`); the drive hears unlatch, speed, motion, latch in that order,
as chip's closure-app orders a panel's actions
(`examples/closure-app/linux/ClosureManager.cpp` `HandlePanelUnlatchAction`
:595, `HandlePanelSetTargetAction` :656). SecureState stays derived: with LT
true only FullyClosed and latched, null with an unknown latch — chip
refuses any other true SecureState (`:364-386`); a drive report carrying
Latch or Speed without the feature is refused, and a speed outside the enum is ignored (`:342-360`); a reached latch
clears OverallTargetState's Latch as an arrival clears its Position (the
addition above). Two differences: a request whose Latch and Speed are
both ignored keeps the fallback to OverallTargetState.Position and changes
nothing without one, where chip calls the delegate and sets Moving; and a
MoveTo is Moving, never WaitingForMotion — chip's `IsReadyToMove`
(`:626-635`) has no port, the drive reports WaitingForMotion itself.
CountdownTime and LT without PS stay out (the server serves Positioning
always). Parity: `closurecontrol_features_chip_test.go` (the chip unit
tests `TestHandleCalibrate`, `TestHandleMoveToAllFeatures`,
`TestHandleMoveToLatchedPositionChangeRequiresUnlatch`,
`TestHandleMoveToRemoteLatchingConformanceChecks`,
`TestHandleMoveToConstraintValidation`,
`TestSetOverallCurrentStateFeatureValidation`, by meaning).

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): connectedhomeip's
`examples/closure-app/linux/ClosureManager.cpp` is outside the exports the
review read and was not re-read; what this entry says of it is unverified.

Review II, close-out C3 (R2-C2-fsm-1550, with R2-P1-clu-01 and
R2-P6-fsm-1580): MoveTo, Calibrate and Stop keep a MainState (for MoveTo
also a reached target) the drive reported while the mover had the command,
inline or from another goroutine, and do not overwrite it with the outcome
written after the mover returned (`stateReports`,
`cluster/closure/closurecontrol_server.go`). connectedhomeip writes Stopped
after a successful delegate Stop unconditionally
(`src/app/clusters/closure-control-server/ClosureControlCluster.cpp:544-548`
at `6170af84`) and, after a successful delegate MoveTo, Moving when
`mDelegate.IsReadyToMove()` and WaitingForMotion otherwise (`:623-634`), so a
report from inside the delegate ends as Stopped, Moving or WaitingForMotion
there and as the report here.
Reason: a report from another goroutine has no serial order in which the
command's outcome is newer, and the module keeps one rule for both cases.
Pinned by `cluster/closure:TestClosureControlReportDuringTheCallIsKept`.

### BD-chip-Valve-RulesInServer — the valve's rules, Level and TimeSync are connectedhomeip's; matter.js has none

matter.js's `ValveConfigurationAndControlServer` is the empty subclass
(`packages/node/src/behaviors/valve-configuration-and-control/ValveConfigurationAndControlServer.ts:14`
at `862ad75f`), so `cluster/valve.Server` follows connectedhomeip's
`ValveConfigurationAndControlCluster.cpp` at `6170af84` behind the
`StateSource` port, which holds the state chip's cluster keeps itself. The
rules served before phase 38: an unchanged DefaultOpenDuration write is a
no-op success (`:165-166`), Open and Close reach the source and a source
error is FAILURE (chip's FailureDueToFault needs a ValveFault the port does
not carry), an absent OpenDuration means DefaultOpenDuration and a present
null an indefinite opening (`:300-310`). Phase 38 adds Level (LVL) and
TimeSync (TS), behind the row (`valve.Ahead`, surface yes). LVL needs the
source's `LevelSource` (CurrentLevel, TargetLevel), DefaultOpenLevel its
`DefaultOpenLevelSource`, each refused with `ErrSelection` naming what is
missing. TS reads the node's Matter time, the root TimeSynchronization's
UTC, which the node hands the server as its endpoint joins the topology
(`valve.Server.AttachMatterTime`, the server's one input of it), as chip's
tracker asks the node's TimeSynchronization for a valid time and reads the
clock SetUTCTime sets (`CodegenIntegration.cpp:46-58`; the cluster's `:391-400`). Chip's
Startup refuses TS without a time tracker (`:46-50`): a node with
`TimeSynchronization.Off` refuses a TS valve in the same way: the
Aggregator's Add and Replace refuse it before it joins the set, with an
error naming the endpoint and cluster (`valve.Server.RequiresMatterTime`;
the topology check behind them is a backstop); a TS server outside a node is built
without a time and, until its host attaches one, every Open leaves
AutoCloseTime null — the standalone case's recorded divergence, since
`valve.New` cannot know whether the host will attach. A DefaultOpenLevel write is 1 to 100
and 100 or a multiple of LevelStep, an unchanged one a no-op (`:175-192`,
`ValueCompliesWithLevelStep` `:483-490`); an Open resolves its level — the
command's TargetLevel, else DefaultOpenLevel where served, else 100 — and a
TargetLevel off the LevelStep grid is CONSTRAINT_ERROR (`:312-341`); the
resolved level reaches the source in the request's TargetLevel, as chip
hands it to `HandleOpenValve(level)`
(`valve-configuration-and-control-delegate.h:39`). AutoCloseTime is the
Matter time at the Open plus the opening's duration (`:391-413`), set anew
as the time plus RemainingDuration whenever the node adopts a time while
the valve counts down — chip's `UpdateAutoCloseTime` (`:415-423`), which
the reference application's `UTCTimeAvailabilityChanged` calls
(`examples/all-clusters-app/linux/ValveControlDelegate.cpp:70-73`) —, null for
an indefinite opening, without a synchronized time (`:394`), after a Close
(`:243-247`), and — where chip's countdown closes the valve — once the
source reports no RemainingDuration. Differences: the Matter time carries
epoch-s, so AutoCloseTime is whole seconds; TargetLevel 0 on Close
(`:253-256`) and CurrentLevel are the source's report, not the server's
write; a TargetLevel without LVL stays CONSTRAINT_ERROR where chip ignores
it (issue 42777, `:274-276`). Parity: `valve_level_chip_test.go`
(`WriteAttributeTestDefaultOpenLevelOutOfRange`,
`SetAutoCloseTimeNoIntegerOverflow`, `OpenCommandFieldsValidation`, the
Level reads, by meaning). Reasoning: chip is the only reference with
rules. Retire when matter.js's server gains them.
### BD-Matter-ICDVerificationKeyConstantTime — the ICD VerificationKey is compared in constant time

matter.js's `IcdManagementServer.ts:756-764` at `862ad75f` (`#assertMayModify`)
lets a Manage caller modify or unregister an ICD client when its
VerificationKey equals the stored ICDToken, compared with `Bytes.areEqual`
(`:761`). `cluster/core/icd_management.go` `assertMayModify` takes the same
decision — Administer modifies any entry, otherwise the key must match,
FAILURE if not — but compares with `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`
after a length check (review 2026-11 W2-sec-04). Reasoning: the key is a
shared secret that gates rewriting another client's registration, and a
constant-time compare costs nothing. Pinned by
`TestICDVerificationKeyComparedInConstantTime`.

### BD-Matter-OtaImageHeaderSizeCap — an OTA image header over 1024 bytes is refused before it is read

matter.js's `OtaImageReader.#processHeader` (`OtaImageReader.ts:157-191` at
`862ad75f`) takes the header size the 16-byte prefix states (`:182`) and
collects that many bytes as the stream delivers them, without a bound.
`bdx/otaimage.ReadHeader` refuses a stated size over `MaxHeaderSize` (1024)
as `ErrInvalid` before it reads the header, as connectedhomeip does
(`src/lib/core/OTAImageHeader.cpp:53` `kMaxHeaderSize`, checked at `:128`,
"Safety check against malicious headers", at `6170af84`) (review 2026-11
W4-ctlint-07). Reasoning: a consumer streaming an image from the network
would otherwise pay whatever a hostile prefix claims; every header this
module or chip's tooling writes stays far below the cap. Pinned by
`TestReadHeaderRefusesOversizeHeader` and the `FuzzReadHeader` seed.

### BD-Matter-OtaImageDigestAtStore — `Images.Store` verifies the header's payload digest when the ledger carries no checksum

matter.js's `DclOtaUpdateService.#verifyUpdate` (`DclOtaUpdateService.ts:388-408`
at `862ad75f`) passes checksum options to `OtaImageReader.file` only when the
DCL record carries `otaChecksum`; without them `calculateFullChecksum`
defaults to true (`OtaImageReader.ts:70`), the reader takes the full-checksum
branch and verifies the payload size only (`:246-260`); the header's payload
digest is checked later, at extraction (`:282-332` at `db021da0`,
`#extractAndValidatePayload`). `controller/softwareupdate.Images.Store` runs
`otaimage.ValidateFile` with the payload digest in both cases
(`storeValidation`), so a corrupted local image is refused when it is stored,
not when it is first served over BDX (review 2026-11 W4-ctlint-03; owner
decision 2026-11-02). Reasoning: the store is the one place that reads the
whole file once; a digest failure at serve time would surface as a device's
failed download. Pinned by `TestImagesStoreValidatesFileParity`. The reuse
check of `Images.DownloadUpdate` validates a stored image the same way, as
matter.js's `#checkStoredImage` runs `#verifyUpdate` on it (`:433-451`).

### BD-Matter-OtaImages-DeleteProductWithoutMode — `Images.Delete` narrows by product without a mode too

matter.js's `DclOtaUpdateService.delete` documents `productId` as a filter
of the files to delete, but reads it only together with a mode: a call with
`vendorId` and `productId` and no `mode` (nor `isProduction`) falls through
to the vendor branch and deletes every file of the vendor
(`packages/protocol/src/dcl/DclOtaUpdateService.ts:1226-1243`, `:1245-1274`
at `862ad75f`). `controller/softwareupdate.Images.Delete` applies
`DeleteOptions.ProductID` with or without a mode, so that call deletes the
product's images only (pinned by `TestImagesDeleteParity`). Reasoning: the
documented contract, not a fall-through that deletes other products' images.

### BD-Thread-TBRM-ChipLogic — ThreadBorderRouterManagement follows connectedhomeip behind the `BorderRouter` port

matter.js's `ThreadBorderRouterManagementServer.ts:14` at `862ad75f` is the
empty subclass. `cluster/threadbr.ManagementServer` follows connectedhomeip's
`ThreadBorderRouterManagementCluster.cpp` at `6170af84`: the reads (:32),
the command rules of `InvokeCommand` (:148-322: NEEDS_TIMED and
FAILSAFE_REQUIRED, the pending dataset's sequence, INVALID_IN_STATE, the
revert on fail-safe expiry), `OnActivateDatasetComplete` (:272) and the
fail-safe events (:297), with `ThreadBorderRouterManagementDelegate.h:63-106`
as the port. `thread/otbr.BorderRouter` adapts OTBR's REST API as chip's
`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate` adapts OpenThread; the activation polls
the node state until attached, bounded by the fail-safe's context. Three
deliberate differences: the server caches the border router's values (read
at construction, after each command and on `Refresh`; chip reads the
delegate on every read), so an agent id that is not 16 bytes fails
construction rather than the read; `PanChange` is a feature selection, not
a port method; and the activation flag is held in memory, not persisted as
chip's `kFailsafeActiveDatasetConfigured`, so there is no revert after a
reboot. The fail-safe check asks for the accessing fabric's fail-safe, as
chip's `:212` does (`failSafeArmedFor`,
`cluster/threadbr/management.go:292-306`, `:359-361`;
`BD-chip-FailSafeOfTheAccessingFabric`). The
revert over REST ends with the interface disabled and the dataset left in
place when the border router answers `DELETE /node/dataset/active` with
405: ot-br-posix at main registers only GET and PUT on that path
(`rest_web_server.cpp`, the `RegisterGet`/`RegisterPut` of
`OT_REST_RESOURCE_PATH_NODE_DATASET_ACTIVE`), matter.js's
`deleteActiveDataset` (`OtbrRestClient.ts:428-433`) targets a firmware that
had the route, and chip's empty-dataset attach
(`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:191-208`) has no REST equivalent
(found by the first virtual OTBR run, 2026-10-28). Pinned by
`management_chip_test.go` (chip's 22 cases) and the `fabrictest` wire tests.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): ot-br-posix's `rest_web_server.cpp` is
outside the exports the review read and was not re-read; what this entry
says of it is unverified.

Review II, run 3 (R3-fsm-3350, owner decision 545), a fourth deliberate difference, ahead of connectedhomeip: the activation flag moves to *not configured* only through an activation of this delegate, and a clear that succeeded returns it (`thread/otbr/borderrouter.go`, `CommitActiveDataset`, `clear`). chip saves `IsThreadAttached()` at every CommissioningComplete (`src/platform/OpenThread/GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:186-189`, the save `:188`; `ThreadBorderRouterManagementCluster.cpp:319-322`) and reverts on the flag at every fail-safe expiry (`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:191-212`; `ThreadBorderRouterManagementCluster.cpp:301-322`), and after the revert it saves the flag `false` again (`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:208`), so every later expiry (`ThreadBorderRouterManagementCluster.cpp:309`) and every `Init` (`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:62`) attaches the empty dataset again — all at `6170af84`. There the delegate drives the process's own OpenThread instance. Over REST the border router has other writers, so a commit that finds it not attached must not let an unrelated fail-safe expiry disable it and delete a dataset no activation of this node set. What stays chip's: an own activation followed by a CommissioningComplete that finds the border router not attached keeps the flag `false` with no bound in time, and a later, unrelated expiry then clears a dataset this node set and the commissioner completed (`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:188`). At a border router that answers DELETE with 405 the dataset the activation wrote stays in place with the interface disabled, and the flag returns all the same. What ot-br-posix does on the two requests is unverified. Pinned by `thread/otbr:TestRevertTouchesOnlyAnUncommittedActivation`. *Ahead* register row above.

Review II, run 4 (R4-fsm-4302, R4-fsm-4303, under decision 545's row, ahead of connectedhomeip): an activation whose `PUT /node/dataset/active` the border router refuses with a 4xx wrote nothing and takes only that activation off the uncommitted ones; a transport failure, a timeout or a 5xx leaves the revert owed, as chip leaves the flag on every error (`GenericThreadBorderRouterDelegate.cpp:131`, `:136-140` at 6170af84). A clear returns the flag only when no activation started while it ran, and takes off the activations numbered before it began (`thread/otbr/borderrouter.go`). chip has no overlapping activation and revert (one event loop), so the count has no counterpart there. Left as it was (decision 603): a cancelled activation is not waited for, so its PUT can land after the revert's DELETE. Pinned by `thread/otbr:TestRevertTouchesOnlyAnUncommittedActivation` (case (d)), `TestActivationOfUnknownOutcomeKeepsTheRevertOwed`, `TestRefusedActivationKeepsAnEarlierUncommittedOne`, `TestClearKeepsAnActivationThatOverlapsIt` and `TestTwoOverlappingRefusedActivationsLeaveNothingArmed`. Reason: a 4xx is the border router's own answer that nothing was written; any other failure may have written.

Review II, run 5 (R5-fsm-5401, a fix-regression of R4-fsm-4302, owner decision 640): overlapping activations are counted one by one. An activation onto no active dataset is numbered and pending; its own 4xx takes only itself off, a commit (border router attached) or a clear takes off those numbered before it began; the dataset is configured exactly when none is pending (`thread/otbr/borderrouter.go`, `pending`). chip has no counterpart — a request while one is pending answers Busy (`ThreadBorderRouterManagementCluster.cpp:232-235` at `6170af84`, `if (mAsyncCommandHandle.Get()) { return … Status::Busy }`; fix-plan §3, confirmed by fable-diff-h5) — so the module stays ahead. Pinned by `TestTwoOverlappingRefusedActivationsLeaveNothingArmed`.

matter.js's `ThreadNetworkDiagnosticsServer.ts:14` at `862ad75f` is the

### BD-chip-AmbientContextSensing-RulesInServer — detections, hold times and the count rules follow connectedhomeip; the kit mounts it only as a host server

matter.js's `AmbientContextSensingServer.ts:14` at `862ad75f` is the empty
subclass: the generated behaviour derives no detection attribute and
expires nothing, so a sensor would report a detection forever.
`cluster/sensing.AmbientContext` follows connectedhomeip's
`AmbientContextSensingCluster.cpp` at `6170af84`: the constructor and
Startup (:48-89), the writes of ObjectCountConfig and HoldTime (:140-159),
`AddDetection` (:205-301), `SetObjectCountConfig` (:303-367),
`SetObjectCount` (:369-385), `SetHoldTimeLimits` (:438-466), the expiry
timer (:498-509 with :792-842) and `CheckPredictedActivity` (:844-892);
chip's delegate (`AmbientContextSensingDelegate.h:78-106`) becomes the
server's own state and the module's clock, so there is no port. A repeated
detection keeps chip's hold from the first start (:284; owner decision
2026-10-28). SensorFusion is not served: the matter.js model
(`ambient-context-sensing.element.ts:22-29`) has HA, OC, OI, AUD and PRED
only, and schema values come from matter.js verbatim. No device type at
the pin lists the cluster as a server (matter.js has it as a thermostat
client only), so the kit refuses a kit `Declare` for it and a host mounts
`sensing.NewAmbientContext` as `HostServer` (owner decision 2026-10-28).
Pinned by `ambient_chip_test.go` (chip's 15 cases, 14 by meaning) and
`ambient_rules_test.go`.

Review II, close-out C3, three rules as chip (`AmbientContextSensingCluster.cpp`
at `6170af84`): a change of ObjectCountConfig stores the threshold and does
not re-derive the held count or ObjectCountThresholdReached — chip's
`SetObjectCountConfig` stores, notifies and persists and calls nothing that
touches the count; the flag is re-derived only where
`UpdateDetectionAttributes` runs (`SetObjectCount`, `AddDetection`, a limit
change, expiry; `:303-367`, `:636-645`, `:380`) (R2-C2-fsm-1451). At
SimultaneousDetectionLimit `AddDetection` drops the oldest detection first,
with no end event, and only then searches for the same detection, so a
repeat of the oldest is allocated as new and DetectStart is sent again
(`:214-233`, `:236-248`, `:251-267`, `:285-288`) (R2-C2-fsm-1452). A new
AmbientContextTypeSupported list from the host neither filters the held
detections nor re-checks ObjectCountConfig: chip's
`SetAmbientContextTypeSupported` checks the list, copies it and notifies
(`:190-203`) (R2-C2-fsm-1458).

### BD-chip-TlsCertificateManagement-RulesInServer — root and client certificate tables follow connectedhomeip behind the `CertificatePort`; reads serve the full certificate

matter.js's `TlsCertificateManagementServer.ts:14` at `862ad75f` is the
empty subclass. `cluster/tls.CertificateManagement` follows connectedhomeip's
`TLSCertificateManagementCluster.cpp` at `6170af84` (the constructor's
maxima :61-73, the nine handlers :230-575 with chip's status codes and
the fabric-scoped tables) and its example delegate's table rules
(`CertificateTableImpl.cpp`, `IncrementingIdHelper.h`: ids shared across
fabrics, from 0). The keys and the CSR are the host's behind the
`CertificatePort`; the tables persist as one settings record per server.
Two deliberate differences: the reads of ProvisionedRootCertificates and
ProvisionedClientCertificates serve the full certificates, as matter.js's
generated behaviour does (rule 1) — chip's id-only encoding outside a
large-payload transport (:136-166) is not mirrored (owner decision
2026-10-28); and `ClientCSR` publishes a change notification for the new
entry. The consequence over a UDP-sized message: a list entry that does
not fit a report chunk on its own turns the whole attribute into an
AttributeStatusIB(RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) (`bridge/reply.go:497-503`,
`chunkReportData`; the cap is `udp.MaxDatagramSize - 200` = 1848 bytes,
`bridge/reply.go:435`, `transport/udp/listener.go:39`), and a certificate
may be 3000 bytes (`cluster/tls/certificates.go:40`) — the case chip's
id-only encoding avoids (`TLSCertificateManagementCluster.cpp:139-150`,
`:158-169` at `6170af84`: "Drop the certificate payload if transport
doesn't support large payload"). The findings register holds it as
TC-TLSCERT-2.2 / TC-TLSCERT-2.9 (review II, W3-club1-09). The node mounts
both TLS servers on endpoint 0 through
`node.Config.TLS`, as chip serves them on the root endpoint only. Pinned
by `tls/*_chip_test.go` (17 + 16 of chip's cases) and the fuzz target
`FuzzCertificateUpserts` (chip's three `FUZZ_TEST`).

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-conc-1109): a removal that will be refused because the certificate is in use hides the certificate for the length of its dependency check, so a concurrent ProvisionEndpoint naming it answers RootCertificateNotFound / ClientCertificateNotFound once — fail closed, and gone with the check. This module's own; the dependency check runs across the two servers.

### BD-chip-OccupancySensing-HoldTimer — the hold timer is connectedhomeip's; matter.js has none

matter.js's `OccupancySensingServer`
(`packages/node/src/behaviors/occupancy-sensing/OccupancySensingServer.ts`
at `862ad75f`) emits OccupancyChanged with the OccupancyEvent feature
(:67-74) and, for HoldTime, only clears its dependents when it is unset
(:76-85, :93-104): no timer delays the clear of Occupancy. The device
kit's server `cluster/sensing.Occupancy` (phase 36) serves HoldTime as
connectedhomeip's `OccupancySensingCluster.cpp` at `6170af84` does when a
host serves the attribute: the limits are sanitised (`SetHoldTimeLimits`
:333-351), and a configured HoldTime outside them refuses construction
with CONSTRAINT_ERROR as matter.js validates it at initialization
(`DotQualifiedConstraintTest.ts:189`; chip clamps it, :100); a
HoldTime outside them is CONSTRAINT_ERROR (:209-210); the host's
unoccupied starts the timer on the clock's monotonic reading and Occupancy
clears when HoldTime elapses, its occupied cancels the timer (`SetOccupancy`
:277-297, `TimerFired` :299-302); a new HoldTime re-arms a running timer
for the time that remains, or clears at once (:234-258); the deprecated
`*OccupiedToUnoccupiedDelay` attributes read and write HoldTime (:151-155,
:170-181). Two chip rules give way to matter.js: chip forces OCCEVENT on
and always emits OccupancyChanged (`OccupancySensingCluster.h:51-56`,
`.cpp:315-320`), here the event follows the feature as in matter.js;
chip clamps a configured HoldTime, matter.js refuses it; and chip shows the delay aliases by default, here a host serves them when it
opts them in. The surface is no ahead element: HoldTime and its
dependents are model attributes matter.js serves as stored values when an
application sets them. Persistence is the host's through the change
reports and `OccupancyConfig.HoldTime` (chip persists HoldTime,
`.cpp:111-123`, `:265-272`). Tests: `cluster/sensing/occupancy_chip_test.go`
(fifteen of chip's twenty-five cases by meaning, two of them as matter.js
decides them; the rest test chip's delegate, its attribute persistence and
its feature-to-type table, which are the host's or matter.js's here). Reasoning: TC-OCC-2.3 and TC-OCC-3.1
read HoldTime and wait for it; a server that stored HoldTime without the
timer would serve a value that does nothing (owner decision 2026-11-05,
brief phase 36 §1.3).

The camera's signals to the requestor (issue #351) follow the camera app's
provider manager, `examples/camera-app/linux/src/clusters/webrtc-provider/
webrtc-provider-manager.cpp` at `6170af84`: `Provider.Offer`, `Answer`,
`IceCandidates` and `End` are the requestor's commands invoked on the
session's peer node and fabric (`FindOrEstablishSession` on the
ScopedNodeId the request carried, :860-942) at `originatingEndpointId`
(`SendOfferCommand` :1093-1121, `SendAnswerCommand` :1189-1218,

with `TransportPayloadCapability::kLargePayload` and so establishes it over
TCP; this node initiates CASE over UDP only and reuses the newest live
session with the peer of either transport (matter.js `Peer.connect`,
`Peer.ts:439-459`), and a signal larger than one message of that session is
`camera.ErrPayloadTooLarge` (`bridge.ErrPayloadTooLarge` is the same value,
#356) and is not sent — a controller that reached the
camera over TCP leaves the session the signals need. Pinned by
`cluster/camera/provider_peer_test.go` and the two-device
`node/webrtc_provider_peers_test.go` (the signals over CASE to a
`camera.Requestor`, the UDP refusal).

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): connectedhomeip's
`examples/camera-app/linux/src/clusters/webrtc-provider/webrtc-provider-manager.cpp`
is outside the exports the review read and was not re-read; what this entry
says of it is unverified.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-bound-1610, R2-P6-sec-1622; owner decision 150): the Provider bounds sessions by the id space only and stores the session the port returns as it is (Id, PeerNodeId, FabricIndex unchecked); a per-fabric or total bound and the end of a session whose requestor's CASE session closed are the port's, as chip's cluster (`WebRTCTransportProviderCluster.cpp:376-397`, `:803-811`, `:1111` at `6170af84`) leaves them to the camera app's delegate (`webrtc-provider-manager.cpp:39`, `:472-476`). Other than chip, which stores the delegate's session unconditionally (`:811`, `:1111`), a session the schema refuses — one naming no stream ("O.a+") — is not stored and the command answers FAILURE; the port is not told and keeps a session the server does not list.

Review II, run 4 (#590 item 1, owner decisions 606-610, 619-621): the session bounds. The camera app's delegate holds at most `kMaxConcurrentWebRTCSessions` (5) sessions (`webrtc-provider-manager.cpp:39` at `6170af84`) and over it answers ProvideOffer RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (`:472-477`) and SolicitOffer with the session it then ends with OutOfResources (`:281-293`, the End `:990-999`); the cluster server counts nothing, its only bound is the id space (`WebRTCTransportProviderCluster.cpp:371-398`). The kit offers the delegate's bound as `ProviderConfig.MaxSessions` and adds this module's own `ProviderConfig.MaxSessionsPerFabric` (decision 607: one fabric cannot take every session; chip's count is one map across fabrics, `mWebrtcTransportMap`, keyed by session id, `:234`); both count every CurrentSessions entry, the host's included, which is never refused (608), and nothing is evicted (609). Four differences, so the host is not asked for a session it cannot have: the bound is counted by the server before the session id and the port (the camera app counts in its delegate, after the id and the insert, `:281`, `:472`); a refused SolicitOffer's session is not entered in CurrentSessions (chip's cluster stores it, `WebRTCTransportProviderCluster.cpp:811`) and its DeferredOffer is false (the camera app answers its `cameraDeferredOffer` option, `:220`); the End's reason is always OutOfResources (the camera app's is PrivacyMode whenever soft livestream privacy is on, `webrtc-provider-manager.cpp:994-997`, also for a usage the privacy check lets through, `WebRTCTransportProviderCluster.cpp:424`); and the Ends wait in a queue of at most the bound behind one sender — full, or without a PeerConnector, SolicitOffer answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED instead. The End send has no deadline of its own, as the camera app's `SendEndCommand` sets none (`:1327`): the connector's response timeouts bound it, and at worst a send that never returns holds the sender and every later over-bound SolicitOffer answers RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (decision 620). A device built through the facade carries both bounds as `wpdef.Declare.MaxSessions` / `MaxSessionsPerFabric` (decision 619); the reference daemon declares MaxSessions 5 and keeps no count of its own (610). For the bound this replaces the phase-6a paragraph's "a per-fabric or total bound … are the port's"; the end of a lost requestor's sessions is `BD-Matter-Camera-LostRequestorEndsSessions`. Pinned by `cluster/camera/provider_cap_test.go` (`TestProviderSessionBoundParityChip` among them), `device:TestProviderSessionBoundsThroughTheFacade` and `examples/reference-bridge:TestCameraSimWebRTCSessionBound`.

### BD-matterjs-server-CameraStreamManagement — the controller manages a camera's streams and WebRTC sessions, ahead of matter.js

matter.js at `862ad75f` gives the controller side of cameras the
WebRtcTransportRequestor and nothing above it
(`packages/node/src/devices/camera-controller.ts:133` mandates the requestor; `git ls-tree 862ad75f packages | grep -i webrtc`
lists six behaviour files and one test). The stream allocation against a
camera's capacity, the SDP narrowing, the session table a camera calls
back into, the leases and their eviction, the leftover sweep and the
quirks of real cameras are matterjs-server's (`packages/ws-controller/src/camera/CameraStreamManager.ts`,
`streamPolicy.ts`, `videoWindowSearch.ts`, `sdpConstraints.ts`, `codecLevels.ts`,
`snapshotPolicy.ts`, `sessionRegistry.ts`, `webRtcProviderArguments.ts`,
`docs/CAMERA_LIMITATIONS.md:84-` at `0bd06f2`), ported by meaning into
`controller/camera` (phase 37, issue 410): the policies as pure functions
with their tests (`*_parity_matterjsserver_test.go`, the matterjs-server
test register), the `Service` over the controller's own requestor. What the
provider does with the controller's commands is chip's
(`BD-chip-WebRtcTransportProvider-RulesInServer`). The one-identity serving of
the requestor is matter.js behaviour — the controller is a node
(`ControllerBehavior.ts:43-50`, `Peers.ts:109,:549-552,:574-579`) — and carries
no row; ADR 0026's note of 2026-11-05 records it. Reason: a host that
streams from a Matter camera needs these rules once, typed and testable,
not re-derived in every server that maps a WebSocket API; go-fabric-server
maps `camera_*` onto this package (its #40). Reconciliation: when matter.js
grows a camera controller behaviour, its allocation and SDP rules are
compared with these, and the register row closes as caught up.

Review II, phase 1, added bounds of this module's own. matterjs-server at
`0bd06f2` is not among the sources exported at the review's pins, so what
it does in their place was not read (not performable: not exported). A
session's `Signals` hold at most 1024 signals and 1 MiB unread; a camera
that signals past either bound ends the session with `EndSignalOverflow`
and an EndSession, by identity — a newer session that reused the id is
left alone (R2-P1-cam-b-06, R2-P1-dr-rest-05; pinned by
`controller/camera:TestSignalMailboxIsBounded` and
`TestOverflowEndSparesTheSessionThatReusedItsID`). A node removed from the
fabric takes this controller's stream leases along (R2-P1-cam-a-02), and
a start, a raw offer, a snapshot or a stop after the service's `Close` is
refused with `ErrClosed` (R2-P1-cam-b-04).

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): matterjs-server is outside the exports the
review read and was not re-read; what this entry says of it is unverified.

Review II, phase 6b (decision 207): divergences from matterjs-server at `0bd06f22`. A WebRTC session a host opened through the raw route (`Provider.Send`) that the camera stops listing in CurrentSessions without an End leaves the controller's requestor once an earlier report listed it — the rule the registry applies to its own sessions; a report built before the offer does not list it, and a new session under a reused id starts unlisted. matterjs-server applies a report to registry lives only (`packages/ws-controller/src/camera/sessionRegistry.ts:414-432` at `0bd06f22`) and a report takes a requestor entry away only through the registry's `sessionVanished` (`src/controller/MatterController.ts:581-584`), so the entry outlives the camera's session there. connectedhomeip at `6170af84` does no better: a requestor session leaves `mCurrentSessions` on the peer's End (`src/app/clusters/webrtc-transport-requestor-server/WebRTCTransportRequestorCluster.cpp:278-279`) or the controller's establish timeout (`examples/camera-controller/webrtc-manager/WebRTCProviderClient.cpp:399-406`), and `CurrentSessions` occurs in `examples/camera-controller` only at `WebRTCProviderClient.cpp:448` and `:498`, both comments on the requestor's own list (grep over the directory; a read by attribute id without the name would not match). Reason: a kept entry counts as held for the leftover sweep and lets the requestor accept signals for a dead id (R2-P6-store-2203; pinned by `controller/camera:TestReportDropsListedRawSession`).

The give-back chain of a failed or released request and the leftover sweep's EndSession run within the device cleanup budget as their deadline, and `settle` returns once the chain has ended; matterjs-server abandons the chain at the budget and lets it run on, because its invoke takes no abort signal (`packages/ws-controller/src/util/deviceCleanupBudget.ts:24-26`, `src/camera/CameraStreamManager.ts:386-398` at `0bd06f22`). Go's client invoke returns at its context's end (`client/interaction/invoke_batcher.go`, `client/exchange/exchange.go`, `clock/context.go`), so a give-back the camera does not answer is cut; its exchange stops retransmitting once every command of the exchange is abandoned, and what it already sent can still reach the camera after the lock is released — the late-effect window is narrowed to that command, not closed. The cost: a lease a cut give-back left goes with the camera's next report that no longer names the stream only if the camera named it before (a lease the camera never named lives for the process run); a never-named lease whose deallocate then lands lives until a release the camera answers NOT_FOUND — where matterjs-server's abandoned chain would have dropped it at its late answer. matterjs-server's case "lets an abandoned deallocate drop a lease that was only reused since, not allocated again" (`CameraStreamManagerTest.ts:8151` at `0bd06f22`) is a by-design left row of the test register; Go's own case states the cut (R2-P6-conc-2210; pinned by `TestSettleBoundsItsGiveBacks`, `TestSweepEndSessionHasTheBudget`, `TestSliceDDeviceCleanupBudgetParityMatterjsServer` "keeps a lease a cut deallocate left until the camera's report no longer names the stream").

This module's own bounds, with no reference: `Service.Close` ends the requestor entries of its fabric the registry does not track, so no raw-route session outlives the service (R2-P6-fsm-2202); an ended session's unread signals are handed to a reader for `endedSignalsGrace` = 10 s, the device cleanup budget, and then dropped (R2-P6-bound-2206); the camera's uint32 values saturate at the `int` ceiling and the pixel arithmetic is 64-bit, so a 32-bit build computes what a 64-bit one does (R2-P6-bound-2250, -2251).

Review II, run 3, two quirks kept as matterjs-server has them at `0bd06f2`. `satisfiesVideoCallerBounds` checks a reused stream only against the caller's bounds, not its own min ≤ max, as matterjs-server's `satisfiesVideoCallerBounds` (`packages/ws-controller/src/camera/streamPolicy.ts:447-462` at `0bd06f2`); rejecting an inverted reported stream would go beyond the source and is not done (R3-wire-3601, controller half). With a bit-rate ceiling of 0 and no `minBitRate` hint, `bitRatesOf` gives `maxBitRate` 0 and `minBitRate` 1, the same inverted range as matterjs-server: `maxBitRate = Math.max(Math.min(bitRateCeiling ?? …, defaultCap), hints?.minBitRate ?? 0)`, and `bitRateFloor` returns a floor only when `floor <= maxBitRate`, so `minBitRate = … ?? 1` (matterjs-server's `packages/ws-controller/src/camera/streamPolicy.ts:332-334`, `:212-227`, `:226` at `0bd06f2`); the camera's refusal comes back as `IncompatibleError{Reason: bounds}` (R3-wire-3653).

### BD-chip-JointFabricDatastore-RulesInServer — the datastore's tables, refresh and sync follow connectedhomeip behind the `DatastoreSync` port

matter.js's `JointFabricDatastoreServer.ts:14` at `862ad75f` is the empty
subclass. `cluster/jointfabric.Datastore` follows connectedhomeip's
`JointFabricDatastore.cpp` at `6170af84`: the operations and their status
codes (:181-2373), the refresh (:241-1130), the pending/committed state
(`MarkEntryCommittedIfFound`, `.h:75-85`), the capacities (`.h:512-517`)
and the 20 commands the model has at the pin
(`joint-fabric-datastore-server.cpp:293-785`). The pushes to the member
nodes are the host's behind `DatastoreSync` (chip's `Delegate`,
`.h:166-285`), synchronous — chip's two failure points collapse into one,
handled as chip handles the completion; the tables persist as one record
per server (chip keeps them in memory) and every attribute a change
touches is reported (chip reports NodeList only). Two recorded
divergences (owner decision 2026-10-28): the refresh's binding merge
removes only the refreshed endpoint's missing committed bindings, as the
groups' merge does (:397) — chip's predicate (:567-585) also drops the
node's bindings on every other endpoint, which a node with bindings on two
endpoints shows; and a refresh of a node the datastore does not hold ends
cleanly — chip leaves `mRefreshingNodeId` set (:247-249) and refuses every
later refresh. Pinned by `datastore_chip_test.go` (chip's 26 cases) and
`datastore_rules_test.go` (the rules of `TC_JFDS_2_2…2_5`).

The delegate's endpoint-scoped overload `SyncNode(nodeId, endpointId,
bindingEntries)` (`JointFabricDatastore.h:196-203` at `6170af84`) is
`DatastoreSync.SyncEndpointBindings` (phase 39). chip's datastore never
calls that overload — every `SyncNode` it makes carries one entry or a
node's whole list — and its test delegate does not implement it; its
jf-admin-app does, and carries the one binding entry the datastore pushes
as the endpoint's merged list: it fetches the endpoint's current bindings,
removes the entries whose target matches a DeletePending entry's (no list
id travels to the node) or appends the entry, and writes the list to the
endpoint's Binding attribute, an empty list included
(`examples/jf-admin-app/linux/JFADatastoreSync.cpp:1706-1757` at
`6170af84`, the write :1759-1779 and :661-685). The datastore does that
merge for every port, so the host writes a list and reads a list
(`FetchEndpointBindingList`), nothing more — owner decision 2026-11-06,
against the recommendation of an optional interface: a required method,
so every host writes the merged list; chip's delegate has the
single-entry overload (`JointFabricDatastore.h:189-194` at `6170af84`),
the module's datastore merges itself, so the port does not carry it
(decision 8). One divergence: a fetch that fails is the push's error and
leaves the entry Pending or DeletePending for the next `RefreshNode`;
jf-admin-app writes the one entry over an empty list
(`JFADatastoreSync.cpp:1726-1730` at `6170af84`), which drops the node's
other bindings on a transient read failure. The fetch, the merge and the
write run under one lock per node and endpoint, so two pushes to one
endpoint cannot both merge into the list read before the other wrote;
jf-admin-app's fetch-then-write has the same race in principle, two
`SyncNode` calls in flight each fetching before either writes
(`JFADatastoreSync.cpp:1706-1757` at `6170af84`). A push held at the port
therefore holds the later pushes to its endpoint, so the two ports of
chip's deferred-completion cases (`TestRemoveBindingIteratorUseAfterFree`,
`TestAddBindingBackReferenceMarksWrongEntry` in `datastore_chip_test.go`)
run their adds beside the held push, where chip's adds return before the
delegate completes. Pinned by `datastore_endpoint_sync_test.go`.

A binding push and the node's refresh are serialised per node, and a push
whose node list already holds a matching entry writes nothing (review II,
R2-P1-clu-05, R2-P1-dr-rest-04): a push that waited behind a `RefreshNode`
of the same node, which had delivered the Pending entry with the whole
list, would otherwise write the binding a second time. This module's own
rule: jf-admin-app's delegate appends the entry with no test for one already
present (`examples/jf-admin-app/linux/JFADatastoreSync.cpp:1742-1745`, `:1744`
at `6170af84`, read in review II, phase 6a). Pinned by
`cluster/jointfabric:TestBindingPushAfterARefreshThatDeliveredIt`.

Read at `6170af84` (review II, phase 6a, R2-P6-doc-1117 d):
`examples/jf-admin-app/linux/JFADatastoreSync.cpp:1706-1747` (the
single-entry `SyncNode`: fetch, merge, write; a failed fetch clears the
merged list, `:1727`). Lines past `:1750` were not re-read.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-sec-1103, owner decisions 129 and 152): the datastore is the anchor fabric's, ahead of both references — connectedhomeip's cluster asks no accessing fabric (`src/app/clusters/joint-fabric-datastore-server/joint-fabric-datastore-server.cpp` at `6170af84`: no hit for `AccessingFabric|SubjectDescriptor|FabricIndex`), and matter.js's server is the empty subclass (`JointFabricDatastoreServer.ts:14` at `b25ed960`). A command of a request of a fabric other than the recorded anchor fabric answers UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS before it decodes. A read or subscription of such a request is refused by the dispatcher before the server is read — UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS on a concrete path, the attribute left out of a wildcard (`Datastore.MatterReadAllowed`, `BD-Matter-ReadAccessCapability`); behind a dispatcher that does not ask the capability the empty-value read stays the fallback (`MatterReadFiltered`: every attribute but the universal globals withheld, one a later schema adds included). The Datastore admits the universal global attributes (0xFFF8–0xFFFD) to every request, and a successful read of one carries the cluster's DataVersion: a fabric the Datastore refuses still sees that the datastore changed, and when — no content. The anchor is its fabric index and that fabric's identity (root public key, fabric id) in the node's fabric table, which the node hands the datastore (`Datastore.AttachNode`): a request is admitted only when both match, and an UpdateNOC keeps a fabric's root and fabric id, as in matter.js (`packages/protocol/src/fabric/Fabric.ts:579-595`); a reused index with another identity wipes the stale registry when the datastore is attached; a record without the identity (written before this build, or after a host's `SetAnchorFabricIndex` before a table was attached) adopts the table's fabric of that index once — if that index was handed out again while the datastore's endpoint was absent, the new fabric inherits the registry (accepted, review II RECORD-17). While no anchor is recorded every peer is refused: a datastore without an Administrator, or an anchor whose NOC lacks the two CATs, serves peers only after the host's `SetAnchorFabricIndex`; chip serves those. A datastore command during the anchor's fail-safe, before CommissioningComplete, is refused; chip's cases send none (`src/python_testing/TC_JFDS_BindingSync.py:112-114`, `:239-255`; `TC_JFDS_2_2.py:144-146`). Host calls are not fenced. A host that wires the datastore outside the node calls `AttachNode` and forwards every fabric removal and install to it (`MatterDropFabric`); without a fabric table every peer is refused.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-sec-1106, owner decision 129): RefreshNode fetches the node's key sets and takes them into nothing — a held key set's keys and policy are never replaced, an unknown one is not adopted, and the node is enrolled as no recipient (NodeKeySetList is written by the commands alone). connectedhomeip updates the held entry with the node's and appends an unknown one (`src/app/server/JointFabricDatastore.cpp:724-743` at `6170af84`; a null source is cleared, `:119-134`); that a faithful KeySetRead (null keys) would then erase the registry's keys is inferred from this module's own KeySetRead (`cluster/core/group_key_management.go`), not run against chip.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-bound-1113): AddGroup holds GroupList to MaxGroups — tighter than connectedhomeip, whose AddGroup has no capacity test (`src/app/server/JointFabricDatastore.cpp:1360-1385`; its capacity tests are `:183`, `:1159`, `:1227`, `:1684`, `:1930`, `:2122` only, at `6170af84`). RefreshNode refuses a fetched list longer than the per-command cap of that list (memberships and bindings MaxGroups, ACL entries MaxACLs) with ErrNoMemory before anything changes, so no truncated list is pushed; the table's total is not bounded, as chip's merges append without one (`:389`, `:562`, `:959`). After a wipe a push already collected calls no port; the store's last record is a second plaintext copy of the epoch keys in memory until the next save (chip's buffers are self-zeroizing, `JointFabricDatastore.h:532-559`) — recorded, not changed.

Review II, phase 6a (R2-P6-par-1115): UpdateGroup refuses a group whose stored CAT is the Administrator or the Anchor CAT and takes the request's GroupCAT unchecked — mirrored: connectedhomeip `src/app/server/JointFabricDatastore.cpp:1418-1423`, `:1491-1500` at `6170af84` (AddGroup, `:1367`, checks the request's). A group can so be moved onto a reserved CAT, after which it can be neither updated nor removed by command.

Review II, close-out C3 (R2-C2-bound-1101, R2-C2-bound-1102, decision 533):
NodeKeySetList holds at most `MaxGroupKeySet` (256) entries — UpdateGroup and
AddGroupIDToEndpointForNode answer ErrNoMemory before any change — and a
refresh whose node lists more than 256 endpoints ends with ErrNoMemory
before any change, the node staying Pending. Both are this module's own
bounds; whether chip bounds these two lists was not read (unverified).
AddGroup and UpdateGroup accept a GroupKeySetID the datastore does not hold,
with Success, as chip: `groupEntry.groupKeySetID = commandData.groupKeySetID`
is copied without any lookup in `mGroupKeySetList`
(`src/app/server/JointFabricDatastore.cpp:1375`); UpdateGroup's key set
branch (`:1473-1487`) and `AddNodeKeySetEntry` (`:2225-2280`) never consult
it; `IsGroupKeySetEntryPresent` (`:1169-1180`) has no caller on these
paths; chip's tests fix the acceptance
(`src/app/server/tests/TestJointFabricDatastore.cpp:336-339`, `:370-393`) at
`6170af84`. matter.js has no server logic
(`packages/node/src/behaviors/joint-fabric-datastore/JointFabricDatastoreServer.ts:14`
at `b25ed960`). Pinned by `cluster/jointfabric:TestNodeKeySetListIsBounded`
and `TestRefreshEndpointListIsBounded`.

### BD-Matter-ControllerRemainder — the invoke batcher, the discovery sessions, the vendor-info service and the NOC rotation after matter.js, with five Go-shaped edges

Wave 27-A mirrors four matter.js controller behaviours (all at `862ad75f`):
the invoke batcher (`ClientInteraction.ts` `#invokeWithBatching` :744-1005,
`isBatchable` :185-214: one lane per network, CommandRefs per lane, a
faster window restarts the timer, a batch above maxPathsPerInvoke is
split, alone-and-at-once for endpoint 0, timed, suppressed-response,
Large Message and the other `isBatchable` exclusions); the discovery
sessions (`behavior/system/controller/discovery/`: `Discovery.ts:37`,
`InstanceDiscovery.ts:18`, `ContinuousDiscovery.ts:18`,
`ParallelPaseDiscovery.ts:45`, `PaseDiscovery.ts:28`,
`CommissioningDiscovery.ts:23`) as `client/discovery.Session[T]` with
`FindInstance`, `FindAll`, `Race`, `CommissioningRace` and `PASERace`, so
`controller.Pair` races DNS-SD and BLE and the first PASE wins; the
DCL vendor-info service (`DclVendorInfoService.ts:166-468`, wired as
`DclBehavior.ts:101-115` wires it: `controller.Config.DCL`,
`Controller.VendorInfo`); and the NOC rotation (`FabricAuthority.ts:57,
:181-205`, on every controller start as `MatterController.ts:402-415`;
no opt-out, owner decision 2026-10-28). Five Go-shaped edges: the batch
window's Instant is a goroutine yield, not a clock timer, and there is no
interaction-level default lane; the race's transports report as the
progress sub-steps `Discovery.IP` / `Discovery.BLE` (number 2.1, Go
names — an extension of BD-Matter-ControllerProgressAndUpdateEvents);
`VendorInfoService.Observe` is Go-only and `ProductInfo` bitmaps are kept
raw; `FabricAuthority` manages one fabric per store and never rotates a
key an `OperationalSigner` holds; `Discover` reports a device only once it
has an address. PQC phase 1 (`Specification.ts:78-105`, the forward
feature) is implemented on Go 1.27's `crypto/mldsa` and `crypto/x509`
(no dependency; the circl decision of 2026-10-28 is superseded) and stays
off behind `internal/forward`, as matter.js keeps it off until a released
revision carries it (owner decision 2026-10-28); device-side PQC (NOC,
ICAC, CASE) stays out, as matter.js admits ML-DSA only in the attestation
certificates. Pinned by the `*_parity_matterjs_test.go` ports listed in
`notes/briefs/reports/27A.md` (test register, planned ratchet 3).

### BD-chip-TimeSynchronization-Features — TZ, NTPC, NTPS and TSC follow connectedhomeip when the host selects them; the node's UTC is an offset over its clock, with chip's time client

matter.js's `TimeSynchronizationServer.ts:14` at `862ad75f` is the empty
subclass. `core.NewTimeSynchronizationWith` (`node.Config.TimeSynchronization`)
follows connectedhomeip's `TimeSynchronizationCluster.cpp` at `6170af84`:
the attribute gating (:186-248), the feature logic (:619-1028), the four
handlers with their statuses and events (`HandleSetTrustedTimeSource`
:1138-1157, `HandleSetTimeZone` :1161-1213, `HandleSetDSTOffset`
:1216-1243, `HandleSetDefaultNTP` :1246-1275), LocalTime, fabric removal
and persistence through `store.Settings` (chip's `TimeSyncDataProvider.h:58-75`).
The features are off by default and `FeatureMap` is the host's selection.
Two edges: a SetTimeZone list over two entries answers CONSTRAINT_ERROR
from the request constraint before chip's RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED check
(:1168-1171) can; an IPv4 NTP address counts as a domain, as in chip's
default delegate; no DSTTableEmpty at startup, since the emitter attaches
after construction.

The node's UTC is a served source (owner decision 2026-11-06, phase 39,
replacing the decision of 2026-10-28 that SetUTCTime answers chip's
statuses without setting the clock): every server, with or without
features, serves UTCTime as its clock plus an offset, with Granularity and
the optional TimeSource. Until something sets the offset the host clock is
the platform source — chip's `DefaultTimeSyncDelegate.cpp:42-58`,
MillisecondsGranularity and MixedNTP while the clock is past the Matter
epoch, or the host's `TimeSynchronizationConfig.PlatformTime` (chip's
`UpdateTimeFromPlatformSource`). UTCTime is null without a granularity
(:255-267). `SetUTCTime` sets the offset with chip's checks
(`HandleSetUTCTime` :1110-1136, `SetUTCTime` :856-872, `UpdateUTCTime`
:74-86): INVALID_COMMAND outside the enums; TimeNotAccepted for
NoTimeGranularity, a granularity coarser than the current one while the
node has a time, or seconds past 32 bits; TimeSource Admin. The time client
is ported: `Start` (the node's server-ready, `OnPlatformEventFn` :556-569)
and a trusted time source set while the node has no time (:584-587) run
`AttemptToGetTime` (:541-554) — the trusted node's root UTCTime and
Granularity read through `core.TimePeerReader` (:401-460, :525-539; the
node's reader runs over its client stack, `node.Config.Client`), adopted
with chip's conservative granularity and TimeSource NodeTimeCluster
(:462-492); else the NTP fallback through the host's `core.NTPClient`
asking DefaultNTP, adopted with milliseconds and NonMatterSNTP (:510-518);
else TimeFailure (:379-398, :519-522). Differences, each because the host
clock is never set: the offset lives in memory and a restart serves the
host clock again (chip's system clock keeps the time); the platform source
is read live, not once at server ready; Last Known Good Time is not
updated (`UpdateUTCTime` :82; the module keeps none); an NTP answer
before the Matter epoch or past 32-bit seconds is a failed query; each
read and NTP query ends after `core.TimeSyncAttemptTimeout` (30 s) on the
server's clock, a bound of the module's because the ports are a host's
and an attempt that never ended would hold every later one. The node's UTC
is the Matter time of Thermostat TSUGGEST and Valve TS (issue 428): the node hands
`TimeSynchronization.MatterEpochSeconds` to the Thermostat's suggestions
and the Valve's AutoCloseTime as their endpoints join the topology
(`AttachMatterTime`) and tells them whenever it adopts a time
(`MatterTimeChanged`: SetUTCTime, the trusted time source, the NTP
fallback; a move of the host clock or of `PlatformTime` tells nobody), as
chip's SetUTCTime calls `UTCTimeAvailabilityChanged` for SetUTCTime
(`TimeSynchronizationCluster.cpp:1129`) and the trusted source's time
(`:479`) — chip's NTP fallback (`:510-522`) makes no such call, the node
tells of that adoption too because it moves the time the participants
read —, and as chip's servers read the system clock
SetUTCTime sets through `GetClock_MatterEpochS`
(`src/system/SystemClock.cpp:284-306` at `6170af84`; the delegate call is
`TimeSynchronizationCluster.cpp:865`). Since issue 445 every device-side
reader of real time reads the node's UTC, as chip's read the one system
clock: the participants — Thermostat TSUGGEST, Valve TS, ResourceMonitoring's
LastChangedTime (`cluster/filter`, chip `ResourceMonitoringCluster.cpp:379`,
`GetClock_RealTimeMS`), DeviceEnergyManagement's forecast and pause times
(`DeviceEnergyManagementCluster.cpp:449`, `:698`), CommodityTariff's
current day and period (`commodity-tariff-server.cpp:928`) and EnergyEVSE's
targets and session times — through `AttachMatterTime`; of these only the
Valve re-evaluates on `MatterTimeChanged` (the others read the time per
command or timer, as chip's) and only the Valve requires the time (chip's
Startup refuses it, `ValveConfigurationAndControlCluster.cpp:46-50`); and
the root's readers through `SetUTCClock(TimeSynchronization.UTC)` — the
event log's EpochTimestamp (`im.EventLog`, chip `EventManagement.cpp:433-439`,
which stamps a system time when the UTC is null; the Go record has no
system-time form and takes the host clock then), GeneralDiagnostics'
TimeSnapshot and DiagnosticLogs' UTCTimeStamp (omitted while the UTC is
null). While the node's time is null a participant does what its chip line
does on GetClock_MatterEpochS's error (DEM fails the request, EVSE skips the
stamp and re-checks in 30 s, the tariff refuses); only a server outside a
node reads its own clock (`clock.MatterTimeOf`),
and the duplicated Matter-epoch offsets of the readers are gone onto it.
TimeSource and
TimeZoneDatabase go out as plain integers; a named enum type went out as
TLV null through the bridge's reply writer. Pinned by `cluster/core`
time-synchronization tests (3 chip cases, 9 rules, 6 client cases, 1 wire,
1 epoch-seconds case), `node`'s client wire test, its
`TestOneMatterTimePerNode` and `TestRootReadersFollowTheNodesUTC`,
`cluster/filter:TestMatterNow` and `cluster/energy:TestNodeTime`.

### BD-chip-GeneralCommissioning-TermsAndConditions — the TC feature follows connectedhomeip when the node states its terms

matter.js's `GeneralCommissioningServer.ts:31` at `862ad75f` is the class
line of a 285-line server without terms-and-conditions text.
`core.GeneralCommissioningConfig.TermsAndConditions`
(`node.Commissioning.TermsAndConditions`, the host's requirement: the
version, the acknowledgement bits, the optional deadline) serves the TC
feature as connectedhomeip's `GeneralCommissioningCluster.cpp` at
`6170af84` serves it under `CHIP_CONFIG_TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS_REQUIRED`:
`SetTCAcknowledgements` judges the version (TCMinVersionNotMet) and the
bits (RequiredTCNotAccepted) against the requirement (:617-650) and
records a changed acceptance tentatively while the fail-safe is armed,
committed at once otherwise (:663-672); `CommissioningComplete` refuses
without an acceptance (TCAcknowledgementsNotReceived), below the version
or short of a bit (:476-510), then commits the tentative one (:512-525);
an expired or disarmed fail-safe reverts the acceptance its window set
(:149-157); the last fabric's removal resets it (:357-374), a factory
reset erases the store it lives in (`store.SettingTermsAcceptance`);
TCAcknowledgementsRequired is whether the acceptance in force satisfies
the requirement (`DefaultTermsAndConditionsProvider.cpp:192-217`),
TCUpdateDeadline the configured deadline or null (`GeneralCommissioningCluster.cpp:221-231`). Two
differences to chip: the requirement is configuration, never absent
while the feature is on (chip's provider may hold none, :199-202); and
the gate runs after the fail-safe's fabric check rather than before the
session-type check (:530), so a mismatched fabric answers
InvalidAuthentication before the terms are judged — matter.js's order of
the checks it has. Pinned by `cluster/core/general_commissioning_tc_chip_test.go`
(TC-CGEN-2.5 to 2.11 by meaning) and the CGEN family against the daemon
with `--tc-required`. Served behind `surface.Policies.Extensions`
(surface `yes`). The commissioner side goes with it: matter.js's flow has
no terms step (`ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:558-567` at `862ad75f`
runs ConfigureRegulatoryInformation, then SynchronizeTime);
`commissioner.Options.TermsAndConditions` adds chip's
kConfigureTCAcknowledgments stage as step 8.3 (`AutoCommissioner.cpp:485-487`,
`CHIPDeviceController.cpp:3946-3970` at `6170af84`: SetTCAcknowledgements
after the regulatory configuration, skipped without the acknowledgement).

### BD-chip-Concentration-ProjectedSelection — the projection serves the host's concentration selection; values it cannot refuse are held or read Unknown

matter.js has no logic for the concentration clusters or AirQuality
(`AirQualityServer.ts:14` and the ten `*ConcentrationMeasurementServer.ts`
at `862ad75f` are empty subclasses). The measurement projection serves the
selection a host states through `contract.ConcentrationSelection`
(LevelIndication with MediumLevel and CriticalLevel, PeakMeasurement and
AverageMeasurement with their windows, the AirQuality grades), the readings
coming from `contract.ConcentrationReadings`, as connectedhomeip serves the
values the application sets. The closure follows connectedhomeip
(`ConcentrationMeasurementCluster.cpp:77-89` at `6170af84`: MED and CRI
imply LEV). Three differences, because a projected read has no caller to
refuse: a peak or average outside the measured range is held to it, and a
window beyond one week to the week, where chip's setters answer
CONSTRAINT_ERROR (`:170-176`, `:198`); a level the selection does not serve
(Medium without MED, Critical without CRI) reads Unknown, where chip's
`SetLevelValue` refuses it (`:213-225`). AirQuality grades on published
scales — CO2 on the Umweltbundesamt's 1000 / 2000 ppm bounds, PM2.5 and
PM10 on the WHO 2021 guideline and interim targets — and folds a grade the
selection leaves out towards Poor; the specification leaves the mapping to
the manufacturer. Pinned by `cluster/measurement:TestConcentrationSelection*`,
`TestAirQualityGrades` and `TestParityMatterJS_FeatureGatedAttributesMatchFeatureMap`.

### BD-Matter-CompositeDeviceTypesAsParts — VideoDoorbell and FloodlightCamera compose their components as parts; no superset on the composite's own endpoint

matter.js counts a simple component of a composite only on an endpoint
below the composite: `DeviceTypeConformance.ts` `candidatesOf` (:586-599)
counts the composing endpoint itself only for a utility device type it
lists (`listsUtility`, :601-613), every other candidate comes from the
composition scope — the endpoint's children, never the endpoint itself
(`ResolvedEndpoint.ts:216-243`) — and the device type id must match
exactly (:591-592 at `b25ed960`). OnOffLight, Camera and Doorbell are simple, so
`device.NewVideoDoorbell` and `NewFloodlightCamera` (devicegen, wave 27-B)
add the components as parts, the kit's one-device-type-per-endpoint rule
stays, and a superset type on the composite's own endpoint is not offered
(owner decision 2026-10-28, after the citation: matter.js does not count
it). ADR 0018's addendum records the shape.

### BD-Matter-CameraPersistenceIsTheHosts — Chime and the camera settings persist through the host, not a store record

connectedhomeip persists Chime's SelectedChime and Enabled through its
attribute persistence (`ChimeCluster.cpp:83-104`, `:221-223`, `:233-235` at
`6170af84`, `LoadPersistentAttributes`) and the camera's MPTZPosition,
MPTZPresets and DPTZStreams (`CameraAvSettingsUserLevelManagementLogic.cpp:139-332`,
`StoreMPTZPosition` …); matter.js's servers for both are the empty
subclasses and persist nothing of their own. `cluster/camera` reports every
change through the server's change notification and takes the restored
values from the declaration's `Initial`; no `store.Port` record is added
(owner decision Q5 of brief 26-A1, kept at report 26-A2 and the milestone-6
sweep): persistence is the host's, as every other host-owned value of the
device model, so a host that does not persist them starts at chip's
defaults after a restart. Moved here from the findings register at the
triage of 2026-10-29.

### BD-chip-CameraApp-Simulation — the reference daemon's `--camera-sim` follows connectedhomeip's camera-app managers without a media stack

matter.js has no camera test device (`support/chip-testing/src/devices/all-devices.ts` at
`862ad75f` lists none). The reference daemon's `--camera-sim`
(`examples/reference-bridge/camera.go`, phase 34) follows connectedhomeip's
camera-app at `6170af84`: the HAL's capabilities and features
(`camera-device.h:41-88`, `camera-device.cpp:1491-1640`,
`camera-app.cpp:43-283`), the available streams and their compatibility
(`InitializeVideoStreams`, `InitializeAudioStreams`, `AddSnapshotStream`,
`camera-device-interface.h:51-97`), the managers' allocation statuses
(`camera-av-stream-manager.cpp:347-677`), the provider's session
(`webrtc-provider-manager.cpp` `HandleSolicitOffer`, deferred with
`--camera-deferred-offer`), the zone manager's trigger timing
(`zone-manager.cpp:169-289`) and the chime's sounds (`chime-manager.h:41-45`).
Deliberate differences: nothing is captured or sent — ProvideOffer keeps the
session but sends no Answer, a push transport uploads nothing and is never
busy, its recording only the PushTransportBegin and PushTransportEnd of the
camera-app's transport lifecycle (a continuous transport while Active, a
triggered one for its InitialDuration), CaptureSnapshot returns a generated JPEG under `--camera-test-videosrc`
and fails without it (the camera-app's `/dev/video0` capture); the camera and
the chime are bridged devices, the chime one of its own (the Camera device
type lists no Chime); with PERZONESENS the zone management serves no
Sensitivity ("!PERZONESENS"), where the camera-app sets one that is not
served either; the AvAnalysis app-pipe commands are logged and dropped (no
AvAnalysis cluster in the snapshot); a triggered zone stops when its
TriggerDetectedDuration has elapsed, where the camera-app's one-second timer
stops it a second later (`zone-manager.cpp:197`) — at the very end of the
window TC-ZONEMGMT-2.4 allows (`TC_ZONEMGMT_2_4.py:279-285`). TESTING ONLY, off by default; the
stream, PTZ and chime state is kept in `--db` as
`BD-Matter-CameraPersistenceIsTheHosts` leaves it to the host.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): connectedhomeip's camera-app
(`examples/camera-app`) is outside the exports the review read and was not
re-read; what this entry says of it is unverified.

### BD-Matter-BTP-RenegotiationAfterStall — a BTP central that stalls after the handshake is re-established once at the minimum segment size, as matter.js's channel does

matter.js's `BtpSessionHandler` reports a central session above the minimum
segment size whose peer completed the handshake and then sent no BTP packet
before the acknowledgement timeout, although it was sent Matter data
(`stalledAfterHandshake`, `packages/protocol/src/ble/BtpSessionHandler.ts:67-84`
at `862ad75f`), and its own comment calls the remedy "an interop workaround
with no basis in the specification": "Some peripherals were observed to
behave this way with large segments on Bluetooth 4.1 adapters and to work
with the minimum segment size; the cause is not established." Its central
channel acts on the report (`packages/nodejs-ble/src/NobleBleChannel.ts:835`,
`:864-889` `#startRenegotiation` — at most once per channel, every send
awaits it, a failure closes the channel unless the channel is closing;
`:891-918` `#renegotiate` — the C2 handler detached, C2 unsubscribed, a new
handshake with `MINIMUM_ATT_MTU`, the session adopted, the unacknowledged
messages replayed in order; `:920-926` the channel lost meanwhile ends it).
connectedhomeip closes the endpoint when its acknowledgement timer fires
(`src/ble/BLEEndPoint.cpp:1454-1464` at `6170af84`,
`HandleAckReceivedTimeout`: "ack recv timeout, closing ep",
`DoClose(kBleCloseFlag_AbortTransmission, BLE_ERROR_FRAGMENT_ACK_TIMED_OUT)`).
Here `controller/ble.Channel` mirrors matter.js (phase 39): the session
half (`transport/btp.Session.OnStall`, `Suspend`) reports the stall, the
channel swaps the session behind its `btp.Conn` (`Channel.Conn` is the
current one), `Channel.Send` waits for a renegotiation in flight and
answers `ErrChannelClosed` when the channel is lost meanwhile, a failed
renegotiation or a lost connection closes the channel, each C2 unsubscribe
runs under `ble.DisconnectTimeout` (5 s, `BLE_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`,
`NobleBleChannel.ts:38`, `:579`) and each handshake's C1 write and C2
subscribe under its `btp.ConnRspTimeout` attempt (`:602-606`, `:634-641`),
both on the channel's clock, so a peripheral that vanished without a
disconnect event fails the renegotiation within the bound and the channel
closes, and `Dial` waits up
to `ATTMTUSettleTimeout` (2 s, `NobleBleChannel.ts:40-41`, `:526-567` at
`862ad75f`) for a connection that reports its ATT_MTU exchange
(`ble.MTUExchange`) before it sizes the segment. The workaround is adopted
as matter.js's production-hardened behaviour (the order of authority:
matter.js decides where it models something), and recorded here because
the specification neither describes nor forbids it and connectedhomeip does
not do it. One Go-side difference: the cleanup unsubscribe after a
handshake timeout runs on a context that outlives the caller's and `Dial`
reports `ErrHandshakeTimeout`, where matter.js raises its `AbortedError`
when the abort lands during that unsubscribe
(`packages/nodejs-ble/test/NobleBleChannelTest.ts:1075-1097` at `862ad75f`);
the register leaves that case. Supersedes `BD-Matter-BTP-NoStallRenegotiation`
(report 27-C, 2026-10-29), which recorded the absence. Proof:
`controller/ble/channel_parity_matterjs_test.go` over the `bletest`
peripheral's `Stall` and `Faults`; no chip-tool leg exists (no BTP family).

### BD-Matter-BLEPeripheralOverBlueZ — the BLE peripheral on Linux speaks BlueZ's D-Bus API after connectedhomeip, where matter.js drives the controller through bleno

matter.js's peripheral is `BlenoBleServer` on bleno
(`packages/nodejs-ble/src/BlenoBleServer.ts` at `db021da0`): raw HCI through
a native binding, the advertising payload handed over as EIR bytes (`:384`),
the GATT service set once advertising started (`:224-231`). `ble/bluez`
reaches the same controller through bluetoothd, as connectedhomeip's Linux
platform does (`src/platform/Linux/bluez/BluezEndpoint.cpp:448-534`,
`BluezAdvertisement.cpp:43-101`, `BluezConnection.cpp:172-238` at `6170af84`):
a GATT application with C1 through `AcquireWrite` and C2 through
`AcquireNotify`, and an `LEAdvertisement1` object. Six things follow from
the platform. (1) BlueZ composes the advertisement from properties: the
service data is taken out of the payload matter.js would hand bleno, the
flags are BlueZ's, and the local name is connectedhomeip's
`MATTER-<discriminator>` (`BLEManagerImpl.cpp:377`) where matter.js sends
none. (2) A refused C1 write or C2 subscription is logged and not answered
with an ATT error (`BlenoBleServer.ts:51-57`): bluetoothd has answered the
central before the socket delivers the write. (3) A central counts from its
first use of the Matter service, where connectedhomeip counts every device
that connects to the adapter (`BluezEndpoint.cpp:296-350`), so another use
of the adapter does not take the node's one slot. (4) The end of the C2
subscription is the end of the notify socket; it is reported and closes the
session as in matter.js (`BlenoBleServer.ts:81-84`), where connectedhomeip
does not report it on this path at the pin (`BLEManagerImpl.cpp:699-712`).
(5) A C2 subscription that arrives before the first C1 write was read is
held until it was: the two travel on different sockets, so their order of
arrival is the platform's, not the central's, and matter.js's refusal of a
subscription before the handshake request (`BlenoBleServer.ts:288-291`)
would refuse a correct central. (6) Where bluetoothd reports an
indication's confirmation through C2's `Confirm` call, the call names no
device: connectedhomeip completes the connection of the device seen last
(`BluezEndpoint.cpp:207-217`), the peripheral the live connection that
waits for one, so a refused second central cannot take the first one's
confirmations (`TestPeripheralConfirmAfterRefusedCentral`). Everything above the platform is
matter.js's and shared by every platform — the handshake held until the
subscription, the 15 s timer, the single session, the advertisement's
schedule, BLE only without a fabric (`transport/btp/accept.go`,
`bridge/ble.go`, `node/commissioning.go`); the single connection, bleno's
limit in matter.js (`BlenoBleServer.ts:130-133`), is the bridge's rule
here: a second central is disconnected. Reasoning: bleno needs a native
build and takes the HCI device away from bluetoothd; this module is pure Go
and shares the adapter (ADR 0031, decision 5). Pinned by
`TestPeripheralAdvertisement`, `TestPeripheralConnectionEvents` and
`TestPeripheralServesBTP` (`ble/bluez/peripheral_linux_test.go`) over an
in-process bluetoothd, and `TestBLEOneCentralAtATime` (`bridge/ble_test.go`).

One further point since wave 28c: after a successful `AcquireWrite` or
`AcquireNotify` the characteristic reports `WriteAcquired` /
`NotifyAcquired` true before the call completes, as connectedhomeip does
(`src/platform/Linux/bluez/BluezEndpoint.cpp:129`, `:186` at `6170af84`),
so a GATT server that decides by the property writes into the socket it
holds instead of acquiring one per write. connectedhomeip never sets the
properties back; here each follows whether any connection still holds that
socket and returns to false when the last one ends, state and signal
changed under one lock. Reasoning: the peripheral serves one central after
another for the life of the process, and a property left true would tell
the platform that the next central's socket already exists. Pinned by
`TestPeripheralAcquiredFlags`, `TestPeripheralAcquiredFlagsAcrossCentrals`,
`TestPeripheralAcquiredFlagsWhenTheLinkDrops` and
`TestPeripheralAcquiredSignalsInOrder`
(`ble/bluez/peripheral_linux_test.go`).

Review II, run 3 (R3-fsm-3301, owner decisions 555, 574): the peripheral follows its adapter object. On `InterfacesRemoved` of the adapter it marks its advertisement unregistered; on `InterfacesAdded` it unregisters what it believes held (errors ignored, since a bluetoothd that ended without `InterfacesRemoved` cannot be told from one that did), registers the GATT application, then the advertisement, and retries with a pause doubling from 1 s to 30 s until they hold (`ble/bluez/peripheral_linux.go`, `followAdapter`). Both references follow the adapter: chip shuts the advertisement and the endpoint down and clears `kAppRegistered` / `kAdvertisingConfigured` when the adapter is removed and calls `DriveBLEState()` when it is added (`src/platform/Linux/BLEManagerImpl.cpp:434-469`, `BluezObjectManager.cpp:196-232` at `6170af84`); matter.js follows Bleno's adapter state (`stateChange`, `poweredOn`; `packages/nodejs-ble/src/BlenoBleServer.ts:170-185` at `b25ed960`). `Adapter1.Powered` is not followed, by measurement (bluetoothd probe of decision 574, issue #610 row 1: BlueZ 5.72, the probe script `bluetoothd-probe.sh` of branch `phase8/l0-probe` at `243b1e3ec`, not on `main`, CI run 45459009820). `Powered` going false and true again — set over D-Bus or with `hciconfig down` / `up` — sends `PropertiesChanged` on `Adapter1` and nothing else: no `InterfacesRemoved`, no `Release`; `ActiveInstances` stays 1 while `Powered` is false, and registering both again from the same bus name is refused with `org.bluez.Error.AlreadyExists`. bluetoothd stopping (`systemctl stop`) and the controller leaving both take the application and the advertisement: after the return `ActiveInstances` is 0 and both registrations are accepted again. In both, bluetoothd calls `Release` on the advertisement, after the `InterfacesRemoved` of `LEAdvertisingManager1` and before that of `Adapter1`, and makes no call to the GATT application.
