A registering process whose bus name leaves loses both without a signal to anyone but `ActiveInstances`. Not measured: a bluetoothd that is killed, any BlueZ but 5.72, whether the radio advertises again once `Powered` is back, and whether a central is still served after any of these. Pinned by `ble/bluez:TestPeripheralFollowsTheAdapter` and the six further tests of `peripheral_adapter_linux_test.go`.

Review II, run 4 (R4-fsm-4301, a fix-regression of R3-fsm-3301, owner decision 589): the order application, then advertisement, holds for every adapter signal, also one that names only `GattManager1` or only `LEAdvertisingManager1` and arrives before an earlier signal's work finished: what a signal owes stays owed until it is done, and no advertisement is registered while the application is missing (`ble/bluez/peripheral_linux.go`). chip acts on the object that carries `Adapter1` only (`src/platform/Linux/bluez/BluezObjectManager.cpp:195-212`, `:224-232` at `6170af84`); the per-manager branch is the module's own. bluetoothd 5.72 sends such signals (probe of decision 574, CI run 45459009820): every adapter came with `LEAdvertisingManager1` alone in a second `InterfacesAdded`, 0.13 to 3.7 ms after the one that carries `Adapter1` and `GattManager1` (six of six), and the adapter that held registrations left in steps — `GattManager1` with `NetworkServer1`, then `LEAdvertisingManager1` alone, then `Adapter1` (two of two). `GattManager1` was never named alone. Pinned by `TestPeripheralAdvertisingOnlySignalKeepsTheApplicationOwed`, `TestPeripheralGattOnlySignalKeepsTheAdvertisementOwed` and `TestPeripheralAdvertisingOnlySignalDuringTheRetry`.

Review II, run 5 (R5-fsm-5502, a fix-regression of R4-fsm-4301 and the second of the R3-fsm-3301 line, owner decision 639): a signal naming `GattManager1` that arrives while an earlier `RegisterApplication` is still in flight keeps the application owed — `appLost` is settled only for the adapter generation the work started under (`ble/bluez/peripheral_linux.go`, `restoreApplication`). The module's own mechanism; no reference was read for it. The probe of decision 574 did not show this trigger: with BlueZ 5.72 `GattManager1` arrived only in the `InterfacesAdded` that carries `Adapter1` (six of six); the signal that does arrive while `RegisterApplication` is in flight names `LEAdvertisingManager1`. The guard stays for a bluetoothd that orders them differently. Pinned by `TestPeripheralGattSignalDuringRegisterApplication`; the run-4 tests above stay green.

Review II close-out, phase 8 (#610 rows 1–5, decision 678): the peripheral follows each manager on its own. On an addition, the application is owed on `GattManager1` and the advertisement on `LEAdvertisingManager1`; `Adapter1` counts for both only on a removal. While a side's manager is absent the peripheral registers nothing again on its own, and a `Release` retry stops then (a host `Advertise` or `RegisterService` still calls BlueZ and returns its error). `appLost` is settled against an application generation that only `GattManager1`/`Adapter1` signals move, so the advertising manager's own `InterfacesAdded` during `RegisterApplication` no longer causes a second registration. `RegisterService`, a registration's end and the work that follows the adapter are serialised by `advMu`, which callers with a context take with that context; `Close` and the end of `Serve` wait for it at most `peripheralTimeout` and then unregister without it. `Powered` is observed for the log only (Warn off, Info on) and never written (`BD-Matter-BLEPeripheral-PoweredNotWritten` below). Pinned by the `*W2B1` tests of `ble/bluez/peripheral_linux_w2b1_test.go`; the run-3/4/5 tests stay green.

### BD-Matter-BLEPeripheral-PoweredNotWritten — the BLE peripheral on Linux neither writes nor follows `Adapter1.Powered`

The peripheral never writes `Adapter1.Powered` and keeps its registrations across a `Powered` edge; it logs the edge — Warn when the adapter goes off, Info when it returns (`ble/bluez/peripheral_linux.go`, `poweredChanged`; decision 678). chip sets `Powered` each time it takes the adapter (`SetupAdapter`, `src/platform/Linux/bluez/BluezObjectManager.cpp:133-136`, called from `GetAdapter` `:93`; `DriveBLEState` takes the adapter there, `src/platform/Linux/BLEManagerImpl.cpp:745`, again after an adapter-added `:440`) and reads no later change of it — its adapter properties handler reads `Class` only (`BluezObjectManager.cpp:244-257`), lines at `6170af84`. matter.js, on a Bleno state other than `poweredOn`, calls `Bleno.stopAdvertising()` (`packages/nodejs-ble/src/BlenoBleServer.ts:174-178` at `b25ed960`) and on `poweredOn` starts the advertisement again (`:178-184`); it does not switch the adapter. This module does neither on `Powered`, because BlueZ 5.72 keeps the registration (measured, probe of decision 574, CI run 45459009820); whether the radio advertises again once `Powered` is back is unmeasured. Review II, issue #610 row 1, owner decision 678. Pinned by `ble/bluez:TestPeripheralLogsPoweredEdgesW2B1`. Reason: the adapter's power is the host's policy, not the module's, and a registration repeated once `Powered` is back is refused with `AlreadyExists` (BlueZ 5.72, measured; one issued while `Powered` is false is unmeasured).

### BD-Matter-GeneratedServerSuffices — clusters whose generated server is complete: no source carries behaviour beyond the model

Audit of 2026-10-27 (owner question at the milestone 6 concept; read map
`read-generated-clusters-chip-rules.md`, connectedhomeip at the harness
commit `6170af84`, matter.js at `862ad75f`): for every cluster this module
serves, chip's server was checked for command handlers and validation
beyond the data model. Every cluster where chip carries such rules already
has a hand-written server here (`cluster/core`, `energy`, `media`,
`appliance`, `closure`, `fan`, `pump`, `valve`, `filter`, `thermo` and the
measurement projections; the `BD-chip-*` entries above record each rule
set), or is a milestone 6 wave (concept v10). What remains generated is
complete by the model alone — no `*Server.ts` logic at the pin (the empty
subclass: 14 lines, 18 or 19 for the ten concentration servers and
`ElectricalPowerMeasurementServer.ts` at `b25ed960`), no chip handler, no chip status beyond UnsupportedAttribute /
UnsupportedCommand: **WaterTankLevelMonitoring** (0x0079; chip has no server
at all — `src/app/clusters/water-tank-level-monitoring-server` is absent at
`6170af84` — and matter.js's `WaterTankLevelMonitoringServer.ts:14` is the
empty subclass; brief 26-C), **MeterIdentification** (0x0B06), **ElectricalGridConditions**
(0x00A0; one `Status::Failure` when the CurrentConditionsChanged event
cannot be logged, `electrical-grid-conditions-server.cpp:160`), **FixedLabel**, and the
attribute-only measurement clusters (Temperature, RelativeHumidity,
Illuminance, Pressure, Flow, the ten concentration
measurements, ElectricalPowerMeasurement, SoilMeasurement — their host
projections in `cluster/measurement` add the materialisers, not rules).
BooleanState, which this list named, is not one of them at `b25ed960`:
`BooleanStateServer.ts:19-28` emits StateChange on a change of StateValue
under the ChangeEvent feature, and `measurement.HeldBooleanState` is the
port of that (`cluster/measurement/booleanstate_held.go:26-63`). matter.js
turns that feature on by default (`BooleanStateServer.ts:11-13`), and so does
the device kit when a host's declarations select no BooleanState feature
(`serverEnabledFeatures`, `device/device.go:546-554`; review II, phase 4;
pinned by `device:TestClusterBehaviorFeaturesParityMatterJS`).
Reasoning: the generated server enforces the model's constraints and
conformance (ADR 0017); a rule that no reference implementation has is not
a gap. Two findings came out of the same audit and are register entries,
not divergences: TimeSynchronization's optional features (milestone 6 wave
27-B) and AirQuality's feature-gated values. Re-read at every pin lift
together with the Ahead-of-matter.js markers: a `*Server.ts` of one of
these clusters growing past the shell reopens the question.

### BD-Matter-NoConfiguredCATs — the client stack keeps no configured CATs for a peer; matter.js keeps its ignored option

Since the db021da0 lift a CASE session's CATs are the peer's NOC's on both
sides of the handshake (wave P1, #435), and matter.js documents its own
`PairOptions.caseAuthenticatedTags` as "Not applied yet; the option is
ignored" (`packages/protocol/src/session/case/CaseClient.ts:396-404` at
`db021da0`) while `PeerSet.addKnownPeer` still replaces a known peer's
descriptor CATs (`packages/protocol/src/peer/PeerSet.ts:321-323`). This
module removes the field instead (owner decision 2026-11-06 on #433):
`peer.Descriptor.CaseAuthenticatedTags`, `client.CommissionOptions` and
`client.Record`'s set are gone, a stored record's field 1 is read and
ignored and dropped by the next save — a facade option that does nothing
is no option. Proof: `controller/client:TestRecordIgnoresRetiredCATs`; the
`client/peer` merge row "CATs replace" (`PeerSet.ts:321-323`) is dropped
from `client/peer:TestParityKnownPeerMerge`'s table.

### BD-Matter-VIDStatementVerification — the VID Verification Statement path fails closed where matter.js's is open

matter.js `VendorIdVerification.verifyData` (`packages/node/src/behaviors/operational-credentials/VendorIdVerification.ts:230-293`
at `b25ed960`) decodes a VVSC and checks its profile (`Vvsc.ts:25-30`,
`:45-80`), compares its SubjectKeyID with the statement's signer and checks
the statement signature; but it accepts a statement without a VVSC
("TODO Fail if not available!", `:263-271`), leaves the path of the VVSC
to a trust anchor of the vendor a TODO (`:232-240`), signs over the whole
to-be-signed message where `createStatementBytes` names the fabric binding
message (`:282-286` against `:311-322`), and parses a 76-byte binding
message inside the statement (`:324-339`) that chip's 85-byte statement
(`src/crypto/CHIPCryptoPAL.h:137-141` at `6170af84`, `version ||
signer_skid || signature`) does not carry; chip does not support the
statement at all (`src/credentials/jcm/VendorIdVerificationClient.cpp:103-104`).
`client/jcm.Verify` takes the statement path when `Info` carries one: the
statement in chip's 85-byte form, appended to the to-be-signed message
(`CHIPCryptoPAL.h:151-155`), the VVSC through `mattercert.DecodeVVSC`, the
signer key identifier, the statement signature over `version ||
vendor_fabric_binding_message || signer_skid`, and the VVSC signed by the
trust anchor `TrustAnchorLookup` returns for the vendor id and the VVSC's
AuthorityKeyID (`mattercert.VerifyVVSCIssuedBy`; an intermediate is
refused). Each difference fails closed: a statement anyone can sign with a
self-made VVSC would otherwise verify any vendor id. The JCM trust
verification still refuses a statement, as chip's does. Proof:
`client/jcm:TestVendorIdVerificationParity`; Ahead row above. Retires when
matter.js closes its TODOs — the statement message then follows matter.js
or is recorded against it.

### BD-Matter-Commissioner-TermsRequirementRead — the commissioner reads the device's terms-and-conditions requirement and fails early with it

matter.js's commissioning flow has no terms-and-conditions step: it goes
from `GeneralCommissioning.ConfigureRegulatoryInformation` (8.1) to
`TimeSynchronization.SynchronizeTime` (8.2) and leaves the consent a TODO
(`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:556-570` at
`db021da0`). connectedhomeip sends SetTCAcknowledgements when its
parameters carry an acknowledgement and skips the stage otherwise
(`src/controller/CHIPDeviceController.cpp:3946-3957` at `6170af84`;
`AutoCommissioner.cpp:485-487` orders it after the regulatory
configuration), and its `kReadCommissioningInfo` reads GeneralCommissioning's
SupportsConcurrentConnection, Breadcrumb, BasicCommissioningInfo,
RegulatoryConfig, LocationCapability and IsCommissioningWithoutPower — no TC
attribute (`CHIPDeviceController.cpp:2592-2603`). Neither learns that a device requires terms before
the device refuses CommissioningComplete with TCAcknowledgementsNotReceived,
after AddNOC. `controller/commissioner`'s step 0.1 (`getInitialData`) adds
the root GeneralCommissioning's FeatureMap, TCMinRequiredVersion,
TCAcknowledgementsRequired and TCUpdateDeadline to its second read (seven
paths, within the nine a server has to accept,
`CHIPDeviceController.cpp:2581-2582` at `6170af84`), and when the
device has the TC feature, holds no satisfying acceptance and the options'
acknowledgement is absent or below TCMinRequiredVersion, ends the
commissioning right after that step with `*commissioner.TermsRequiredError`
(`Version`, `Deadline` as Matter epoch seconds) — before ArmFailSafe, so the
device is left as found. The error names no acknowledgement bits (owner
decision 2026-11-08): a device serves no attribute naming the bits it
requires (TCAcknowledgements is the accepted set; the required set is the
vendor's DCL entry), so a missing bit stays the device's
RequiredTCNotAccepted at SetTCAcknowledgements, typed as
`*commissioner.GeneralCommissioningError` like every refused
GeneralCommissioning command. `controller.PairOptions.TermsAndConditions`
carries the acknowledgement. Owner decision 2026-11-07 (issue 449): read in
the information step, no step of its own. Pinned by
`TestTermsRequirementRead`, `TestTermsRequiredBeforeArmFailSafe`,
`TestGeneralCommissioningErrorTyped` (`controller/commissioner/terms_test.go`)
and `TestPairTermsRequired` (`controller/pair_terms_test.go`). Retire when
matter.js's flow reads the requirement (the marker goes).

### BD-matterjs-mdns-interface-allowlist — the mDNS responder can be restricted to named host interfaces

matter.js's `MdnsServer` keeps one `InterfaceResponder` per network
interface and announces "on every multicast interface", re-reading the
interfaces on `Network.interfacesChanged`
(`packages/protocol/src/mdns/MdnsServer.ts:36-43`, `:210-214` at
`db021da0`); it has no allow-list: its `MdnsService` limits the server to
one named interface or to none (`mdns.networkInterface`,
`packages/protocol/src/mdns/MdnsService.ts:34`, `:56`, `:63`; the
announcement's interfaces, `MdnsServer.ts:484-487`). `node.MDNS.Interfaces` restricts the
module's responder to the named host interfaces: `defaultAdvertiser`
composes `mdns.Responder.InterfaceFilter` as the default container filter
(`mdns.DefaultInterfaceFilter`) or "not named", so a named `docker0` or
`hassio` stays filtered, and an interface outside the list is announced on
and answered on as one the advertise policy excludes — listed, no
addresses, no records (`BD-Matter-MdnsFollowsAdvertisedAddresses`). An
unknown name is accepted (the interface check picks it up when it appears)
and `Node.DiagnoseMDNS` names it (`mdns.DiagnoseInterfaces`:
`interface_not_found`, `interface_filtered`, `interface_no_addresses`). It
does not scope `Network.Listen`. The case is a dual-homed host whose
gateway relays mDNS between its networks, so controllers cache the far
network's address too (go-ha2fabric issue 40); matter.js-based bridges
offer the same choice to operators at the host level. Owner decisions
2026-11-07 (issue 450): by name, within the default filter, `Listen`
untouched. Pinned by `TestMDNSInterfacesFilter`, `TestMDNSInterfacesValidate`,
`TestDiagnoseMDNSNamesUnknownInterface` (`node/mdns_interfaces_test.go`),
`TestDiagnoseInterfaces` and `TestAllowListAdvertisesOnNamedInterfaceOnly`
(`mdns/diagnose_interfaces_test.go`). An ordinary divergence — one named
interface there, a list of names here — and no longer a row of the Ahead
register (re-filed 2026-11-14, review II, phase 4): the register is for
behaviour matter.js implements none of, and the row's marker, the doc
sentence "…on every multicast interface." (`MdnsServer.ts:211`), stood beside
the working choice of one interface. Retire when matter.js's server takes a
list of interfaces.

### BD-matterjs-mdns-JoinsLateInterfaces — the mDNS responder joins the group on interfaces that come up after it started

matter.js joins the mDNS groups once, when `UdpMulticastServer.create`
opens its sockets (`packages/general/src/net/udp/UdpMulticastServer.ts:61`,
`:78` at `b25ed960`); a membership that fails is logged per interface and
the socket stays (`packages/nodejs/src/net/NodeJsUdpSocket.ts:189-205`),
and only a missing IPv6 socket fails the server (`UdpMulticastServer.ts:70-83`).
On `Network.interfacesChanged` its `MdnsServer` reads the interfaces again
and publishes on them (`packages/protocol/src/mdns/MdnsServer.ts:40-43`),
without a further `addMembership`: an interface that came up after the
sockets were opened is announced on, and queries multicast on it are not
received. The module's responder keeps matter.js's rule for the open —
`openSockets` succeeds with no interface up — and goes one step further:
at every listing of the interfaces, which it takes before each publication
and at each interface check, `joinNew` joins the groups on every up,
multicast-capable interface it holds no membership on, and leaves the group
of an interface that is gone (`mdns/socket.go`). Reasoning: a node
commissioned over BLE onto Wi-Fi (ADR 0031) starts with no network at all
and must answer the commissioner's operational query on the interface that
appears during commissioning; without the join it was announced once and
never found again — the defect wave 28c's proof showed. The resolver's
`joinMcast4`/`joinMcast6` keep refusing a join on no interface. Pinned by
`TestOpenSocketsWithoutInterface`, `TestSockets_JoinNewInterfaces` and
`TestSockets_ReceiveAfterJoinNew` (`mdns/socket_live_test.go`). Reconcile
when matter.js joins on an interface change.

### BD-chip-WpaSupplicantDriver — the Linux Wi-Fi driver speaks wpa_supplicant's D-Bus API after connectedhomeip, with seven departures

matter.js ships no Wi-Fi driver: its `NetworkCommissioningServer` is the
empty class (`packages/node/src/behaviors/network-commissioning/NetworkCommissioningServer.ts:18`
at `b25ed960`) and its example fakes the join
(`examples/device-onoff-advanced/src/cluster/DummyWifiNetworkCommissioningServer.ts:110-139`).
`wifi/wpasupplicant` (a nested module, the driver behind
`node.Network.WiFi.Driver`) therefore follows connectedhomeip's Linux
platform (`src/platform/Linux/ConnectivityManagerImpl_NetworkManagementWpaSupplicant.cpp`
at `6170af84`: bring-up `:464-520`, scan `:1251-1280` and `:1545-1595`, the
BSS mapping `:1385-1543`, connect `:852-943`, the verdict from the
interface's `State` `:287-418` with eight retries after an authentication
timeout `:56-61`), under the Ahead row of
BD-chip-WiFiNetworkCommissioningServer. Seven things differ. (1) A join that
does not end in Success removes the network it added; connectedhomeip
keeps it until the next join removes the current network (`:861-877`).
Owner decision 2026-11-11: the credential lives in the node's store only,
and wpa_supplicant must not go on trying a network whose join the node
reported as failed. (2) The committed network is not written into
wpa_supplicant's configuration: no `SaveConfig` (`CommitConfig`,
`:1118-1135`); the cluster keeps it in the node's store and rejoins at
start, so there is one copy. (3) No DHCP client is started
(`CHIP_DEVICE_CONFIG_LINUX_DHCPC_CMD`, `:1098-1115`): addressing is the
host's network stack's, and Matter needs the IPv6 link-local address the
kernel configures. (4) A credential of exactly 64 hex digits is handed
over as the 32 bytes of the raw PSK and an SSID that is not valid UTF-8 or
holds a NUL as its octets, both as D-Bus byte arrays; connectedhomeip
hands both as C strings (`:936-940`), which wpa_supplicant quotes — a
64-digit string is then refused as a passphrase over 63 characters, and a
C string ends at the first NUL (hostap `wpa_supplicant/dbus/dbus_new_handlers.c:141-170`
and `:225-257`, `wpa_supplicant/config.c:620-695` at `6d3d778`). A raw PSK
joins a WPA2 network; SAE needs the passphrase. (5) Empty credentials are
an open network, `key_mgmt` `NONE` without `psk`, where connectedhomeip
sends `psk ""` with `SAE WPA-PSK`. (6) A scan that does not end within its
timeout is UnknownError; connectedhomeip's StartWiFiScan (`:1251-1280`)
starts no timer of its own. The bound is a safety net of 30 s
(`DefaultScanTimeout`), above the 10 s the node advertises as
ScanMaxTimeSeconds as connectedhomeip does
(`src/platform/Linux/NetworkCommissioningDriver.h:86`): a scan of an
associated station measured 10.0 s against wpa_supplicant on a simulated
radio (3.7 s unassociated), and the bound covers the wait for `ScanDone`
only, not the reads of the results (`TestScanReadsAfterTheBound`). A
`ScanDone` that arrives before the driver's own `Scan` call has returned
is not read as its scan's (`TestScanIgnoresAStaleScanDone`). (7) The
network the interface was on is not removed before the join has ended;
connectedhomeip removes the current network first (`:861-877`), then adds
the new one, disconnects and selects it (`:881-904`). Here it is kept: a
successful join removes it then — one network, as there — and a failed
join, which removes the network it added (1), selects it again, so that
wpa_supplicant is back on the network it was on (review II, R2-P3-net-01;
`TestAFailedJoinKeepsTheNetworkItWasOn`). As there, a
`ScanDone` of another client's scan ends a waiting scan and its `success` argument is not read
(`:1545-1595`), and the attempt reads the interface's `State` only from
its own `SelectNetwork` on, where connectedhomeip's one flag
(`mAssociationStarted`, `:297-300`) also sees an association that was
under way before. The credential reaches `AddNetwork` and nothing else:
no log line, no error text, no debug text (the D-Bus error's name only).
Not carried over: PDC, AP mode and Wi-Fi PAF. Pinned by `TestConnect`,
`TestConnectFailureRemovesNetwork`, `TestConnectRawPSK`,
`TestConnectNonUTF8SSID`, `TestConnectOpenNetwork`,
`TestConnectIgnoresStatesBeforeSelect`, `TestScanOneAtATime`,
`TestScanDoneFailure` and `TestCredentialNeverLeaves`
(`wifi/wpasupplicant/driver_test.go`). Retire a point when connectedhomeip's
driver takes it; reconcile onto matter.js when it ships a driver.

Review II, phase 4 (2026-11-14): hostap at `6d3d778` is outside the exports
the review read and was not re-read; what this entry says of it is
unverified.

Review II, run 4 (R4-err-4351, owner decision 625), within departure (1): an `AddNetwork` that ends without wpa_supplicant's answer — the join's timeout or context, the bus daemon's NoReply — is settled by diffing the interface's `Networks` before the call against a later read: right after the call, or, when wpa_supplicant does not answer that read, before the next join or at Close; every new path is removed. Until that later read every network that appears in `Networks` and was not handed to the driver is removed — another client's included, and after a wpa_supplicant restart whatever comes back under a path not in the earlier list — so the window is bounded by the next join or Close, not by the one call; a Close whose read fails leaves the network behind. A join whose `Networks` read before `AddNetwork` stalls or fails — a timeout, the bus daemon's NoReply, a closed bus, any error name other than `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownProperty` — ends there: no credential is sent that the driver could not settle (decision 625, fail-closed). A wpa_supplicant that answers that read with `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownProperty` serves no such property — connectedhomeip's test mock does (`matter/testing/linux/wifi.py:665-695` at `6170af84` declares no `Networks`; the name measured over `dbus-send` in the CHIP harness image, sdbus 0.14.3) — and is joined without the list, as chip's join is; there an unanswered `AddNetwork` cannot be settled and the network it may have added stays (decision 637). chip's join (`_ConnectWiFiNetworkAsync`, `ConnectivityManagerImpl_NetworkManagementWpaSupplicant.cpp:850-905` at `6170af84`) reads no `Networks` before `AddNetwork` (`:881-882`) and has no settlement of an unanswered call: a failed `AddNetwork` is logged and fails the join, nothing removed (`:880-888`); so where the `Networks` read stalls or fails chip's join proceeds and this one fails. That wpa_supplicant carries out an `AddNetwork` whose caller stopped waiting, and that a later read on the same connection is answered after it, is unverified (hostap and dbus-daemon not pinned). Unverified as well (review II, run 5, R5-err-5403; not performable, hostap not pinned and not read): that an `AddNetwork` answered with an error reply other than the bus daemon's NoReply added nothing — the premise on which such a join settles nothing and looks for no network afterwards (`refused`, `wifi/wpasupplicant/driver.go`). Settling after such an answer too would remove another client's network in the case `TestAnAddNetworkNobodyAnsweredIsRemoved` ("an answered refusal owes nothing") holds, so the premise stays and is labelled. Reason: the credential lives in the node's store only, as in (1). Pinned by `TestAnAddNetworkNobodyAnsweredIsRemoved`, `TestAJoinWithTheNetworksUnreadableSendsNoCredential`, `TestAJoinWithoutANetworksPropertyAddsTheNetwork` and `TestUnknownProperty` (`wifi/wpasupplicant/driver_test.go`).

### BD-Matter-CertValidityNotEnforced — a NOC or ICAC outside its validity period verifies; the verifier's clock is not read

matter.js checks neither bound of an operational certificate's validity
period against the clock: its verification ends with "notBefore date
should be already reached, notAfter is not checked right now", logs a
warning for a notBefore in the future and has the throw commented out
(`packages/protocol/src/certificate/kinds/OperationalBase.ts:99-106` at
`b25ed960`). `mattercert.Verifier.checkValidity`
(`secure/mattercert/verify.go:602-612`) does the same without the warning:
it refuses a NotBefore or NotAfter that names no representable time and
compares neither with a clock; the `TimeSource` a verifier is built with
(`verify.go:48`, `:197`) is stored and never read. Mirrored: a node
without a trusted clock cannot judge expiry, and matter.js leaves the
check to its Last-Known-Good-Time TODO (`:100`). connectedhomeip's
validity policy was not read for this entry (unverified). Pinned by
`secure/mattercert:TestCertValidityNotEnforced` (`cb2377a9`): a NOC and
an ICAC, expired and not yet valid, verify through
`Verifier.VerifyAndExtractPubKey`, and a `TimeSource` that counts its
reads is read zero times. Three older tests already held that a
certificate outside its period verifies, one case each —
`TestVerifyAndExtractPubKey_Expired`,
`TestVerifyAndExtractPubKey_ICAC_Expired` and
`TestCheckValidity_NotYetValid`; until 2026-11-13 this entry said no
test did, and what none held was that the clock is not read. The
representable-time half is pinned by
`TestCheckValidityRejectsAWrappingNotBefore`,
`TestCheckValidityRejectsAWrappingNotAfter` and
`TestCheckValidityAcceptsOrdinaryBounds` (review II, W1-sec-04). Retire
when matter.js enforces the period.

### BD-Matter-BTP-ATTMTUFieldIsSegmentSize — the BLE central writes the BTP segment size into the handshake request's ATT_MTU field

matter.js's central derives the segment size from the connection's
ATT_MTU (`packages/nodejs-ble/src/NobleBleChannel.ts:679-681` at
`b25ed960`; `btpSegmentSizeFromAttMtu` is the ATT_MTU less 3, clamped,
`packages/protocol/src/ble/BleConsts.ts:37-42`) and sends it as the
request's `attMtu` (`NobleBleChannel.ts:624`, `attMtu: segmentSize`); its
peripheral reads the field as a "Number excluding 3 header bytes" and
takes it as the fragment size
(`packages/protocol/src/ble/BtpSessionHandler.ts:99`, `:111-122`).
`controller/ble` does the same (`channel.go:275`
`btp.SegmentSizeFromATTMTU`, `:301` `ATTMTU: uint16(segment)`).
connectedhomeip's peripheral reads the field as the ATT_MTU and subtracts
3 itself (`src/ble/BLEEndPoint.cpp:991-994`, `:1001-1004` at `6170af84`),
so against a chip device the fragment size comes out 3 bytes below what
the link carries (inferred from the two reads; not measured against a
chip device). Mirrored: matter.js decides the wire shape (order of
authority 1), and the cost is throughput only. Pinned by
`controller/ble:TestNobleBleChannelAttMtuSettle` (an ATT_MTU of 247
offers 244, `channel_parity_matterjs_test.go:131`; review II, W1-wire-10).
Retire when matter.js's central sends the ATT_MTU.

### BD-Matter-Read-RepeatedPathsDropped — a repeated AttributePathIB of a Read or Subscribe is read once

matter.js's server registers one data producer per requested path, in
request order and with no check for a repeat
(`packages/protocol/src/action/server/AttributeReadResponse.ts:88-94`,
`:442-448` at `db021da0`), and runs the producers one after the other
(`:96-100`), so a path sent twice is answered twice (inferred from those
lines; not run); only its client-side request builder dedupes
(`packages/protocol/src/action/request/Read.ts:338-352`).
`im.DedupAttributePaths` (`im/read.go`) drops every byte-identical repeat
of an earlier path, first occurrence first, when the expansion of a read,
a priming report or a re-established subscription's report is built
(`im.NewAttributeExpansion`, `im/read_expansion.go`). What is deliberate
in it is small: a repeat would be expanded and sent a second time, and the
drop saves that work and those bytes. It is this module's own saving and
no bound: paths that differ in a field the expansion ignores, and
wildcards that overlap, are each expanded, as matter.js expands them. Until
review II, R2-P2-alloc-04 this entry gave a bound on the materialised
report as its reason; that did not hold for such paths, and what bounds a
response since is that it is generated chunk by chunk (owner decision 44),
as matter.js generates it
(`AttributeReadResponse.ts:96-100`, `:311-332`). connectedhomeip prunes
its path list too, by another rule: a concrete path that a wildcard of the
same request covers is removed (`src/app/ReadHandler.cpp:530`,
`src/app/InteractionModelEngine.cpp:1669-1716` at `6170af84`); that
function leaves identical repeats alone. Pinned by
`im:TestHandleReadRequest_IdenticalPathsAreReadOnce` and
`im:TestDedupAttributePaths_KeepsOrderAndDistinctPaths` (review II,
W2-wire-15). The first half of the condition this entry named for its
retirement — the report bounded without the drop — holds since
R2-P2-alloc-04, whose fix kept the drop. Retire when a repeat is answered
as matter.js answers it.

### BD-Matter-Peer-ConnectAfterDisconnectRetries — a connection process started after `Set.Disconnect` retries an attempt that cannot succeed

matter.js's `PeerSet.disconnect` clears its exchange manager "to prevent
future connections" (`packages/protocol/src/peer/PeerSet.ts:248-256` at
`b25ed960`), after which the peer context's `exchanges` accessor throws
`ImplementationError("Client networking is not initialized")` (`:83-86`).
A connection attempt reads the accessor when it creates its exchange
(`packages/protocol/src/peer/PeerConnection.ts:544`), and the error
handling gives an error that is neither a status response nor a
`TransientPeerCommunicationError` the delay
`timing.delayAfterUnhandledError` and the category "general"
(`:715-717`), a warning (`:762-764`) and another attempt. `client/peer`
mirrors it: after `Set.Disconnect` an attempt returns `ErrNotConnectable`
(`client/peer/connection.go:1381-1383`), which the classifier answers
with `DelayAfterUnhandledError` and "general" (`:1747-1748`; the error
handler may replace the delay or end the process, `:1643-1656`).
Mirrored, not improved: a refusal in `initiateConnection` would be an
*Ahead of matter.js* row with `PeerSet.ts:85` as its marker (review II,
W4-ctlnet-07). Pinned for the attempt's error by
`client/peer:TestInitialContactRefreshKickBeforeSend`
(`initial_contact_schedule_parity_matterjs_test.go:507`), for the first
pause and the timeout by `TestUnhandledErrorAndDisconnectedSet`, and for
the repetition by `client/peer:TestConnectAfterDisconnectRetries`
(`cb2377a9`): four rounds, each failing with `ErrNotConnectable`, each
pausing `DelayAfterUnhandledError`, nothing sent and the process still
running. Retire when matter.js refuses the connect.

### BD-Matter-Attestation-ValidityAtDacNotBefore — the attestation chain is judged at the DAC's notBefore; without a clock, a DAC past its notAfter is accepted

matter.js's validator checks "Certificate validity at DAC's notBefore
timestamp": the DAC's notBefore must lie inside the PAI's and the PAA's
validity (a notAfter of 0 is none), and the current time is not consulted
(`packages/protocol/src/certificate/DeviceAttestationValidator.ts:393-419`
at `db021da0`). `controller/attestation` does the same
(`validate.go:229-241`; the file reads no clock), so a DAC past its own
notAfter, or a PAI that has expired since the DAC was issued, passes.
connectedhomeip refuses an expired DAC where it has a clock
(`src/credentials/attestation_verifier/DefaultDeviceAttestationVerifier.cpp:638-641`
at `6170af84`: `IsCertificateValidAtCurrentTime(info.dacDerBuffer)` →
`kDacExpired`, compiled out under `CURRENT_TIME_NOT_IMPLEMENTED`).
Mirrored: matter.js decides where it models something (order of authority
1; review 2026-11 W4-ctlsec-03, verdict "stay with matter.js", no Ahead
row). Pinned by
`controller/attestation:TestAttestationValidityAtDacNotBefore`
(`cb2377a9`): an expired DAC, a PAI that expired after the DAC was
issued and both are accepted, and a DAC issued after the PAI's notAfter
is refused (review II, W4-ctlsec-03). Retire when matter.js consults the
clock.

Review II, phase 6b (owner decision 193, R2-P6-par-1805): the entry holds for a validation context without a clock only. With a clock — the commissioner always sets one — a DAC past its notAfter is the error finding `CertificateExpired`, as connectedhomeip refuses it (`BD-chip-Attestation-DacExpiredAtClock`).

### BD-chip-Commissioner-AbortDisarmsFailSafe — a commissioning that ends after PASE disarms the device's fail-safe, whatever ended it

matter.js's `#expireFailsafe`
(`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:1097-1132` at
`b25ed960`) runs after every step failure `executeCommissioning` does not
recover from (`:448`). In its order it stops the re-arm timer; sends nothing
without an end time (`:1101`) or when the device stopped responding
(`:1102-1105`, `#deviceStoppedResponding` `:996-1003`); then awaits a re-arm
in flight (`:1107`) and sends ArmFailSafe(0) over an existing session only,
checks the response, and only logs a failure (`:1108-1131`).
`flow.expireFailsafe` mirrors this; on a skip it cancels the re-arm in
flight (pin lift b25ed960, unit P3-D). What remains ahead is the abort and
the disarm before an ArmFailSafe of the flow's was answered (the end time is
set only at `:878`). The flow takes no abort signal (the constructor, `:332-351` at `b25ed960`); the
commissioner's `abort` option is the "External abort signal that, when
fired, cancels all in-flight PASE attempts"
(`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioner.ts:196` at `b25ed960`;
handed on at `:262` and `:277` at `db021da0`, not re-read), and
`executeCommissioning()` is called without one (`:771` at `b25ed960`). A Go caller ends a commissioning through its context: a step that
returned the context's error left the device's fail-safe armed until it
expired. `controller/commissioner` follows connectedhomeip, whose
`CleanupCommissioning` — "If we're cleaning up because cancellation has
been requested via StopPairing(), expire the failsafe in the background" —
sends ArmFailSafe with expiry 0 over the session the commissioning holds
and ignores a failure (`src/controller/CHIPDeviceController.cpp:2219-2247`,
the request `:2164-2170`, the ignored failure `:2233-2236`, `StopPairing`
`:1204-1233` at `6170af84`). When `execute`'s context has ended and the
step's error is neither a CommissioningError nor a status error, or is one
that carries the context's error — the Reconnect step's
ErrOperativeConnectionFailed, which wraps what the operational connection
gave up with (`callerAborted`) — `disarmAfterAbort`
(`controller/commissioner/flow.go`) stops the BLE re-arm timer and sends
the request `#expireFailsafe` sends (`sendFailsafeExpiry`, the response
checked) on a context of its own,
then returns the step's error unchanged (from the Reconnect step that is
the step's error with the context's as its cause: it matches the context's
with `errors.Is` and is not that error). The disarm is owed from the PASE
session's establishment, which armed the device's fail-safe (the last
paragraph), and for an ArmFailSafe that was started, not only for one that
was answered (`armStarted`, set in `newFlow` and in `armFailsafe` before the
invoke); a device that holds no fail-safe answers it with "a success
response with no side effect" (matter.js
`packages/node/src/behaviors/general-commissioning/GeneralCommissioningServer.ts:96-98`
at `db021da0`). Nothing is sent once the device has confirmed
CommissioningComplete or a disarm, or when the session is closed.
connectedhomeip does not ask what was armed either: its branch tests the
completion status alone (`:2219`) and a failed stage's next stage is
`kCleanup` whatever it was (`src/controller/AutoCommissioner.cpp:465-468`
at `6170af84`; the path from there to `CleanupCommissioning` was not
traced, unverified). Two differences from connectedhomeip, both this
module's: the send is awaited, for at most
`abortDisarmTimeout` = `FailSafeMaxSendTime` (10 s; `FAILSAFE_MAX_SEND_TIME`,
`:302`), because `Commission` closes the PASE session when the flow returns;
and the request carries the flow's current breadcrumb where connectedhomeip
sends 0 (`:2168`). That the disarm leaves over BLE too is inferred from the
channel keeping its own context, not exercised (unverified). Not covered,
and said in `disarmAfterAbort`'s comment: a datagram of the aborted
ArmFailSafe still on its way can reach the device behind the disarm, and so
can a re-arm of the BLE timer already in flight. Owner decision 5
(review II, W4-ctlsec-08, R2-P0-rv-C01, R2-P0-rv-C02). Pinned by
`controller/commissioner:TestFlowDisarmsFailsafeWhenCallerAborts`,
`TestFlowDisarmsFailsafeStartedNotAnswered` and `TestFlowReconnectAbort`.
Register row above; the row closes when matter.js's flow takes an abort
signal and resets on it.

**Every exit after PASE (added 2026-11-14; review II, phase 3 rework, R2-P3-rr-ctl-03, R2-P3-rr-ctl-05).** Both references' devices arm a fail-safe when a PASE session is established — matter.js "As required by Commissioning Flows any new PASE session needs to arm the failsafe for 60s" (`packages/node/src/behaviors/general-commissioning/GeneralCommissioningServer.ts:55-65` at `db021da0`), connectedhomeip in `OnSessionEstablished` (`src/app/server/CommissioningWindowManager.cpp:226-236` at `6170af84`, the arm at `:236`) — and matter.js's accepts no new PASE exchange while a PASE session exists that is not closing (`packages/protocol/src/session/pase/PaseServer.ts:76-82` at `db021da0`), which the fail-safe's expiry closes (`packages/protocol/src/common/FailsafeContext.ts:277-279`). matter.js's commissioner disarms on one way out: `#expireFailsafe` after a step failure it does not recover from (`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:439-454` at `b25ed960`, the call at `:448`), which returns at once while no fail-safe end is known (`:1101`). Its other exits close only: the catch of `commission` force-closes the PASE session (`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioner.ts:304-306`, `#closePaseSession`, `:313-319` at `db021da0`), a session `continueAfterPase` refuses is force-closed (`:368-373` at `db021da0`), and so is one established after another candidate won the connection (`packages/protocol/src/peer/CommissioningConnection.ts:140-157` at `db021da0`). connectedhomeip disarms after a failure before its network setup stages — the branch at `src/controller/CHIPDeviceController.cpp:2248` at `6170af84` keeps the fail-safe from `kWiFiNetworkSetup` on, the one at `:2271-2278` sends the disarm, "we also need to force a reset on the failsafe so we can start fresh on the next attempt". Here every exit after PASE disarms while the device may hold the fail-safe and the session stands (`controller/commissioner`): a step that failed for any reason, classed or not and whether or not an ArmFailSafe of the flow's was answered (`flow.disarmAfterFailure` → `expireFailsafe`; with a fail-safe end known it is matter.js's `#expireFailsafe`, without one ahead of it, and in both cases skipped when the device stopped responding); a node id another candidate claimed, and a failure before the flow runs (`Commissioner.disarmPASE`); a PASE session established after another candidate had won the connection or after the abort (`connectionConfig.giveUp`, `Commissioner.giveUpPASE`); and one that `EstablishPASE`'s `ContinueAfterPASE` refuses. Each disarm is bounded by the caller's context and the exchange's response timeout and, that context having ended, by `abortDisarmTimeout`; a losing session is disarmed beside the next candidate's attempt, and a connection without a winner returns only after its losing sessions were disarmed. No CloseSession is added: the device's rollback closes the session. Two choices are this module's, with no reference: a losing session is disarmed without a check that it does not reach the winner's device — it relies on a device accepting one PASE at a time — and a disarm before the flow carries the flow's starting breadcrumb (`initialBreadcrumb` = 1, matter.js's `lastBreadcrumb`, `ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:326` at `b25ed960`). Not covered: a commissioning whose Reconnect fails on a non-concurrent device holds no session to disarm over, as in matter.js ("For non-concurrent flow the BLE connection already dropped when connectNetwork was sent", `ControllerCommissioningFlow.ts:2050` at `b25ed960`), and neither does one whose device completed PASE while the commissioner never saw its last message. Who sees it: a device a `Pair` gave up on, which accepts the next one at once and not after its fail-safe; a caller, whose failed `Pair` returns after the disarm's exchange. Pinned by `controller/commissioner:TestCommissionGivenUpBeforeTheFlowFreesThePASESession`, `TestEstablishPASERefusedAfterPASEFreesThePASESession`, `TestPASESessionThatLostTheRaceIsFreed`, `TestFlowDisarmAfterFailureIsBoundedByTheCaller` and `TestConnectionLosingDisarmRunsBesideTheNextAddress`, `TestCommissioningFailsafeExpiry` with its subtest "ahead of matter.js: ends the PASE session's fail-safe before the flow armed" and `TestFailsafeExpirySkipCancelsTheRearmInFlight`, and `controller:TestPairThatGivesUpLeavesNoPASESession`.

**A step after the commissioning channel's loss (pin lift b25ed960, unit P3-D, coordinator decision C-12, 390).** A flow step that starts on the PASE session after its commissioning channel was lost fails with `exchange.ErrSessionClosed` plus the channel's `ClosedCause` (`flow.channelLoss`, `controller/commissioner/flow.go`), so the network steps read it as a channel drop (`isChannelDrop`) and the expiry is skipped as for a device that stopped responding. matter.js attaches the BLE cause to the exchanges pending at the force-close (`packages/protocol/src/peer/ControllerCommissioner.ts:523-558` at `b25ed960`, `#closeOnBleLoss`); what it reports for an exchange started after the close was not established (Fable post-read of P3-D, F1; unverified). This is the module's addition; it has no security effect, because over a closed channel the expiry could not be delivered either way.

### BD-chip-HandshakeSecretsOverwritten — handshake key material is overwritten once it has served or the handshake has failed

matter.js keeps the SPAKE2+ and Sigma secrets as locals and leaves them to
the collector: `Ke`, `hAY` and `hBX`
(`packages/protocol/src/session/pase/PaseServer.ts:174` at `db021da0`, `Ke`
handed to `createSecureSession` at `:190`), `sharedSecret`, `sigma2Key` and
`sigma3Key` (`packages/protocol/src/session/case/CaseServer.ts:243`, `:251`,
`:284`). connectedhomeip clears them: `Spake2p_P256_SHA256_HKDF_HMAC::Clear`
(`src/crypto/CHIPCryptoPALOpenSSL.cpp:1119-1154` at `6170af84`,
`ClearSecretData(Kcab)` and `(Kae)` at `:1150-1151`), `PASESession::Clear`
("so that no security related information will be leaked",
`src/protocols/secure_channel/PASESession.cpp:137-158`), the self-clearing
`SensitiveDataBuffer` and `SensitiveDataFixedBuffer`
(`src/crypto/CHIPCryptoPAL.h:299-306`, `:375-394`; the ECDH secret is one,
`:428`, `src/protocols/secure_channel/CASESession.h:562`), the Sigma salt and
key of `CASESession.cpp:1201` and `:1207` (the key released through
`CASESession.h:467`, `src/crypto/SessionKeystore.h:160-164` and
`src/crypto/RawKeySessionKeystore.cpp:96-99`) and `CASESession::Clear`
(`CASESession.cpp:376-397`). This module follows connectedhomeip.
**Overwritten:** in `secure/spake2` the PBKDF2 output and the passcode
bytes, w1 once L exists, the scalars x and y, the w0 copy, Z, V, the
transcript, K_main and the confirmation keys — and Ke when the confirmation
fails; in `secure/sigma` S2K, S3K, the salts that carry the IPK, the
resumption keys, the bytes the session keys are cut from — and the shared
secret when the handshake fails or the responder is reset; in the callers
the initiator's Ke copy and derived key bytes (`client/handshake/pase.go`)
and the Ke the node facade's PASE callback receives (`node/security.go`).
On the device side too since `065e2207` (review II, R2-P0-rv-B03): the 48
derived bytes of `operational.Manager.OpenFromPase` and `OpenFromPaseWithID`
(`paseSession`, `secure/operational/manager.go`), on every way out, once the
session holds its own copies of the two keys and the challenge is copied
out. And through three `Close` methods what a handshake object still
holds: `spake2.Verifier.Close` (Ke after a success; y, Z, V, KcA, KcB and
Ke of a handshake Pake3 never came for), `spake2.Prover.Close` (Ke after a
success; x, w0 and w1 when Pake2 never came) and
`commissioning.PASEResponder.Close` (its key block) — a closed object
answers every step with its state error and hands out no Ke.
`commissioning.PASEResponder` derives its key block once, in
`HandlePake3`, overwrites its copy of Ke there and closes its verifier on
every way out; `client/handshake`'s `pairPASE` closes its prover on every
way out. **What still lives on, and why:** the session's two keys in
`channel.Session` and the attestation challenge in the session's entry —
they are the session; the stored verifier (`VerifierContext`: w0 and L),
which serves every later handshake; `PASEResponder`'s key block until its
`Close`, because `Session` and `AttestationChallenge` hand it out on every
call; Ke in a `Verifier` or `Prover` until its `Close`, because
`SharedSecret` may be asked for it until then; the session keys and the
ECDH shared secret of a finished CASE for as long as the `Responder` or
`Initiator` is held — their readers take them after Sigma3, and the shared
secret is the resumption record; the four passcode bytes `spake2.PBKDF`
hands to `crypto/pbkdf2` as a string, which cannot be reached to be
overwritten (R2-P0-rv-B08); the Ke the bridge's adapter hands to a host's
`bridge.PaseSessionEstablished` callback — the slice is the callback's to
overwrite, and overwriting it after the call would break a host that derives
later; and the shared secret passed to `store.Port.UpsertResumption`, because
the port states no rule that a store does not keep the slice. **The device
side's gap:** the bridge's PASE adapter does not close its verifier.
`PaseAdapter.consumePake3` takes the copy `SharedSecret` returns and sets
its field to nil, as the adapter's other sites that drop a verifier do
(`bridge/handlers.go`), so the verifier's own Ke — and KcA and Ke of a
handshake that was given up — still goes to the collector there. A `Close`
at those sites is not a line each: `NewPaseAdapter` hands the same verifier
out for every Pake1 ("the verifier is reused for every Pake1 the adapter
sees"), and a closed verifier answers the next one with its state error.
Who owns and ends the verifier a factory returns is a contract decision,
open for phase 5 of review II together with the two contract sentences
W1-sec-05 would need — that the callback of `bridge.PaseSessionEstablished`
overwrites its slice, and that a store does not keep the slice
`store.Port.UpsertResumption` is handed. The CASE adapter clears its copy
of the shared secret of every `sigma.Established` value it drops — a resume
that installs no session, a resume or Sigma3 whose `SetOnEstablished`
callback refuses it, a Sigma3 with no callback, and one handed to the
deprecated `CaseSessionEstablished` callback, which receives only the keys
and the peer session id; a value a host's `SetOnEstablished` callback
installs is the host's record (`bridge/handlers.go`, `dropEstablished`;
review II, C5-h1-n3, decision 658; pinned by
`bridge:TestUninstalledResumeClearsItsSecret` and
`TestDroppedSessionValuesClearTheirSecret`); the value types `Keys` and
`ResumeKeys` of a dropped value are not overwritten. Best effort in any
case: Go gives no guarantee against copies (stack growth, values passed by
value, `math/big`, `crypto/ecdh`, `crypto/aes` key schedules, `crypto/hkdf`,
`hmac`), stated at `secure/sigma/zero.go` and `spake2.zero`. Two behaviour
changes the overwriting forces: a failed PASE confirmation is final for the
`Verifier` and the `Prover`, and `Responder.ECDHSharedSecret` is nil after a
failed Sigma3. Owner decision 6 (review II, W1-sec-05). Pinned by
`secure/spake2:TestHandshakeSecretsOverwrittenAfterSuccess`,
`TestVerifierOverwritesAndEndsAfterFailedConfirmation`,
`TestProverOverwritesAndEndsAfterFailure`,
`TestCloseOverwritesKeAfterSuccess` and
`TestCloseOverwritesAnAbandonedHandshake`, the six tests of
`secure/sigma/zeroise_test.go`, `secure/channel:TestNewKeepsItsOwnKeys`,
`secure/operational:TestOpenFromPaseOverwritesTheKeyBlock`,
`commissioning:TestPASEResponderOverwritesKeAndOnCloseItsKeys` and
`TestPASEResponderOverwritesAfterAFailedOrAbandonedHandshake`,
`client/handshake:TestPASEClosesItsProver` and
`bridge:TestPaseAdapter_TheCallbackOwnsKe`; the overwrite of the
initiator's Ke copy and derived bytes in `client/handshake` and the one in
`node` have no seam and are held by reading only.
Register row above; the row closes when matter.js clears its handshake
secrets.

### BD-Matter-GroupReceptionBoundedPerKey — at most 256 senders per operational group key hold a replay window; a further sender is refused, nobody evicted

matter.js keeps one reception state per operational key and source node without a bound (`packages/protocol/src/groups/MessagingState.ts:19`, `:80-90` at `b25ed960`); connectedhomeip caches the senders per fabric — 15 data, 2 control by default (`src/lib/core/CHIPConfig.h:832-844` at `6170af84`) — and replaces the least recently used sender when the table is full (`src/transport/GroupPeerMessageCounter.cpp:59-98`). go-fabric holds at most 256 senders per operational key (`groups/decode.go` `maxGroupSendersPerKey`, chosen from memory: tens of kilobytes per key at most) and refuses a sender beyond them without evicting one, because eviction lets a party without the key replay a recorded datagram of an evicted sender (R2-P0-rv-B01, owner decisions 22 and 133). The cost: a key set with more than 256 group senders over its life — senders that left keep their places until the key goes — drops the later ones; the first refusal per key is logged at warn (`groups.reception.full`). A replay window survives a `ForgetFabric` and the reload that follows it while the reloaded key set keeps the same keys (`groups/manager.go`, parked windows). Review II, phase 6a (N4-bdnotes-2); pinned by `groups:TestReceptionStateIsBoundedPerKey` and `TestReceptionStateSurvivesForgetAndReload`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js bounds its reception state.

Until review II, phase 6a this entry was `BD-Matter-GroupReceptionUnbounded`. What follows is its record of the unbounded design and of the evicting bound before it. It was not a departure from matter.js: its behaviour, kept against
connectedhomeip's bound and recorded because this module carried that
bound for one commit (`5ca8da6a`, with an Ahead row of this register;
both went with `48e53ec5`, owner decision 22 of review II). matter.js keeps the reception
state of group data messages "per Operational key and source node"
(`packages/protocol/src/groups/MessagingState.ts:18-19` at `b25ed960`):
`receptionStateFor` creates a state for every source node id it is asked
for (`:80-90`), no line counts the entries, and the map's one removal is
`forgetReceptionState`, which drops a whole key (`:97-99`). It is asked
once a group packet has come back decoded from `groupSessionFromPacket`
(`packages/protocol/src/protocol/ExchangeManager.ts:369-378`,
`packages/protocol/src/session/GroupSession.ts:289-295`).
`groups.Manager.receptionWindow` (`groups/decode.go`) keeps the same: one
`mrp.Window` per operational key and source node id, dropped with the last
key set that derives the key (`forgetUnreferenced`, `groups/manager.go`).
**connectedhomeip bounds the table, and what the lines of its bound
show.** `CHIP_CONFIG_MAX_GROUP_DATA_PEERS` is 15 senders per fabric
(`src/lib/core/CHIPConfig.h:832-834` at `6170af84`, under "TODO: Determine
a better value for this", `:830`), kept as "LRU caches"
(`src/transport/GroupPeerMessageCounter.h:53-57`). A sender the table does
not hold is put at the front as a new entry, and on a full table the last
one is evicted (`src/transport/GroupPeerMessageCounter.cpp:63-64`,
`:79-95`); a new entry's counter starts not synchronised
(`src/transport/PeerMessageCounter.h:40`), and under the trust-first
policy `VerifyOrTrustFirstGroup` takes the first counter such an entry
sees and returns no error (`src/transport/SessionManager.cpp:1287-1294`,
`PeerMessageCounter.h:102-108`). The lookup follows the decryption — a
message that decrypts under no group key is discarded before it
(`SessionManager.cpp:1213-1260`) — and a recorded datagram decrypts as it
did the first time. By these lines, once a fabric has had 16 or more
senders, a recorded message of a sender that fell off the table is taken
as that sender's first, whoever presents it, with the key or without.
That is a reading of the lines; connectedhomeip was not run (unverified
against a build). **What was run** is this module's own table while it
was bounded the same way — 15 senders per operational key, the least
recently accepted evicted, a new sender's first counter trusted:
`groups:TestRecordedGroupMessageStaysADuplicate` against an export of
`5ca8da6a` (one recorded datagram per sender, presented again round-robin,
oldest first, three rounds) fails with "48 of 48 byte-identical replays
were accepted as new messages" for 16 senders, 300 of 300 for 100 and
3000 of 3000 for 1000 (re-run for this entry; the diff review's own run
found 80 of 80 over five rounds, R2-P0-rv-B01). On the code since
`48e53ec5` the test passes: every such replay is a duplicate for as long
as the key is held. **What the missing bound costs:** memory, under a
holder of the group key. An entry is 48 to 67 bytes of retained heap —
measured for this entry as the `runtime.MemStats.HeapAlloc` difference,
two `runtime.GC()` before each reading, over n entries added under one key
through `receptionWindow(key, source).Accept(7)`: 66.6, 53.6, 47.8 and
61.8 bytes per entry for n = 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 and 1e6 (go1.27.4,
darwin/arm64; a throwaway test, not committed), so 61.8 MB for a million
claimed source node ids — and costs its maker one datagram that
authenticates. **Who can grow the table:** only a holder of the group key.
The source node id of a group message is its sender's claim under a
symmetric key, so a holder adds one entry per id it states, until the key
set is removed or rewritten; a datagram that does not authenticate under a
mapped key adds none
(`groups:TestOnlyAnAuthenticatedGroupMessageCreatesReceptionState`: a
recorded message under 1000 forged source node ids, a changed counter,
payload or tag, a key the node does not hold under a session id it does, a
key set no group is mapped to). **Decided** (review II, phase 6a, owner decision 133): the bound per operational key that refuses and evicts nobody, above. R2-P0-bound-A07 = R2-P0-bound-E02 asked for a bound and
R2-P0-rv-B01 showed what the one taken first cost.

### BD-Matter-UnsecuredRetransmitEviction — the unsecured session's retransmit table holds 16 messages, evicts the one tracked first and never refuses a reply

matter.js keeps the message awaiting its acknowledgement and its timer on
the exchange (`packages/protocol/src/protocol/MessageExchange.ts:285`,
`:293` at `db021da0`); there is no table to bound, and the session intervals
a peer states are "uint32 and accepted unbounded"
(`packages/protocol/src/session/SessionIntervals.ts:52-53`). matter.js's
one cap on exchanges, `MAXIMUM_CONCURRENT_OUTGOING_EXCHANGES_PER_SESSION` =
30 (`packages/protocol/src/protocol/ExchangeManager.ts:63`), leaves a
session that is not secure out — "PASE/CASE exchanges are not relevant for
this limit" (`:578-582`); a search of `packages/protocol/src` for another
constant that names a maximum of exchanges found none. Before `834eb5ac` any peer could park one entry per Sigma1 on
this module's unsecured session, paced by the intervals it stated. The
bridge holds at most `unsecuredEntryLimit` = 16 reliable messages on the
unsecured session (`bridge/outbound_reliable.go`) — a responder's replies
and the messages of a handshake this node opened. **The rule, this
module's own** (owner decision 23 of review II): a message on the unsecured
session is always sent and always tracked; when the table is full the
entry tracked first loses its place — its datagram went out when it was
tracked, it loses its retransmissions and nothing else, and a warning
`matter.tx.reliable.unsecured_evicted` names it. An entry ends with its
acknowledgement, when its handshake moves past it or fails, when its
retries are spent, or `unsecuredEntryLifetime` = 60 s after it was tracked,
due or not. The StatusReport that ends a handshake is sent after the
handshake's other entries were dropped, as a reliable message, so it is
the one entry the exchange keeps and is retransmitted — as both references
send a StatusReport they send: matter.js through `exchange.send` without
`suppressAck`, which asks for the acknowledgement, starts the
retransmission timer and waits
(`packages/protocol/src/securechannel/SecureChannelMessenger.ts:209-232`,
`MessageExchange.ts:692`, `:785-790`, `:821-830`), connectedhomeip through
a plain `SendMessage`, reliable on a session that allows MRP
(`src/protocols/secure_channel/PairingSession.h:157-190`,
`src/messaging/ExchangeContext.cpp:111-114` at `6170af84`). When the
references send none, and this module did, was the finding F-db021da0-7,
closed 2026-11-17 (owner decision 173): the module sends none there either. **What a flood costs:** retransmissions. Sixteen further
reliable messages on the unsecured session between a handshake's reply and
its acknowledgement evict that reply; the handshake then fails only if the
reply's datagram is lost as well, at the initiator's own timeout. **What a
flood cannot do:** keep a reply from being sent, or make the table grow.
**connectedhomeip is the comparison, not the source.** Its table holds
every session's entries and has the same default size —
`ObjectPool<RetransTableEntry, CHIP_CONFIG_RMP_RETRANS_TABLE_SIZE>`
(`src/messaging/ReliableMessageMgr.h:267`), sized by
`CHIP_CONFIG_MAX_EXCHANGE_CONTEXTS`
(`src/messaging/ReliableMessageProtocolConfig.h:134`, `:146`; 16,
`src/lib/core/CHIPConfig.h:303-305`) — and it refuses the message that
does not fit: `CHIP_ERROR_RETRANS_TABLE_FULL`
(`src/messaging/ReliableMessageMgr.cpp:254-263`), returned before the
message is sent (`src/messaging/ExchangeMessageDispatch.cpp:63-64`). That
bound holds only where its pools are static: with
`CHIP_SYSTEM_CONFIG_POOL_USE_HEAP` "the ObjectPool size parameter is
ignored" (`src/lib/support/Pool.h:619-626`), and Linux and Darwin set it
(`src/platform/Linux/SystemPlatformConfig.h:41`,
`src/platform/Darwin/SystemPlatformConfig.h:39`). This module refused the
message that did not fit first (`834eb5ac`, under another Ahead row of
this register): sixteen entries for all peers, the
newest refused, each for up to 60 s, let any node on the link keep every
handshake from being answered with sixteen Sigma1 a minute (the diff
review's trace, R2-P0-rv-A01); `e98028e4` replaced the refusal with the
eviction. **Why 16:** under eviction the size has to cover the handshakes
of honest peers that wait for an acknowledgement at the same moment — one
PASE, the single-active slot, and the CASE handshakes of controllers that
reconnect together — and a flood evicts at any size, so a larger table
buys memory, not protection (a judgement: no count of concurrent
handshakes was measured). The lifetime's value is matter.js's PASE pairing
timeout (`packages/protocol/src/session/pase/PaseServer.ts:33`), applied
to every message of the unsecured session; the rule is no reference's.
Review II, R2-P0-bound-A06, R2-P0-rv-A01, -A02, -A04, -A05, -A07. Pinned by
`bridge:TestUnsecuredRetransmitTableEvictsItsOldestEntry`,
`TestSigma1FloodDoesNotStopLegitimateHandshakes`,
`TestSigma1FloodDoesNotGrowTheRetransmitTable`,
`TestUnsecuredRetransmitEntriesEndWithTheirHandshake`,
`TestInitiatedHandshakeIsTrackedAtAFullTable`,
`TestInitiatedHandshakeKeepsItsFailureReportTracked`,
`TestUnsecuredRetransmitEvictionWakesItsWaiter` and
`TestUnsecuredRetransmitEntryKeepsItsSchedule`. Register row above; the
row closes when matter.js bounds what an unauthenticated peer can park.

### BD-Matter-OTAImage-DownloadBound — an OTA image download is bounded by `MaxImageSize`

matter.js fetches an OTA image with a timeout as its only limit
(`packages/protocol/src/dcl/DclOtaUpdateService.ts:690-693` at `db021da0`),
hands the response body to `store` (`:703`) and streams it to storage
(`:571`) before the stored file is verified (`:573-574`).
`dcl.OTAVersions.Download` (`dcl/ota.go`) refuses a ledger record
that announces more than `MaxImageSize` before the request, and cuts an
answer without an announced size one byte past the bound; both are an
`*OTAError` matching `ErrOTAImageTooLarge`. The default,
`DefaultMaxImageSize`, is 256 MiB: owner decision 11 of review II — a
judgement, no image sizes were measured — and a host sets its own.
connectedhomeip has no DCL image download to follow. The bound matters more
here than it would in matter.js because this module buffers the image and
hands the store a slice (`controller/softwareupdate/images.go`), where
matter.js streams; streaming to the store changes the public `Blobs`
interface and is left to the architecture phase. Review II, R2-P0-bound-C01
and W4-ctlint-02. Pinned by `dcl:TestOTADownloadBoundedByMaxImageSize`
and `controller/softwareupdate:TestImagesHonourTheLedgersMaxImageSize`; the
default bound cutting an unannounced 256 MiB stream is not tested. Register
row above; the row closes when matter.js bounds the download.

### BD-Matter-BTP-InFlightBound — a BTP session holds at most 64 delivered messages in flight

matter.js's BLE peripheral starts `handleIncomingBleData` for every write
without waiting for it
(`packages/nodejs-ble/src/BlenoBleServer.ts:268` at `b25ed960`), the BTP
session awaits the message callback
(`packages/protocol/src/ble/BtpSessionHandler.ts:356`), and that callback
calls the listener and returns without waiting for it
(`BlenoBleServer.ts:316-322`). No count limits the messages handed on at
this layer; what the listener's side does with them was not read
(unverified). In this module the receiver of a BTP session
(`bridge/ble.go`, `connReceiverMaxInFlight` = 64) takes a slot before it
queues a message and waits at 64 until a handler returns or the receiver
closes, so the central's next write is not consumed; nothing is dropped and
the connection is not closed. The number and the mechanism are this
module's own, those of its TCP connection (`transport/tcp/conn.go`,
`maxInFlightPerConn`); connectedhomeip's handling was not read (unverified),
and how a BLE stack behaves while a write waits was not measured against a
real central. Review II, R2-P0-bound-E05. Pinned by
`bridge:TestConnReceiverBoundsTheMessagesInFlight` and
`TestConnReceiverCloseEndsAWaitingDelivery`. Register row above; the row
closes when matter.js bounds the messages of a BTP session it has not
finished.

### BD-Matter-BTP-WindowZeroRefused — a BTP handshake that states a window size of 0 is refused on both roles

matter.js accepts the value: its peripheral answers with
`Math.min(MatterBle.BTP_MAXIMUM_WINDOW_SIZE, clientWindowSize)`
(`packages/protocol/src/ble/BtpSessionHandler.ts:123` at `b25ed960`), which
is 0 for a request that states 0, and its central hands the response's
`windowSize` to the session unchecked (`:180-191`). What a matter.js session
with a window of 0 then does was not traced (unverified). connectedhomeip
refuses on both roles — `VerifyOrReturnError(req.mWindowSize > 0,
CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT)` for the request (`src/ble/BLEEndPoint.cpp:1014`
at `6170af84`) and the same for the response (`:1081`) — and the error
closes the end point (`:1151-1152`, `:1160-1169`, `:1294-1297`).
`transport/btp` follows connectedhomeip: `NewPeripheral` writes no response,
calls the disconnect callback and returns a `*ProtocolError`; `NewCentral`
returns a `*ProtocolError` and its callers drop the connection
(`transport/btp/session.go`). Deliberate: a peer whose window is 0 can never
be sent a packet, and the device is a BLE peripheral since ADR 0031 (owner
decision 1 of review II, W1-wire-07). One difference from connectedhomeip in
*when*: it refuses on the write of the request ("a peripheral receiving a
capabilities request write", `:1154-1160`), where this module parses the
kept request at the subscription, as matter.js does
(`packages/nodejs-ble/src/BlenoBleServer.ts:258-263`, `:299`). Pinned by
`transport/btp:TestBtpSessionRefusesZeroWindowRequest`,
`TestBtpSessionRefusesZeroWindowResponse`, `TestAcceptRefusesZeroWindow`
and, for a window of 1 on both roles, `TestBtpSessionAcceptsSmallestWindow`.
Retire when matter.js refuses a window of 0.

### BD-chip-StatusIB-EightBitStatus — the client-side decoders refuse a StatusIB status that does not fit 8 bits

matter.js declares both StatusIB fields as `TlvEnum<Status>()`
(`packages/types/src/protocol/types/TlvStatus.ts:15-16` at `b25ed960`; the
first carries the comment "8Bit"), and `TlvEnum` is `TlvUInt32`
(`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvNumber.ts:302-303`, "We use internally 32bit
here"), so a status above 255 decodes to its number (inferred from the two
schemas; not run). connectedhomeip reads `Status` into an
`enum class Status : uint8_t`
(`src/protocols/interaction_model/StatusCode.h:43` at `6170af84`) and
`ClusterStatus` into a `uint8_t` (`src/lib/core/DataModelTypes.h:33`), both
through `TLVReader::Get` (`src/app/MessageDef/StatusIB.cpp:54-60`,
`src/lib/core/TLVReader.h:531-538`), which answers
`CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_INTEGER_VALUE` for a value that does not fit
(`src/lib/core/TLVReader.cpp:204-214`). `im.statusIBField` (`im/status.go`),
which both StatusIB readers of the client side use, refuses the wider value
as connectedhomeip does. Deliberate: this module's `StatusCode` is 8 bits
wide, and before `30abc8f6` the wider value was masked — a status 0x100
read as Success. The event priority of an EventDataIB is held to 8 bits
the same way (`im/client.go`), where matter.js again declares a `TlvEnum`
(`packages/types/src/protocol/types/TlvEventData.ts:21`); connectedhomeip's
width for it was not read (unverified). Review II, R2-P0-wire-A05. Pinned
by `im:TestClientDecodersRefuseOutOfRangeIntegers` and
`TestClientDecodersKeepTheWholeRange`. Retire when matter.js refuses a
status above 8 bits, or when this module's status type holds 32.

### BD-Matter-SetupCode-ErrorOmitsPasscode — an error for a refused passcode names the rule, not the value

matter.js prints the value: `assertValidPasscode` throws
``Invalid passcode ${passcode}``
(`packages/types/src/schema/PairingCodeSchema.ts:181-185` at `b25ed960`),
and four of its tests expect "Invalid passcode 12345678"
(`packages/types/test/schema/PairingCodeSchemaTest.ts:163-165`, `:170`,
`:420-422`, `:427`). The errors of `secure/setup` for a passcode that is
zero, above 99999998 or one of the disallowed values name the rule
(`secure/setup/setup.go`, `passcodeRule`), and the ported assertions expect
the text without the value
(`secure/setup/pairing_code_schema_parity_matterjs_test.go`). Deliberate: an
error text reaches logs and a controller's diagnostics, and a disallowed
passcode is still the passcode of the device that ships with it. The same
rule holds for this module's own checks, which have no matter.js text to
depart from: `node`'s configuration and window checks, the PASE responder
(`commissioning.ErrPASEInvalidPasscode`) and the example commands. Review
II, R2-P0-sec-E04. Pinned by `secure/setup:TestErrorsDoNotRenderThePasscode`
and `commissioning/pase_error_text_test.go`. Retire when matter.js's text
drops the value.

### BD-Matter-WildcardFabricScopedWriteWithoutFabric — a wildcard-endpoint write of a fabric-scoped attribute without an accessing fabric is skipped without a status

On a concrete path both references answer UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS, and this
module mirrors matter.js: `if (limits.fabricScoped && !this.session.fabric)`
(`packages/protocol/src/action/server/AttributeWriteResponse.ts:248-251` at
`db021da0`; connectedhomeip `src/app/WriteHandler.cpp:804-812` at
`6170af84`, for a fabric-scoped list). On a wildcard-endpoint path
matter.js has no accessing-fabric check: `#writeAttributeForWildcard`
tests writable (`:331-333`), the write privilege (`:335-341`), timed
(`:343-345`) and a write in progress (`:355-358`) and then calls
`writeValue` (`:360`), which assigns the decoded value to the behaviour's
state (`:434`) and turns a thrown status error into a status entry for the
resolved path (`:452-458`). The enforcer's "No accessing fabric" refusal
covers a fabric-sensitive attribute only
(`packages/protocol/src/action/server/AccessControl.ts:314`, `:358-365`),
and the assignment runs the fabric-scoped list merge
(`packages/node/src/behavior/state/managed/values/StructManager.ts:243-265`)
through a proxy that treats an entry without a fabric index as visible and
fills in the session's (`ListManager.ts:480-481`, `:533`). **What matter.js
answers there per attribute and per value is not established (unverified):**
the path was read, not run — the pinned export has no build — and the
behaviours' own reactions were not traced to the end. connectedhomeip does
not model the case: a unicast write needs a concrete path
(`src/app/WriteHandler.cpp:353-354`), and a path without an endpoint exists
for group writes only (`ProcessGroupAttributeDataIBs`, `:434`); which status
the failure at `:353-354` maps to was not read (unverified). `im`'s write
gate (`im/write.go`) skips the attribute without a status, like every other
gate of the wildcard path, and no cluster server sees the write. Deliberate:
following matter.js would hand a fabric-less write to the cluster servers
again, the class owner decision 14 of review II closed (R2-P0-test-B09).
Pinned by `im:TestWriteFabricScopedGateOrder`. Retire when what matter.js
answers is established and mirrored, or when matter.js gates the wildcard
path.

### BD-chip-TimedRequestsBounded — a session may leave at most 8 timed interactions waiting

matter.js keeps a timed interaction as a timer on its exchange
(`packages/protocol/src/protocol/MessageExchange.ts:272`, `:1066-1084` at
`db021da0`): a second TimedRequest on the same exchange is refused
(`:1067-1070`) — as the bridge refuses it since review II, INVALID_ACTION
with the running window ended (`bridge/receive_dispatch.go:882-892`,
R2-P4-imwrite-16) — and nothing counts the exchanges of a session that hold
one. matter.js does bound the open exchanges of a secure session, at 30,
and closes the least recently active one beyond it
(`packages/protocol/src/protocol/ExchangeManager.ts:63`, `:551-566`,
`:578-596` at `db021da0`), and an exchange that closes stops its timer
(`MessageExchange.ts:1212`); that this holds a session's waiting timed
interactions at 30 is inferred from those lines, not run. The bridge keeps a deadline per (session, exchange) and
answers the TimedRequest past `maxPendingTimedRequests` = 8 pending ones of
a session with Busy, registering no deadline (`bridge/exchange_routing.go`,
`Bridge.dispatchTimedRequest` in `bridge/receive_dispatch.go`); before
`b1d4dd36` a session could register one entry per exchange id until the
deadlines ran out. The number and the answer are connectedhomeip's:
`CHIP_IM_MAX_NUM_TIMED_HANDLER` 8 (`src/lib/core/CHIPConfig.h:1010-1011` at
`6170af84`), the pool `ObjectPool<TimedHandler, CHIP_IM_MAX_NUM_TIMED_HANDLER>`
(`src/app/InteractionModelEngine.h:669`) and `Status::Busy` when it gives no
handler (`src/app/InteractionModelEngine.cpp:963-973`). Two differences,
both this module's: connectedhomeip's pool is the engine's one pool, the
bound here is per session, so one session cannot use up another's; and
connectedhomeip's number binds only where its pools are static (with
`CHIP_SYSTEM_CONFIG_POOL_USE_HEAP` "the ObjectPool size parameter is
ignored", `src/lib/support/Pool.h:619-626`; Linux and Darwin set it,
`src/platform/Linux/SystemPlatformConfig.h:41`,
`src/platform/Darwin/SystemPlatformConfig.h:39`). Review II, W2-conc-12.
Pinned by `bridge:TestTimedRequestsOfOneSessionAreBounded`. Register row
above; the row closes when matter.js bounds the timed interactions a
session may leave waiting.

### BD-Matter-ClientNode-StartAdoptsFilterBeforeOnline — a client node adopts the default subscription's fabric filter before it goes online, within the caller's context

matter.js's `NetworkClient.startup` binds the peer's signals first — four
`reactTo` calls on the peer
(`packages/node/src/behavior/system/network/NetworkClient.ts:85-88` at
`b25ed960`) — and then awaits, as one reaction on its `subscriptionChanges`
mutex, `#adoptFabricFilter()` followed by `#syncAutoSubscribe()`
(`:93-98`). `#adoptFabricFilter` awaits
`structure.adoptFabricFilter(fabricFiltered)` and hands it no abort signal
and no timeout (`:280-298`, the call at `:284`); what
`ClientStructure.adoptFabricFilter` waits for inside was not read
(unverified). `controller/client`'s `Node.start`
(`controller/client/node.go`) turns the order around: under `subSync` it
first calls `adoptDefaultFabricFilter(ctx)`, which waits within `ctx` for
the node's queued report jobs — their store writes and hooks — and only
then marks the node started, restarts the persister, observes the peer and
syncs the default subscription. When `ctx` ends while jobs are still
queued — a hook that blocks, the queue a `Stop` that timed out left
behind — `Start` returns `ctx`'s error and has started nothing: the node is
not started, no signal of the peer is bound, the cache keeps its fabric
filter, and a later `Start` starts it. Reason: a Go caller bounds `Start`
by its context, and in matter.js's order a `Start` that gave up in the
adoption would leave bound signals behind to be taken back; with the
adoption first there is nothing to take back. Unchanged from matter.js: a
storage failure of the adoption is logged and is not `Start`'s error
(`:285-297`; `adoptDefaultFabricFilter`, `controller/client/network.go`).
Review II, the follow-up of R2-P0-conc-C03 (`5efceca2`); the citation of
matter.js's order in the code is R2-P0-rv-C03's (`a0a0d818`). Pinned by
`controller/client:TestStartReturnsWithItsContextWhileAHookBlocks`. Retire
when matter.js's start takes an abort signal, or adopts before it binds.

### BD-Matter-Bridge-StartDuringStopRefused — a `Bridge` is single-run: a `Start` during or after `Stop` is refused with `ErrStopped`

matter.js's node is restarted: "Once the node is offline you may use
{@link start} to bring the node online again"
(`packages/node/src/node/Node.ts:191` at `b25ed960`), `start` and `stop`
running one after the other on the lifecycle's mutex (`:123`, `:195`). Its
`start()` returns at once, without an error and without starting, while
`lifecycle.isOnline` holds or another start is in progress (`:114-117`),
and `isOnline` holds until the `offline` event has cleared it
(`packages/node/src/node/NodeLifecycle.ts:35-37`, `:52-54`), which the
network runtime emits at the end of its own stop
(`packages/node/src/behavior/system/network/NetworkRuntime.ts:69-77`). So,
by these lines, a `start()` during a `stop()` that has not yet emitted
`offline` resolves as if the node were online and the node ends offline;
one that arrives after it waits for the stop and starts the node. Read,
not run: the pinned export has no build, and which awaits of
`cancelWithMutex` that window spans was not traced (unverified).
`bridge.Bridge` is single-run (review II, R2-P2-stop-05, owner decision
40, which answers the restart question this entry left open): from the
first `Stop` on, `Bridge.Start` returns `ErrStopped` (`bridge/bridge.go`,
`claimStart`) — also for a `Start` that arrives while the `Stop` still
runs, which until `91172715` was refused with `ErrAlreadyStarted` — and a
host that comes back builds a new bridge, as it builds a new `node.Node`
(`node.ErrStopped`, `BD-Matter-FactoryResetEndsTheNode`). Reason: `Stop`
closes what the bridge holds, the advertiser among it, and a second run on
those parts published no operational record; one object with one run has
no state of an ended run to carry into the next, and the caller is told
that nothing was started, where matter.js's early return tells it nothing.
A `Start` that failed leaves the bridge startable. Pinned by
`bridge:TestStartAfterStopIsRefused` and
`bridge:TestStartDuringStopIsRefused`. Retire when the owner reopens a
bridge's restart.

### BD-chip-ChunkedWritesBounded — a session may hold at most four chunked writes open; the hold is taken once the access check grants the write, per fabric for a fabric-scoped attribute

matter.js takes the hold of a chunked write's attribute "before any await" (`packages/node/src/node/server/InteractionServer.ts:538-543` at `db021da0`) — before the batch that checks access runs (`:548`, the batch's write at `:493`) — under a key of endpoint, cluster and attribute with no fabric in it (`writePathKey`, `:86-88`), in one map for the node (`#writingExchanges`, `:180`); a concrete path another exchange holds is answered Busy before anything else (`:505-509`, `#isHeldByOther`, `:211-214`); it releases all but the last accepted path when more chunks follow (`:555-561`) and the rest when `handleWriteRequest` leaves its scope (`:460-469`); nothing at these lines counts the chunked writes a session holds open. matter.js bounds the open exchanges of a secure session at 30 and closes the least recently active one beyond it (`packages/protocol/src/protocol/ExchangeManager.ts:63`, `:551-566`, `:578-596` at `db021da0`); what that close does to a chunked write on the exchange was not read (unverified).
