### BD-chip-SubscriptionFloorAfterPriming — what is outstanding when priming ends waits for MinIntervalFloor, as connectedhomeip

matter.js sends at once what is outstanding when a subscription is activated: `activate` (`packages/node/src/node/server/ServerSubscription.ts:412`) calls `#triggerSendUpdate()` when an update is outstanding (`:441-445` at `db021da0`), with no floor (`:520-528`). connectedhomeip holds MinIntervalFloor from the establishment: priming done → `SendSubscribeResponse`, `mObserver->OnSubscriptionEstablished(this)` (`src/app/ReadHandler.cpp:249-259` at `6170af84`); the scheduler creates the node with `now` (`src/app/reporting/ReportSchedulerImpl.cpp:93-111`) and sets `mMinTimestamp = now + minInterval` (`ReportScheduler.h:103-110`, `:141-147`); `IsReportableNow` needs `now >= GetMinTimestamp()` unless an engine run is scheduled (`:120-125`); a dirty handler inside the floor is scheduled for the floor's end (`ReportSchedulerImpl.cpp:190-204`), and an urgent event waits too (`src/app/reporting/Engine.cpp:1234`, "once reporting is not blocked by the min interval"). `ShouldReportUnscheduled` (`Engine.cpp:922`, `ReadHandler.cpp:652`) was not read. The module keeps chip's floor: `Subscription.EndPriming` (`im/subscription/subscription.go`) stamps `lastReport` with the end of the priming report and marks the events fired meanwhile urgent, so the changes and events of the priming window go out once MinIntervalFloor has elapsed since the priming report. Why chip here, though matter.js models it: the subscriber asked for the floor, and honouring it is what the controllers' own stack does. The cost: a change made during priming arrives up to MinIntervalFloor later than from a matter.js device. Pinned by the subtest "an event fired while the subscription was priming is reported after the floor" of `im/subscription:TestEventReportParityMatterJS`. Review II, F-db021da0-4, R2-P6-par-0779, owner decision 144. Retire when the owner follows matter.js.

### BD-Matter-PersistedSubscriptionsBounded — persisted subscription rows are bounded per peer and per fabric

matter.js removes a persisted subscription only when the subscription is terminated (`packages/node/src/behavior/system/subscriptions/SubscriptionsServer.ts:168-186` at `b25ed960`), appends per peer (`#addSubscription`, `:160-165`), and clears the store after the load at start (`:227-230`): no bound within a run. Here the persisted rows are bounded (`bridge/subscription_persistence.go` `boundPersistedSubscriptionsLocked`): a peer that subscribes with KeepSubscriptions=false loses its rows whose subscription is not live, and a fabric keeps at most its subscription quota of rows — the manager's `MaxSubscriptionsPerFabric` (`im/subscription`) —, the oldest not-live first. A live subscription's row is never dropped, and a row of another fabric is never touched; within one fabric the cap may drop another peer's not-live row (the cut of owner decision 134). The order the cap relies on is the store port's contract. Review II, R2-P6-bound-0502, owner decisions 134 and 175. Pinned by `bridge:TestKeepSubscriptionsFalseForgetsThePeersFormerRows` and `TestPersistedRowsAreCappedAtTheManagersQuota`. Register row above.

### BD-Matter-Subscription-RefusedReportEnds — a peer that refuses a report ends the subscription, and nothing more is sent to it

The closing flush of a subscription whose report in flight failed sends nothing, as matter.js (`#flush` `:753-763` from `#cancel` only, `:825`; the catch returns for a closed subscription, `:558-562`). Review II, R2-P6-par-0702 (b); (a) is mirrored.

### BD-chip-LargeMessageGateEnforced — a Large Message command on a session without large messages answers INVALID_TRANSPORT_TYPE, as matter.js; chip's same gate is inert for its code-driven clusters

matter.js answers a command whose model quality is Large Message ("L") INVALID_TRANSPORT_TYPE (0xD1) when the session carries no large messages (`packages/protocol/src/action/server/CommandInvokeResponse.ts:281-285` at `db021da0`; the quality from the model, `packages/protocol/src/action/server/AccessControl.ts:527`; a UDP or BLE session carries none, a TCP one does, `packages/general/src/net/udp/UdpTransport.ts:69`, `packages/protocol/src/ble/Ble.ts:39`, `packages/protocol/src/transport/tcp/TcpChannel.ts:45`), and the module does the same (`refusesLargeMessage`, `im/invoke.go`; F-db021da0-29, closed). connectedhomeip's engine carries the same gate with the same status (`src/app/InteractionModelEngine.cpp:1875-1884` at `6170af84`) but sets the flag only on the ember path (`src/data-model-providers/codegen/CodegenDataModelProvider.cpp:66`) and in the example shim (`examples/common/server-cluster-shim/ServerClusterShim.cpp:144`): its metadata generator does not emit it (`scripts/py_matter_idl/matter/idl/generators/cpp/sdk/sdk_generator.py:62`, "TODO: kLargeMessage is not available"), so FindTransport's entry is kFabricScoped and kOperate only (`zzz_generated/app-common/clusters/PushAvStreamTransport/Metadata.h:79-81`) and no generated `Metadata.h` carries the flag, so the gate fires for none of the seven clusters whose "L" request commands the snapshot lists (`schema/large_message_gen.go`), all code-driven in chip at the pin. The module therefore departs from chip's observable behaviour on the 21 "L" commands the reference daemon serves (all but CommodityPrice's under `--camera-sim` or `--tls-sim`) — CommodityPrice GetDetailedForecastRequest, CameraAvStreamManagement CaptureSnapshot, WebRtcTransportProvider's five, PushAvStreamTransport AllocatePushTransport and FindTransport, TlsCertificateManagement's nine, TlsClientManagement's three. A CHIP case meets it where its TH sends such a command without a large-payload session: TC-PAVST-2.8 step 4 has TH2, a fresh fabric commissioned on-network, send FindTransport with MRP_PAYLOAD and expects NOT_FOUND (`src/python_testing/TC_PAVST_2_8.py:179-189`, `TC_PAVSTTestBase.py:352-368`, `matter_testing.py:3105`); chip's camera-app, which chip's CI runs the case against (`TC_PAVST_2_8.py:21-36`), answers NOT_FOUND there from the fabric-scoped lookup (`src/app/clusters/push-av-stream-transport-server/PushAVStreamTransportLogic.cpp:1576-1585`) only because the gate is inert. The harness runs the case and requires that failure (`internal/chiptool` PAVST `failsAs`, class (c) on `docs/certifiability.md`). Marker, re-read at every harness pin lift: `sdk_generator.py:62` and `Metadata.h:79-81` — once chip emits the flag, its own DUT is expected to answer 0xD1 to the step as written (inferred from `InteractionModelEngine.cpp:1880-1883`, not run), and the step is chip's to fix. Reasoning: the gate is one rule generated from the model's quality and enforced where matter.js enforces it, whereas an exemption "as chip" would switch it off on every served "L" command and tie the module's wire behaviour to how chip registers a cluster at a pin. Review II, owner decision 183; an upstream report is drafted, not filed. Pinned by `im:TestInvokeLargeMessageGate` and `TestInvokeLargeMessageGateOrder`.

### BD-Matter-Controller-StoredCANeverReplaced — a stored CA or fabric record is never replaced

### BD-Matter-Binding-CreatedPeerReleased — the binding manager stops the connection process of a peer it created when the node's last entry goes

matter.js connects a binding's peer through `PeerSet.for(peerAddress)` and `peer.connect()` (`packages/node/src/behaviors/binding/BindingManager.ts:584-585` at `b25ed960`), and an entry's removal only cancels its pending notification (`#clearPending`, `:613-627`): nothing releases the peer. connectedhomeip only removes the pending notification when a binding goes (`src/app/clusters/bindings/BindingManager.cpp:36-40` at `6170af84`), asks for a session per binding (`:86`) and releases sessions at the fabric's removal only (`:141-149`); it has no peer object with a standing connection process (inferred), so it releases nothing either, but has nothing standing to leak. Here (`binding/resolve.go` `trackCreated`, `releaseUnbound`) the binding manager records, by node address, the peers it created for a client entry: the set held none for the node before. Each binding period runs from the first entry naming the node to the moment its last entry goes. At the end of a period the entries' Connect calls are cancelled and waited for, then the peer's connection process is stopped (`Disconnect` without a cause). The peer stays in the set and is never closed, nor are its sessions, because another holder may use it. The record stays too, so a later entry for the node opens and ends a new period. Known window: `Has` then `For` are two calls, so a host that adds the peer between them has it counted as the manager's. Review II, R2-P6-bound-2104, owner decisions 207, 221. Pinned by `binding:TestPeerCreatedForAnEntryIsReleasedWithItsLastEntry`, `TestPeerCreatedIsReleasedEveryBindingPeriod`, `TestReleaseWaitsForTheEntriesConnectCalls`, `TestReleaseStopsConnectingOnly`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js releases a peer it created.

The manager's record of a peer it created ends when the set no longer holds the node (the peer was closed) or holds another peer there; a new binding period connects only after the previous period's release ran (review II, R2-P6-bound-2104, wave 3).

Here (`client/interaction/subscriptions.go` `AddPeer`) a subscription displaced by one the peer granted the same id is closed at once with the timeout cause, so a sustained one re-establishes; closing at once rather than at its own MaxInterval is this module's choice, connectedhomeip's end is the later of the two. ### BD-Matter-SustainedSubscription-ShortLivedPaced — a peer that grants and drops a subscription at once is re-subscribed on a backoff

matter.js iterates its retry schedule anew in every establishment loop (`for (const retry of this.#retries)` inside the `while (true)` of `:139`, `packages/protocol/src/action/client/subscription/SustainedSubscription.ts:203` at `b25ed960`), and connectedhomeip resets its retry count at every SubscribeResponse (`mNumRetries = 0`, `src/app/ReadClient.cpp:1139` at `6170af84`), so a peer that grants and drops at once is re-subscribed with no spacing. Here (`client/interaction/sustained.go`) the attempts of one establishment run on a schedule that starts over with each establishment, as both references. A second backoff spans establishments for consecutive short-lived subscriptions only: one the peer drops before it lasted that backoff's current interval waits its next step before the re-subscribe, and one that lasted it resets the backoff. A peer that grants and drops at once is therefore spaced (15 s, doubling, up to an hour), and a subscription lost after an outage re-subscribes at once. The backoff is reset only by a subscription that lasted its current interval: after several quick drops (say six, interval 16 min) a subscription that then lasts 10 min and is lost waits 16 min and doubles again — the pacing rule working as written. Review II, R2-P6-fsm-2110, owner decision 207. Pinned by `client/interaction:TestSustainedRetryScheduleSpansEstablishments`, `TestSustainedRetryAfterAnOutageIsNotCarriedOver`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js spaces the re-subscriptions of a peer that drops at once.

### BD-Matter-PeerMonitor-SuspectRunsItsOwnProbe — a session-suspect check never takes an address-change run's result

matter.js starts one address-monitor run and hands it to every caller, whatever its reason (`if (this.#probing === undefined) { this.#probing = this.#run(options.reason)…`, `packages/protocol/src/peer/PeerAddressMonitor.ts:111-112` at `b25ed960`, and `:122`). A set and supported active value is kept (`UnitLocalizationServer.ts:24-27`, `LocalizationConfigurationServer.ts:22-25`, `TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:29-32`); any other start becomes Celsius if listed, else the list's first (`UnitLocalizationServer.ts:29-31`, `:37`), or the detected value if listed, else the list's first (`LocalizationConfigurationServer.ts:27-28`, `:32`; `TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:34-41`), with a warning when one was set (`UnitLocalizationServer.ts:32-36`, `LocalizationConfigurationServer.ts:29-31`, `TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:36-40`). go-fabric (`cluster/core/unit_localization.go`, `localization_configuration.go`, `time_format_localization.go`) starts as matter.js when nothing is configured — a nil TemperatureUnit, an empty or nil list (`len(list) == 0`, matter.js's `!list?.length`) — with three differences. (1) An explicitly configured active value its list lacks is refused with `ErrLocalizationConfig` instead of replaced. (2) A detected value is the host's, passed as the configured one: LocalizationConfiguration with a list and no ActiveLocale starts at the list's first, where matter.js prefers the detected locale when the list holds it (`LocalizationConfigurationServer.ts:27-28`); a detected locale passed as ActiveLocale counts as configured, so the scenario of `LocalizationConfigurationServerTest.ts:120-127` with the detected locale passed in is refused here and the host leaves the field empty instead; TimeFormatLocalization the same since decision 358: an unset (nil) ActiveCalendarType with a list starts at the list's first, where matter.js prefers its detected calendar when listed (`TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:34-35`). (3) With neither an ActiveLocale nor a list Go refuses, where matter.js seeds `[detected]` from its own detection (`LocalizationConfigurationServer.ts:17-20`, `:37`): detection is the host's. TimeFormatLocalization likewise refuses an unset calendar without a list (matter.js `[detected]`, `TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:24-28`) and an unset HourFormat (matter.js `detectedHourFormat`, `:18-20`; decision 358). (4) Without CalendarFormat (`NoFeatures`, decision 359) matter.js's initialize returns before the calendar part (`TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:21-23`) and does not look at calendar state; here a calendar configured beside `NoFeatures`, an ActiveCalendarType or a SupportedCalendarTypes list, is refused with `ErrLocalizationConfig`. HourFormat stays required. What matter.js does with calendar state handed to a server without the feature beyond initialize is unverified. The `cluster/core` constructors hold no stored value; the node facade's own stored values are restored after construction through `SetAttributes`, and one the list lacks is not applied (`node/nonvolatile.go` restore), which is matter.js's outcome for a stale stored value (pinned by `node:TestLocalizationConfigurationStoredParityMatterJS`, `TestUnitLocalizationStoredParityMatterJS`, `TestTimeFormatLocalizationStoredParityMatterJS`). The node facade starts TimeFormatLocalization at the host's `Config.TimeFormat`, nil being 24Hr and [Gregorian] (`node/config.go` TimeFormatConfig.core, `node/root.go` buildRootOptional), where matter.js would detect both (`TimeFormatLocalizationServer.ts:18-20`, `:24-28`); the node passes the host's start to the server unchanged (decision 360), and the stale-calendar fallback with a configured list is pinned by `node:TestTimeFormatConfigStoredParityMatterJS`. Reason (decisions 289, 296): the constructor's configuration is the host's explicit statement, so a contradiction is the host's to resolve, not the server's to paper over. Pinned by `cluster/core:TestUnitLocalizationServerParityMatterJS`, `TestLocalizationConfigurationServerParityMatterJS`, `TestTimeFormatLocalizationServerStartParityMatterJS` and `TestTimeFormatLocalizationServerParityMatterJS` ("starts without the CalendarFormat feature" and the three Go refusals of an unset HourFormat, of neither calendar nor list, and of a calendar beside NoFeatures).

### BD-Matter-Thermostat-ControlSequenceFromFeatures — ControlSequenceOfOperation follows the features; no reheat sequences, no automatic mode management

matter.js keeps the sequence rules in `packages/node/src/behaviors/thermostat/ControlSequence.ts` at `b25ed960` (05645e839, #5000): the sequences without heating are CoolingOnly and CoolingWithReheat (`:9-12`), those without cooling HeatingOnly and HeatingWithReheat (`:14-17`); `allowsSystemMode` (`:41-46`) refuses the heating modes Heat and EmergencyHeat (`:19`) and the cooling modes Cool and Precooling (`:21`) where the sequence forbids them. A SystemMode write it refuses is CONSTRAINT_ERROR (`ThermostatServer.ts:1104`, `:1119-1128`), as is a ThermostatRunningMode change (`:1105`, `:1108-1117`). The sequence is the endpoint's configured start value: a controller's write is accepted and reverted (`:292`, `:1099-1102`, `:1130-1132`). The opt-in automatic mode management (`useAutomaticModeManagement`, default false, `:3148`, doc `:230-233`) sets the running mode from the temperature in Auto, Off where the sequence forbids the direction (`:1735-1742`). The Go server derives the sequence from the features — HEAT and COOL CoolingAndHeating, COOL alone CoolingOnly, else HeatingOnly (`cluster/thermo/thermostat_server.go` `controlSequenceOfOperation`) — accepts a write and stores nothing, and has no automatic mode management: in Auto the running mode is the host's (`SetThermostatRunningMode`). For the three sequences it serves, the definition's per-feature SystemMode check refuses what `allowsSystemMode` refuses, and the running-mode setter is feature-gated alike; the reheat sequences cannot be stated. Reason (coordinator decision C-3 of pin-lift wave P1, the verdict on F-b25ed960-22): no served behaviour differs for a derivable sequence, and no consumer has asked to state a reheat device; a `ThermostatConfig` field for the sequence would make the three refusal cases portable — an owner decision, not taken. Left: ThermostatBehaviorTest.ts's describe "ControlSequenceOfOperation" (six cases, describe `:241-328`).

### BD-Matter-Thermostat-Suggestions-Seams — ThermostatSuggestions without matter.js's protected seams, on the node's Matter time

matter.js lets an application replace `hasSynchronizedTime` (`packages/node/src/behaviors/thermostat/ThermostatServer.ts:701-707` at `b25ed960`), `selectThermostatSuggestion` (`:727-733`) and `suggestionNotFollowingReason` (`:750-757`), and override `handleSetActivePresetRequest` (`:523-538`); it retries a re-evaluation from the timer whose follow failed and rolled back after 10 s, doubling up to 15 min, only while a stored entry is due (`:75-78`, `:2512-2519`, `:2515`). The Go server (`cluster/thermo/suggestions.go`) applies matter.js's defaults as fixed behaviour — the earliest EffectiveTime (`:730-733`), OngoingHold during a hold (`:753-755`) —, takes the host's own reasons through `SetAttributes` where matter.js's application overrides the reason method, and does not retry: following runs SetActivePresetRequest's path on the Sink, a refusal is logged (`matter.thermostat.suggestion_not_followed`) and the next re-evaluation tries again. Four further differences. (1) The time base: matter.js compares EffectiveTime and ExpirationTime with the host clock ("Either way the host clock (Time.nowMs) is the time that EffectiveTime and ExpirationTime are compared with", `:689-691`), a TimeSynchronization cluster answering only whether the time is synchronised (`:701-707`). Here the time is the node's TimeSynchronization UTC, value and synchronised flag both (`AttachMatterTime`), so SetUTCTime moves what is due and every adopted time re-evaluates through `MatterTimeChanged`; a jump back before the current suggestion's EffectiveTime takes its current status away while the preset it activated stays active. The wire values are equal: matter.js holds Unix seconds and `TlvEpochS` converts to the Matter epoch (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvNumber.ts:369-386`). (2) A follow that fails inside a command: matter.js catches a failed follow only on the timer (`:2392-2406`); in AddThermostatSuggestion or RemoveThermostatSuggestion the re-evaluation is not wrapped (`:644`, `:659`, `:2382`), so the command fails and its transaction rolls back. Here the failure (of the Sink or the PresetStore) is logged, the command succeeds and the entry is current with a null reason and its preset not active — read from the code, no matter.js test covers it. (3) The timer runs in whole seconds (coordinator decision C-10): matter.js arms it for the due second in milliseconds minus the wall clock in milliseconds (`:2373`, `:2510-2511`, `:2524-2528`), firing as the due second begins on the host clock; the Matter time port carries whole epoch seconds (`clock.MatterTime`, `clock/mattertime.go`), so `armSuggestionTimerLocked` arms whole seconds from the instant it read the time and the timer fires within the due second — under one second late, never early; within that part of a second a read still lists an expired entry or does not yet show a due one as current. Measuring the sub-second offset is not performable from the port without assuming that the Matter time's second boundary equals the clock's, and a sub-second port would be an exported change of `clock.MatterTime`, which the Valve and every host's attach share. (4) MaxThermostatSuggestions is 5 when the configuration names none; the model's constraint is `min 5` (`packages/model/src/standard/elements/thermostat-cluster.element.ts:265-266`), and where matter.js's default comes from was not read (unverified). The Go server has no transaction to roll back (the js-runtime-only rows of the register's ThermostatSuggestionsTest.ts entry). Reason: one configuration seam per input instead of overridable methods, and the Matter time the node serves on the wire as the one time base. The stored list and override (`ThermostatConfig.SuggestionStore`, `store.ThermostatSuggestionStore` on the Settings area), the application's write of ThermostatSuggestions (`SetAttributes`, the schema's constraints only, `ThermostatServer.ts:2290`, `:2296-2307`) and its activation of a preset with the setpoints (`ActivatePreset`, `:551-567`) follow matter.js since P2-G (decisions 316-318). A store that fails a save after the start is logged (`matter.thermostat.suggestions_not_saved`) and the change stays in memory, where matter.js's failed commit would roll the change back (unverified), and an entry the application writes that names no preset is current and its follow refused and logged — matter.js's follow throws in the writing transaction (`:529-531`, reached through `:2460`; the effect on the write unverified). `SetAttributes` returns before the save, which the scheduled re-evaluation makes; matter.js commits the list, the override and the evaluation in one transaction. Pinned by `cluster/thermo:TestParityMatterJS_ThermostatSuggestionsTest` (the by-design rows of that register entry).

### BD-Matter-Invoke-AbsentFieldsAsEmptyStruct — an InvokeRequest without CommandFields is read as one with an empty structure

An InvokeRequest whose CommandDataIB carries no CommandFields is decoded as one that carries an empty structure (`im/invoke.go` `readAbsentFields`), through the same fields reader: a command with a mandatory field answers INVALID_COMMAND, a command whose fields are all optional runs its handler, and a command without fields hands no payload on (`bridge/fields_definition.go` `decodeByDefinition`, as matter.js's `TlvVoid.ts:20-22`, `:28-29` at `b25ed960`). The three implementations answer differently. matter.js: its model gate reads an absent request as `{}` (`packages/node/src/node/integration/ProtocolService.ts:624-625` at `b25ed960`), so a model-validated command (DoorLock, `packages/node/src/behaviors/door-lock/DoorLockServer.ts:1515`; OperationalCredentials, `packages/node/src/behaviors/operational-credentials/OperationalCredentialsServer.ts:636`) answers absent fields through `onValidationError`; for the other commands its TLV check runs on undefined (`packages/protocol/src/action/server/CommandInvokeResponse.ts:549-551`) and `TlvObject.validate` reads a property of undefined (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvObject.ts:256`, before `:258` looks at `optional`) — a TypeError, answered FAILURE (`CommandInvokeResponse.ts:512`, `:518-520`), a command whose fields are all optional included; an explicit `{}` that lacks a mandatory field is INVALID_COMMAND (`TlvObject.ts:261`, `packages/types/src/common/ValidationError.ts:45-47`, `CommandInvokeResponse.ts:529-535`). connectedhomeip decodes an empty struct (`src/app/CommandHandlerImpl.cpp:497-500`, `:620-628` at `6170af84`) and runs the handler with default-initialised fields (`zzz_generated/app-common/clusters/OnOff/Commands.ipp:108-129`, END_OF_TLV → `CHIP_NO_ERROR` at `:115`; one generated cluster read, code-driven clusters unverified). This module follows matter.js's answer for `{}` and its gate's reading of an absent request, so absent and empty agree; with all fields optional it runs the handler, as chip does. A command of a cluster without a registered definition (and a command of OperationalCredentials, AccessControl or GroupKeyManagement that no hand reader decodes) whose CommandFields are absent reaches the server as the salvaged tag map of an empty structure: a nil `map[uint8]any` in a non-nil interface, where it was a nil interface. Correction of coordinator decision C-13 and of findings F-b25ed960-31: "absent = empty struct" is chip's rule; "a missing mandatory field → INVALID_COMMAND" is matter.js's answer for an explicit `{}` and this module's decoder, not chip's (chip runs the handler). Reason: one decode path for absent and empty CommandFields (owner decision 334). Pinned by `im:TestAbsentCommandFieldsReadAsAnEmptyStructure` and `bridge:TestAbsentCommandFieldsDecodeAsEmpty`.

### BD-chip-JointFabricAdministrator-AddICACResponds — AddICAC with a passing ICAC answers an ICACResponse with StatusCode OK

connectedhomeip answers an AddICAC whose ICAC passes with a SUCCESS status alone (`src/app/clusters/joint-fabric-administrator-server/joint-fabric-administrator-server.cpp:362`, `:383-390` at `6170af84`: a response only when a status is set, else `AddStatus`), against its own model, which answers the command with an ICACResponse ("responded in the form of an ICACResponse command", `controller-clusters.matter:13198-13199`) whose statusCode is not optional (`:13176-13178`); chip's generated Kotlin client throws on a response without statusCode (`JointFabricAdministratorCluster.kt:149-190`), and `TC_JFADMIN_1_2.py` checks no OK answer. matter.js's `JointFabricAdministratorServer.ts:14` at `b25ed960` is the empty generated subclass, no server logic, so the cluster's logic follows chip (`BD-chip-JointFabricAdministrator-RulesInServer`); the response rule is not cluster logic but the invoke engine's, which matter.js models for every cluster: an absent response is validated as `{}`, and a missing mandatory field is FAILURE (`packages/node/src/node/integration/ProtocolService.ts:624-625`, `:717-733` at `b25ed960`). Here that rule is the endpoint dispatcher's (`spec.CheckResponseAsWritten` after the server, as matter.js's `completeResponse` in `invokeCommand`, `:717-733`), for every server with a registered definition that a wire command reaches; a hand-written cluster/core response is judged as the bridge's response writer writes it — a field its definition makes mandatory that the written bytes lack is FAILURE (decision 343); so `cluster/jointfabric` answers AddICAC's success with `ICACResponse{StatusCode: OK}`. Reason: owner decision 340 — the response rule adopted without an exemption, under which chip's status-only success would answer FAILURE. Pinned by `cluster/jointfabric:TestAddICAC`.

### BD-Matter-Controller-PartsListSelfClaim — an endpoint whose PartsList names itself is placed below its other claimant

matter.js counts an endpoint whose PartsList names itself among its own claimants (`packages/node/src/node/client/ClientStructure.ts:1104-1113`, `:1409-1424` at `b25ed960`) and so never places it while its list names none of its other claimants: it is then the chosen owner (`:1607-1609`, `:1636-1643`), and an owner must be placed (`:1437`). No comment and no test of `ClientBridgeStructureTest.ts` covers it. In Go an endpoint is not its own claimant (`controller/client/structure.go` `placeParts`), so it is placed below its other claimant. Reason: review II R2-P2-alloc-01, an endpoint is never its own part; matter.js's outcome is an unhandled peer fault, not modelled behaviour (pin-lift unit P2-C's Fable verdict). Pinned by `controller/client:TestStructurePartsCycleRefused` ("an endpoint naming itself"). Retires when matter.js places an endpoint that names itself.

### BD-Matter-CASE-ResumeWaitSigma1Copies — a copy of the resuming Sigma1 does not fail the resumption's wait for the Success

While a resumed session waits for the initiator's Success, a copy of the Sigma1 that began the resumption does not fail it; any other message on the exchange does, a Sigma1 of other bytes included. matter.js recognises the copy by its message counter — a duplicate is acknowledged and not queued (`packages/protocol/src/protocol/ExchangeManager.ts:353-359`, `packages/protocol/src/protocol/MessageExchange.ts:514-524` at `b25ed960`), every other message fails `waitForSuccess` (`packages/protocol/src/securechannel/SecureChannelMessenger.ts:94-98`, `CaseServer.ts:207-210`): a copy under the same counter leaves the wait in both; the same bytes under a new counter leave it here while the Sigma1's record lives (a provider's adapter) and fail the resumption in matter.js. Through the singleton handler the record ends at the Sigma2_Resume's acknowledgement, after which such a copy fails the wait, as in matter.js. This module recognises the copy by its bytes (`markSigma1Replied`), since the router answers Sigma1 copies from its record across interfaces; whether Apple's copies carry one message counter was not read (unverified). Reason: one dedupe for the handshake's Sigma1, not a second one by counter. Pinned by `bridge:TestCASEResumeSecondSigma1FailsTheFirstWait`.

### BD-Matter-Client-ForgetFailedNode — `Registry.Forget` erases and drops a node that failed to load in one call

`controller/client.Registry.Forget` erases a node that failed to load and drops it from the registry in one call, including the protocol peer of its stored address. In matter.js at `b25ed960` no single call does both: `ClientNode.delete()` rejects for a crashed node (`packages/node/src/endpoint/Endpoint.ts:961-962`, the construction assert) and only deletes the protocol peer at its stored address in its `finally` (`packages/node/src/node/ClientNode.ts:251-263`); `node.erase()` (`ClientNode.ts:265-267`) erases the store and leaves the node in `Peers` — by its code, no test at the pin runs it on a crashed node; `Peers.erase()` drops undeletable nodes and leaves their persisted data (`packages/node/src/node/client/Peers.ts:509-531`). Every fabric operation refuses such a node with its load error, as matter.js's `#runFabricOperation` does (`Peers.ts:641`; decision 357), so nothing erases it as a side effect. Reason: a host needs one explicit way to drop a peer it cannot load. Pinned by `controller/client:TestDecommissionOfNodeThatFailedToLoad` (the `Forget` after the refusal) and `TestPeerAddressOfNodeThatFailedToLoad`. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P2b-K.

### BD-Matter-Controller-InboundReleaseAfterEveryHandler — an inbound unsecured session is released after every handler that ran on it

matter.js releases an inbound unsecured session in the `#onMessage` `finally` of the message that created it, when it is not closed or closing and holds no exchange (`packages/protocol/src/protocol/ExchangeManager.ts:244-256`, `:324-327` at `b25ed960`), or in the `finally` of the PASE or CASE handler that adopted it (`PaseServer.ts:112-113`, `CaseServer.ts:99-100`); a second message admitted on that session while the first handler was awaited releases nothing, so the entry stays until such a `finally` or shutdown (inferred from the code, not run). Here the session is released after every handler that ran on it (`client/exchange/manager.go` `receive`, `dispatch`, `answerBusy` → `releaseInbound`), since Go handlers run on goroutines of their own; the release takes the session out of the table under the lock that admits exchanges, and a message that found it released is received again on a new session. Reason: an unauthenticated peer's session is not left in the table beyond its handler by an interleaving; the 60 s lifetime (`BD-Matter-Controller-UnsecuredSessionLifetime`) is the other bound. Pinned by `client/exchange:TestCheckInReachesTheReceiver` and `TestInitiatingMessageOutlivesTheReleaseOfTheSessionItFound`. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P2b-L2 (coordinator decision C-26).

### BD-Matter-Subscription-KeepAliveNotDeferred — a keep-alive owed after a failure on the session a subscription left goes out under a deferral

A keep-alive owed by a report that failed on the session a subscription left goes out at once even under a deferral. matter.js breaks its resend loop while `#deferredUntil` holds (`packages/node/src/node/server/ServerSubscription.ts:618-621` at `b25ed960`) and sends nothing until the deferral ends; this engine holds data only, never the keep-alive (`im/subscription` `drainLocked`: `held` gates the data), as for every keep-alive. No other entry states the general rule that a deferral does not hold a keep-alive; this is its first statement. Reason: the subscriber's liveness timer does not wait on a deferral. Pinned by `im/subscription:TestServerSubscriptionSupersession` ("resends a keep-alive at once on its new session when it failed on the session it left", without a deferral; the deferred case has no test). Pin lift b25ed960, unit P2b-B.

### BD-Matter-Subscription-PrimingMovesWithItsSession — a subscription still priming moves with a superseded session and is announced

matter.js's `#follow` re-points a subscription's session to the newer one (`packages/node/src/node/server/ServerSubscription.ts:819-834` at `b25ed960`). This module counts a subscription that is still priming in its session's count (`im/subscription` `CountBySession`), so `Manager.MoveSession` moves priming and established subscriptions alike and fires the change hook for both session ids when anything moved; matter.js re-points only the session. Reason: the per-session count the device's diagnostics read stays true across a move. Pinned by `im/subscription:TestServerSubscriptionSupersession` ("follows a newer session set up while its initial report is sent"). Pin lift b25ed960, unit P2b-B.

### BD-Matter-ZoneManagement-LastZoneIdHostPersisted — the last assigned zone ID is the host's

matter.js keeps the ID it assigned last as the server's nonvolatile state `lastZoneId` (`packages/node/src/behaviors/zone-management/ZoneManagementServer.ts:253-260` at `b25ed960`), written with the zone (`:96-105`) and continued from (`:243-250`). Here the zones are the host's to persist, so the last ID is too: `camera.ZonesConfig.LastZoneID` (nil continues after the highest ID in use, as `:245`), which the host learns through `ZonePort.CreateTwoDCartesianZone` — the port receives each new ID before the server keeps the zone (owner decision O-1 (a), 371; decision 290). One owner for one state: the counter is stored and restored with the zones it numbers. A server built through the device facade, which carries no `LastZoneID`, reads it once from the port's optional `camera.LastZoneIDSource`; an explicit `LastZoneID` wins (owner decision O-7, 377). Pin lift b25ed960, unit P3-B.

### BD-Thermostat-HostSchedules — the host's SetSchedules is an authoritative replace, held to matter.js's content rules only

The host's `SetSchedules` is an authoritative replace. It is held to matter.js's content rules for Schedules (`#validateScheduleWriteRequest`, `#validateScheduleTransitions`, `packages/node/src/behaviors/thermostat/ThermostatServer.ts:2693-3002` at `b25ed960`) and its normalisation (`:3028-3049`), not to the lifecycle rules matter.js applies to every stored write, a local one included (`:2618-2620`): an unknown handle (NOT_FOUND, `:2728-2734`), a new built-in schedule (`:2735-2738`, `:2746-2748`), a changed BuiltIn (`:2739-2743`), dropping a built-in or the active schedule (`#validateScheduleCommit`, `:3056-3086`). An active schedule the replace drops is cleared, as matter.js's start clears a handle that names no schedule (`:353-366`). With TEVT the clear emits ActiveScheduleChange `{dropped, null}`, as every change of the handle does (`ThermostatServer.ts:2136-2144` at `b25ed960`); matter.js refuses such a replace (`#validateScheduleCommit`, `:3072-3085`), so it has no event here (pin lift b25ed960, unit P4-A). The configured list is validated against itself, as matter.js does (`:331`), which already admits fixed handles and built-in schedules; the one difference there is a configured schedule with a null handle and BuiltIn true, which matter.js refuses (`:2746-2748`) and the host flag admits. A `SchedulePort` may confirm a commit through `SetSchedules`. Reason: the host is the source of truth for device-owned programs (openccu-loom mirrors CCU week programs with fixed handles, `openccu-loom/internal/model/custom/climate/matter_schedule.go:300, :354` at `934a7dc8`, a host's file — the implementer's lines, not re-read); matter.js models a node that owns its programs. Matter peers keep every rule (owner decision O-8, 378). Tests: `cluster/thermo` `TestHostReplaceOfSchedules`, `TestSchedulesFromTheDevice`. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P3-A.

### BD-Matter-Example-FakeReadingsBothEndpoints — with endpoint bits 0 the reference daemon's fake readings reach both of the grid meter's measurement endpoints

With endpoint bits 0 the reference daemon's grid meter starts or stops the fake readings on both of its measurement endpoints (the meter's and its ElectricalSensor part's), where matter.js's dispatcher stops at the first endpoint whose handler accepts (`support/chip-testing/src/cluster/TestGeneralDiagnosticsServer.ts:25-36` at b25ed960, `!handled`, `:28`) and chip's delegate at the first handler (`src/app/TestEventTriggerDelegate.h:78-85` at 6170af84): the two endpoints are one meter's and the CSA cases trigger with endpoint bits 0 whichever endpoint they read; matter.js's handler states the same intent (`support/chip-testing/src/cluster/FakeElectricalReadingsHandler.ts:13`). Code: `examples/reference-bridge/fleet_energy_market.go`, `fakeReadingsTrigger`. Coordinator decision C-10 (388); pin lift b25ed960, unit P3-E.

### BD-Matter-GiveUp-NextMessageTaken — after this node gives up on a message, its exchange takes the next message, where matter.js refuses one without the acknowledgement until the exchange's close timer

At the give-up matter.js clears the owed acknowledgement (`#receivedMessageToAck`) and both callbacks but keeps `#sentMessageToAck`, and transmits nothing (`packages/protocol/src/protocol/MessageExchange.ts:996-1001` at `b25ed960`); while that is set the exchange refuses a message without an acknowledgement ("Previous message ack is missing") or with another one unless it is a standalone ack (`:534-548`), until it closes — a `close()` without a cause waits out the sum of the remaining retransmission backoffs (`:1198-1215`). The bridge transmits nothing at the give-up either (`outboundReliableTracker.Tick`, `bridge/outbound_reliable.go:1057-1064` at `c8348b35`), but drops the entry, and the receive rules read the live tracker only (`refuseUnacknowledging` → `outstandingOn`, `bridge/receive.go:1412-1437`), so the exchange's next message is taken. For a BDX exchange the give-up ends the exchange and a send waiting on it ends unsent (decision 283), so no difference shows there; for an interaction exchange or a handshake it shows between the give-up and matter.js's close timer. Reason (owner decision 401): the bridge keeps no IM exchange object, so the span would have to be rebuilt as a tombstone that copies an incidental timer of matter.js, and no honest peer tells the difference — it would have to let five transmissions go unacknowledged and then go on with the same exchange without the acknowledgement (Fable's read, none found). No test pins the span. Retire when the bridge gains an exchange object that outlives the give-up. Closes findings row R2-P7-V3-giveup; pin lift b25ed960, unit P3c-E.

### BD-Matter-ReadRequest-EmptyListLeftOut — a ReadRequest this module sends leaves out every list without members, where matter.js sets an empty one it was handed

matter.js's request builder sets each of the four lists that is not undefined (`packages/protocol/src/action/request/Read.ts:75-88` at `b25ed960`: `if (attributeRequests)`, `if (versionFilters)`, `if (eventRequests)`, `if (eventFilters !== undefined)`). A list is undefined when the caller gave neither the option nor a selector of that kind (`:41`); it is empty when the caller passed `[]`, or when a selector has an empty `attributes` or `events` list — the builder creates the list (`:137-139`, `:179-181`) and pushes nothing. The version and event filters are only ever created with a member (`:123-124`, `:173-174`). Whether matter.js's encoder then writes a set empty list was not read (`TlvReadRequest.ts`; unverified). This module's client leaves out every list without members, nil or empty (`ReadRequest.MarshalTLV`, `im/read.go`; the marshal helpers in `im/client.go`). Reason: in Go's `ReadRequest` a nil and an empty list are one value, so the encoder has one form for a list without members; the case is degenerate — a request that names no path of a kind. No test of its own pins it. Recorded for row 902 (phase-6b register, N6b-cite-5); pin lift b25ed960, unit P3c-E.

### BD-Matter-SecretRedaction-NoOffSwitch — a value the model marks secret never reaches the module's log; there is no switch to turn redaction off

matter.js redacts values its model marks `isSecret` from its logs (`packages/model/src/logic/SecretRedaction.ts:17-147` at b25ed960) unless `Logger.redactSecrets` is set false (default true, `packages/general/src/log/Logger.ts:80-88` at b25ed960; checked at `SecretRedaction.ts:33`, `:44`, `:55`). This module redacts unconditionally (`cluster/spec/redact.go`, applied by `bridge/log_redact.go` to the read and priming report value logs): a key, passcode or credential must never reach a log an embedder ships, and an opt-out is a switch nobody audits (owner decision W1, 433). Redaction is applied where a log statement prints a value by its model; error texts and panic values do not pass through it. matter.js names the limit of its own redaction for raw bytes: the decrypted message payload of a debug message log still carries the secrets TLV-encoded (`packages/general/src/log/Logger.ts:73-78`, `:85-86` at b25ed960). Pinned by `cluster/spec:TestSecretRedactionParityMatterJS`, `cluster/spec:TestGeneratedSecretMarksMatchSnapshot` and `bridge:TestValueLogsRedactSecrets`; the two cases of `SecretRedactionTest.ts` that turn the switch off are left by design. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P4-B.

### BD-Matter-OTAManager-QueueRunAfterChange — the update queue runs at the end of the change that asks for it, with the manager's lock released for the registry read

matter.js runs `#triggerQueuedUpdate` inside the change and reads `#peerOf` at that instant (`packages/node/src/behavior/system/software-update/SoftwareUpdateManager.ts:550-561`, `:1302-1353` at `b25ed960`). The Go manager runs the queue a change asks for at the end of that change, with its lock released for one read of the registry, because the registry and its nodes have locks of their own that are not taken under the manager's lock. A peer counts as gone only when that read did not find its node and no change gave it state after the read began (a change sequence, so nothing queued meanwhile is dropped), and the change's own events run after its run, on its caller (`controller/softwareupdate/manager.go` `unlock`, `readPresenceLocked`) — so within one change the events the change posts itself (in the product check, `UpdateAvailable`) come before the events of its deferred queue run (another peer's `UpdateFailed` after a stall), where matter.js queues the run's events first (`:1291` before `:932`). `ForceUpdate` runs the queue before its forced announcement, as `:1291` before `:1521`. Why: a translation of the concurrency model, not a behaviour choice (decision 479). Pinned by `controller/softwareupdate:TestManagerPresenceAsOfTheRun`, `…TestManagerChangeEmitsItsOwnEvents` and `…TestManagerForceRunsTheQueueFirstParity`. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P5-A.

### BD-Matter-OTAManager-AnnouncementLog — a failed announcement is classified without matter.js's "not a MatterError" branch

`#announce` (`packages/node/src/behavior/system/software-update/SoftwareUpdateManager.ts:1417-1444` at `b25ed960`) warns for an error outside matter.js's `MatterError` hierarchy, which is a programming error. In Go such an error is a panic, not an `error`, so the branch has no input. Go's classification is the rest of that table: an announcement that the timeout aborted is logged at Info, any other abort is not logged, a closed session or peer at Debug, and any other failure at Info (`controller/softwareupdate/manager.go` `runAnnouncement`). Whether Go's two closed errors (`exchange.ErrSessionClosed`, `peer.ErrClosed`) are all of matter.js's `ClosedError` cases was not read (unverified). Decision 481; pin lift b25ed960, unit P5-A.

### BD-Matter-OTAManager-LegacyStatusPhase — the deprecated status hook moves an entry into progress without an attempt (closes at v0.26.0)

The deprecated `Manager.OnStatusChange` has no counterpart at the pin: matter.js has no `onOtaStatusChange` any more (no hit in `packages/node/src`, `packages/protocol/src` at `b25ed960`). An entry it moves is in `progress` without an attempt, carrying the reported status and apply delay. Such an entry stalls after its time plus the apply delay plus 15 minutes, never counts as failed, is skipped by `#retarget`, and is replaced by a linked attempt (`controller/softwareupdate/manager.go` `updatePhase`). Why: a legacy view through the deprecation window, nothing to mirror (decisions 466, 472, 481). The row and the phase leave with `OnStatusChange` in v0.26.0. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P5-A.

### BD-Matter-CertificateUpdate-TypedOutcome — a failed NOC update names its outcome as a value

matter.js reports the outcome of a failed operational-certificate update only in the message text: `OperationalCertificateUpdateError` carries `fabricIndexOnPeer` alone (`packages/protocol/src/peer/OperationalCertificateUpdate.ts:70-81` at `b25ed960`), and the messages say whether the peer keeps its previous certificate, has the new one in place, reverted, or whether the outcome is unknown (`:282`, `:331`, `:342`, `:349`; `:281-284`, `:329-352`); Busy and Refused say that nothing changed on the peer (`:89-100`). `commissioner.CertificateUpdateError` carries `Outcome` (`CertificateUpdatePreviousKept`, `CertificateUpdateReverted`, `CertificateUpdateNewInPlace`, `CertificateUpdateUnknown`) and `FabricIndexOnPeer` beside matter.js's message, and `errors.Is` tells `ErrCertificateUpdateBusy` and `ErrCertificateUpdateRefused`, which carry `PreviousKept` (decision 474); the inner step causes matter.js builds without an outcome carry the zero `Outcome` (decision 484). The wire behaviour is matter.js's unchanged. Why: a host or UI decides retry or alarm from a value, not from English text (owner decision W2, 454). Register row above. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P5-B.

### BD-Matter-CertificateUpdate-RootByPublicKey — the NOC update checks the fabric's CA by its root public key

matter.js refuses an update when the fabric's root certificate differs from its CA's (`packages/protocol/src/peer/OperationalCertificateUpdate.ts:254-258` at `b25ed960`); `commissioner.Fabric` keeps no root certificate, so the Go check compares the CA's root public key with the fabric's (`controller/commissioner/noc_update.go`). The two differ only for two RCACs of one key. matter.js stops there before any session; Go proceeds and the device decides — it accepts the new NOC, or refuses it (UpdateNOC answered with an error status → disarm → previous certificate kept). No trust is gained: the authority is the root private key, and the NOC the node reports is verified against the fabric before anything is armed. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P5-B.

### BD-Matter-ClientInteraction-CloseSubscriptionsSweep — disabling or deleting a node closes every active subscription of its peer

matter.js's `ClientNode.disable` (`packages/node/src/node/ClientNode.ts:274-288`, through `cancelWithMutex`, `:326-340`) closes only what the node's interaction established (`packages/protocol/src/action/client/ClientInteraction.ts:293-298` at `b25ed960`); `Interaction.Close` does the same in Go since wave P5 (decision 467). `Node.Disable` and the registry's delete path run `Interaction.CloseSubscriptions`, which closes every active subscription of the peer, including those a host made through another `Commissioner.Interaction(p)` (`controller/client/node.go`, `client/interaction/interaction.go`). Why: wave P5 narrowed `Interaction.Close` to the pin (coordinator decisions 467 and 476) and left `CloseSubscriptions` as it was; the coordinator's reasoning: where the node as a whole is disabled or deleted, no subscription of the peer outlives it, whichever interaction made it. Pin lift b25ed960, unit P5-B.

### BD-Matter-RelaxedEnum-HeldToWireWidth — a relaxed enum field above its wire width is refused with CONSTRAINT_ERROR, where matter.js's handler answers

matter.js turns all validation of three command fields off (`validate = false`, `packages/node/src/behavior/state/validation/conformance.ts:36-40` at `b25ed960`; the only two sites, `packages/node/src/behaviors/general-commissioning/GeneralCommissioningServer.ts:288-289` and `packages/node/src/behaviors/identify/IdentifyServer.ts:162-166`), and its TLV layer types every enum as a 32-bit integer (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvNumber.ts:302-303`, `packages/types/src/tlv/TlvOfModel.ts:221-224`). So SetRegulatoryConfig's NewRegulatoryConfig 0x100 reaches the handler, which answers ValueOutsideRange in its response (`GeneralCommissioningServer.ts:199-206`), and Identify's TriggerEffect runs with SUCCESS (`IdentifyServer.ts:134-139`). connectedhomeip answers FAILURE: the enum decodes through its underlying type (`src/app/data-model/Decode.h:59-66` at `6170af84`), `Get(uint8_t&)` refuses the value with `CHIP_ERROR_INVALID_INTEGER_VALUE` (`src/lib/core/TLVReader.cpp:204-214`), and a core error maps to `Status::Failure` (`src/protocols/interaction_model/StatusCode.cpp:41-62`). Here the definition's decoder holds a `Relaxed` field to its type's width (`cluster/spec/codec.go` `DecodeUintIn`, `cluster/spec/model.go` `DecodeRequest`) and answers CONSTRAINT_ERROR — the status matter.js gives a value outside a field's TLV bounds (`packages/types/src/common/ValidationError.ts:16-29`) and that every other over-wide integer gets here. A value up to 0xFF, defined or not, reaches the handler as in matter.js. Reason: matter.js admits the value only through a 32-bit enum representation that has no Go equivalent — the generated enum8 type and `contract.IdentifyHandler`'s `uint8` cannot carry it — while the relaxation it states is aimed at values chip accepts (`IdentifyServer.ts:162-163`), and chip refuses this one too; widening every relaxed enum field and the host contract, or a sentinel in the decoder, would be worse than the divergence (owner decision W5, 490; F-b25ed960-33). Guard: the SetRegulatoryConfig row of `bridge/fields_reader_range_test.go`; TriggerEffect has no row there.

### BD-Matter-PASE-DeferredCloseCap — a revoked PASE session's deferred close runs after at most 60 s

matter.js defers a PASE session's graceful close until its last exchange closes and bounds it by nothing at session level (`packages/protocol/src/session/Session.ts:304-320`, `packages/protocol/src/session/NodeSession.ts:438-462` at `b25ed960`). Here the deferral is capped at 60 s (`paseCloseDeferralCap`, `bridge/pase_deferred_close.go`; owner decision W6, 491), after which the close runs anyway, CloseSession still sent: the active set is assembled from several Go tables, and a leak in one must not pin a revoked PASE session — and the commissioning channel's implicit Administer — open. Locked by `bridge:TestRevokeClosesThePASESessionWhenItIsIdle/the close runs at the deferral's cap`. Three Go paths free the session's last activity without a recheck and so wait for the cap: a stalled chunked write, counted in `openWriteTxs` until a later write sweeps it (`writeTxTTL`, `bridge/exchange_routing.go`); a message untracked after a failed send by a sender outside a handler turn of the session (`bridge/subscribe.go`, `bridge/ota_provider_link.go`); and an acknowledgement carried only by a duplicate, which frees nothing (`bridge/receive.go`). Every one ends at the cap; the owner judged them no gap against a deferral matter.js does not bound (decision 507, F-b25ed960-59).

### BD-Matter-DoorLock-RefusedModifyKeepsExpiryTimer — a refused local SetUser Modify leaves the user's expiry timer running

A local SetUser Modify that is refused for an undefined or feature-disallowed UserStatus or UserType leaves the user's expiry timer running. matter.js stops the timer (`packages/node/src/behaviors/door-lock/DoorLockServer.ts:312-315` at `b25ed960`) before `replaceUser` throws (`:317-326`; for a feature-disallowed value the throw is derived from the lines F-b25ed960-36 cites, not run) and nothing restarts it; the stored deadline still denies the PIN (`:1082-1090`) and re-arms the timer on that use, so only the transition to OccupiedDisabled at the deadline is late there. Here the record is checked before anything changes (`cluster/lock/users.go` `modifyUserLocked`). Reason: a refused command has no side effect; the difference is reachable only by a local caller, a peer's request is refused before the handler in both (F-b25ed960-36). Guard: `TestLocalStoreRefusesUndefinedEnumValues/a_refused_Modify_leaves_the_expiry_timer_running`.

### BD-Matter-Subscription-FlushOnOwnSessionOnly — a closing subscription is flushed on its own session; there is no per-call flush session

matter.js's `ServerSubscription.close(flushViaSession)` (`packages/node/src/node/server/ServerSubscription.ts:788-789` at `b25ed960`) takes the session to flush on as an argument; its one production caller, `NodeSession.closeSubscriptions` (`packages/protocol/src/session/NodeSession.ts:383-395`), passes the closing session itself (`:386`) for the members of its own set, and a subscription is in the set of the session it reports on (`ServerSubscription.ts:425`, `#follow` `:820-834`). `Manager.FlushSession` / `FlushFabric` (`im/subscription/manager.go`) select by `CurrentSessionID()` and take no session argument: a per-call session would let a subscriber's data, read under its ACL identity, go out on another session (decision 494; F-b25ed960-43). Locked by `im/subscription:TestFlushSessionFollowsAMovedSubscription`; ServerSubscriptionTest.ts "flushes on the session it is given when it closes (characterization)" is left.

### BD-Matter-ICD-CheckInAddressLastActive — the Check-In goes to the address of the session the client sent on last, not the session added last

matter.js's Check-In sender resolves the peer's cached `operationalAddress` (`packages/node/src/behaviors/icd-management/IcdManagementServer.ts:362-365` at `b25ed960`), which is set when a session is added and on that session's `networkAddressChanged` (`packages/protocol/src/peer/Peer.ts:141-164`) and on adoption (`PeerSet.ts:116-124`, `:317-318`), not at each receive. `Bridge.PeerSessionAddress` (`bridge/icd.go`) takes the UDP session the client was active on last, as `livePeerLink` chooses. Among held UDP sessions the two differ when an older session A (address X) and a newer session B (address Y) are held and the client then sends on A from the unchanged X: matter.js sends the Check-In to Y, this module to X. Two more differences, both older than this entry: a TCP session added last — matter.js sets a `tcp` address with the mDNS port (`Peer.ts:150-158`) and its sender picks the TCP interface for it (`IcdManagementServer.ts:367-370`), where `PeerSessionAddress` skips every session without a UDP address and returns an older UDP session's address or none; and no session held — matter.js keeps the cached address (the session's `closing` handler removes the session and does not clear it, `Peer.ts:168-174`), where this module resolves the address over DNS-SD (`node/icd.go`). Reason: the session the client last used is the address it last proved reachable at. Review II, R2-C2-par-0353. Guard: `bridge:TestPeerSessionAddressIsTheNewestSessions`.

### BD-Matter-SecretRedaction-ShapeMismatchFailsClosed — a secret-bearing value whose wire form is another type than its model is redacted whole

matter.js's `redactValue` returns the value unchanged for an array model whose value is not an array and for an object model whose value is not a plain object (`packages/model/src/logic/SecretRedaction.ts:91-122`, `:107-108`, `:114-115` at `b25ed960`); both tests cover a scalar too. Here `redactValue` (`cluster/spec/redact.go`) replaces a secret-bearing list or struct whose TLV node is another type than its model — a struct read as a TLV list, a list as a structure, either as a scalar — by "(redacted)" under its tag; a TLV list under a list model (a list, not an array) is redacted whole too. Reason: a value whose shape the model cannot walk may hold the secret anywhere, so the module's logs fail closed, and the "fails closed" sentence of `bridge/log_redact.go` names the case (owner decision 525). Review II, R2-C2-sec-1303. Pinned by `cluster/spec:TestRedactShapes`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js redacts a mismatched shape.

### BD-Matter-Controller-CrlDerNodeBudget — a CRL's DER decode counts its elements against a budget

matter.js's `#decodeRec` (`packages/general/src/codec/DerCodec.ts:429-442` at `b25ed960`) pushes every element of a constructed node while bytes remain, with no element count (`:436-440`). Here (`controller/dcl/crl.go`) the decode counts each constructed node's children from their headers and charges them against `derMaxNodes` = `maxCRLSize`/4 (262 144 elements per decode) before it allocates them, and refuses a CRL past it. The budget is this module's judgement: a 1 MiB list of real entries (serial, date and reason-code extension, 34 bytes and 7 elements each) still decodes. Review II, R2-C2-bound-1901. Pinned by `controller/dcl:TestDERNodeBudgetBoundsTheWalk`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js bounds a decode.

### BD-Matter-Controller-OtaVersionsPerCheckBounded — an OTA check looks up at most the 64 highest listed versions

matter.js takes the newer versions highest first (`packages/protocol/src/dcl/DclOtaUpdateService.ts:238-240` at `b25ed960`) and looks up every one until one applies (`:253`, `for (const version of newerVersions)`), with no cap in `:235-253`. Here (`dcl/ota.go` `maxOTAVersionsPerCheck`) a check looks up at most the 64 highest and logs the cut (`dcl.ota.too_many_versions`). The result differs: with more than 64 newer versions listed and none of the highest 64 applicable, this module finds no update where matter.js would find one. 64 is this module's judgement. Review II, R2-C2-bound-1902. Pinned by `dcl:TestOTAVersionsExaminedPerCheckAreBounded`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js bounds a check.

### BD-Matter-Controller-DclCertificatesPerAnswerBounded — one root's ledger answer adds at most 16 certificates

matter.js stores every certificate of an answer that passes its checks — a `subjectKeyId`, a PEM that converts, the SKID check (`for (const cert of certs)`, `packages/protocol/src/dcl/DclCertificateService.ts:1206-1249`, the skips `:1207-1232`, `#storeCertificate` `:1236-1245` at `b25ed960`) — with no cap. Here (`controller/dcl/certstore.go` `maxCertificatesPerRootAnswer`) one `RootCertificateBySubject` answer adds at most 16 valid certificates, the asked-for root's key sorted first, and logs the cut (`dcl.certificates.too_many_in_answer`); last-wins among the certificates of one key is unchanged. Not measured: with more than 16 valid certificates under the asked-for key, the 16th is kept where matter.js keeps the last. Review II, R2-C2-bound-1903. Pinned by `controller/dcl:TestCertificatesPerRootAnswerBounded`. Register row above; the row closes when matter.js bounds an answer.

### BD-chip-RCAC-RefusalsBothReferencesShare — `ValidateRCAC` refuses what both references refuse in a root and keeps two leniencies, one from each

`ValidateRCAC` (`secure/mattercert/verify.go`) refuses what both references refuse in a root: an icac-id, a fabric id of 0 and CATs in the subject (chip `src/credentials/CHIPCert.cpp:1129`, `ChipDN::GetCertType` `:606-687` at `6170af84`; matter.js `packages/protocol/src/certificate/kinds/Rcac.ts:69-71`, `:74-76`, `:84-86` at `b25ed960`), and a subjectKeyIdentifier or authorityKeyIdentifier that is absent or not 20 bytes (matter.js `Rcac.ts:112-126`; chip `CHIPCert.cpp:143-144`, `src/lib/core/TLVReader.h:481`, `src/credentials/CHIPCert.h:50`), besides is-CA (chip `:1135`; matter.js `:94-96`). It keeps two leniencies: a root subject with a firmware-signing-id is admitted, as matter.js admits it (`packages/protocol/src/certificate/kinds/definitions/operational.ts:59`; `Rcac.verify`, `:55-136`, has no test for it), where chip refuses it (`:648-650`); and the key usage needs keyCertSign only, as chip (`:1141`), where matter.js refuses a key usage other than 0x0060 or 0x0061 (`Rcac.ts:100-105`) — so a root with keyCertSign and without cRLSign is accepted (`secure/mattercert:TestValidateRCAC_CRLSignAbsent`). The self-signature test compares the RCAC-IDs where chip compares the whole subject and issuer DN (`:1131`): an issuer DN that carries an icac-id or CATs beside the matching rcac-id passes here, refused by chip through that comparison; matter.js's `Rcac.verify` has no issuer test either. An extendedKeyUsage extension on a root is refused, as matter.js refuses it (`packages/protocol/src/certificate/kinds/Rcac.ts:107-110` at `b25ed960`), where chip's `ValidateChipRCAC` (`src/credentials/CHIPCert.cpp:1116-1144` at `6170af84`) reads none (decision 539). Reason: owner decisions 516 and 523 — the refusals both references share are taken; for the two leniencies the owner chose the reference named with each, with no further reason recorded; decision 539 takes matter.js's extendedKeyUsage refusal. Review II, R2-C2-par-0150. Pinned by `secure/mattercert:TestValidateRCACRefusesARootSubjectOfAnotherKindParityMatterJS`, `TestValidateRCACRefusesAKeyIdentifierOfAnotherLengthParityMatterJS`, `TestValidateRCACRefusesAnExtendedKeyUsageParityMatterJS` and `TestValidateRCACRefusals`.

Review II, run 3 (R3-par-3405, decision 538): `DecodeDER` keeps a subject or authority key identifier of any length, as matter.js's DER parser does (`packages/protocol/src/certificate/kinds/Certificate.ts:573-574`, `:577-583` at `b25ed960`); chip's X.509 converter refuses a length other than `kKeyIdentifierLength` for every certificate (`src/credentials/CHIPCertFromX509.cpp:213`, `:232` at `6170af84`; `kKeyIdentifierLength` = `kSHA1_Hash_Length`, `src/credentials/CHIPCert.h:50`, `src/crypto/CHIPCryptoPAL.h:55`; its value, 20, was not read at the pin). The length is refused per kind where matter.js refuses it (`Rcac.ts:112-126`; `Icac.ts:139-152`, `Noc.ts:159-172`): `ValidateRCAC`, `checkNOCShape`, `checkICACShape` (`secure/mattercert/verify.go`).

### BD-Matter-Bridge-IdentifyOnEveryBridgedEndpoint — Identify is mounted on every bridged endpoint that is no part, whatever its device type

matter.js mounts Identify only where an endpoint's device type lists it: ElectricalSensor mandates PowerTopology only and mounts nothing; BridgedNode mandates and mounts Parts, Index and BridgedDeviceBasicInformation; no `Identify` in `electrical-sensor.ts`, `power-source.ts` or `bridged-node.ts` (`packages/node/src/endpoints/electrical-sensor.ts:63-69`, `:72-79`; `packages/node/src/endpoints/bridged-node.ts:118-131`, `:134-145` at `b25ed960`). `endpoint/materialize.go` `ClusterServers` puts the endpoint's Identify first on every bridged endpoint that is no part (a part only where its type mandates it, `partClusterServers`), so an ElectricalSensor (0x0510) or PowerSource (0x0011) endpoint serves a cluster its type does not list. ### BD-Matter-Controller-CommissionableDiscoveryRefreshesCommissioned — a commissionable discovery refreshes a matching commissioned node's record, as matter.js

`ForDevice` (`controller/client/addresses.go`) matches a node by its commissionable instance id, commissioned or not, and overwrites the match's descriptor (addresses, TXT fields, discriminator, mode) before the commission is refused with `ErrAlreadyCommissioned`. matter.js's `find` takes any readable node, and one whose construction is still initialising (`packages/node/src/node/client/Peers.ts:999`), with no commissioned filter (`:997-1007`); it matches by `RemoteDescriptor.is`, which compares peer addresses only when both descriptors carry one (`packages/node/src/behavior/system/commissioning/RemoteDescriptor.ts:38-40`) and otherwise a non-empty device identifier of the discovered one (`:45-47`); the match gets `agent.commissioning.descriptor = descriptor` unconditionally (`Peers.ts:377-396`, `:389-392`; the setter `CommissioningClient.ts:694-696` at `b25ed960`).
