### BD-Matter-Scenes-RecallActivatesHeldScene — a recalled scene that left the table during the apply is not activated

A RecallScene whose scene is removed or replaced while its attribute values are applied: matter.js reads the entry (`packages/node/src/behaviors/scenes-management/ScenesManagementServer.ts:451-460`), awaits `#applySceneAttributeValues` (`:461`, `Promise.all` of the behaviours' apply results, `:897-921`) and then `#activateSceneInFabricSceneInfo` (`:462`), which looks nothing up and writes `fabricSceneInfo` by index, group and scene id (`:1062-1073`); `recallGlobalScene` likewise (`:564-566`); nothing holds the scene table across the await (`packages/node/src/behavior/state/managed/Datasource.ts:1280-1287`, `:1554-1559`; inferred from those lines). So matter.js activates a scene the table no longer holds, and one whose values were replaced meanwhile. The module skips the activation when the scene left the table (`activateIfHeld`, `cluster/core/scenes_management.go`) and, as matter.js, activates a replaced entry whose new values were not applied (R3-conc-3104). Reason: a current scene the table does not hold is a state a reader cannot resolve; the replaced-values case is left as matter.js has it. Review II, R2-C2-conc-1205, owner decision 547; matter.js at `b25ed960`.

### BD-Matter-RetryScheduleInRange — a retry schedule's base interval never shrinks below the initial one; a subscription's schedule is merged over the default per request

`client/discovery` `Retries` (`DefaultRetries.merge`, `newRetrySchedule`) and `client/interaction`'s sustained schedule (`newRetries`) take an initial interval ≤ 0 as 1 s, a backoff below 1 or NaN as 1, a negative maximum interval as none and a jitter factor outside [0, 1] as its bound, so the base interval never shrinks below the initial one. matter.js `RetrySchedule` stores the configuration as given and has no lower bound on the interval (`packages/general/src/net/RetrySchedule.ts:18-21`, `:33-35`, `:48-53`, `:58`, `:114-119` at `b25ed960`); a shrinking schedule without timeout or count would send a multicast query on every loop turn. Hardening beyond matter.js (review II, R3-api-3580). `SubscribeRequest.Retries` is merged field by field over the default sustained schedule (a zero field takes `DefaultSustainRetries`' field; `NoMaximumInterval` / `NoJitter` say none), as matter.js `RetrySchedule.Configuration(SustainedSubscription.DefaultRetrySchedule, sustainRetries)` (`packages/protocol/src/action/client/ClientInteraction.ts:266-269`; `RetrySchedule.ts:114-119`, `{ ...defaults, ...config }`) at `b25ed960`. One difference: matter.js merges by key presence, so an explicitly present `0` (e.g. `jitterFactor: 0`) replaces the default there (`RetrySchedule.ts:114-119`, and `:33` applies its default to `undefined` only); here a zero field stands for matter.js's absent key and keeps the default's field, and `NoMaximumInterval` / `NoJitter` say none. matter.js sets the schedule per `ClientInteraction` (`ClientInteraction.ts:178`, handed on `:1175`), here per subscribe request: a schedule belongs to the subscription it paces, and a client with several peers or uses needs it per subscription (owner decisions 562, 566; `DefaultSustainRetries` is deprecated). Pinned by `client/discovery:TestRetrySchedule_NeverShrinksBelowItsFirstInterval`, `client/interaction:TestSustainRetries_NeverShrinkBelowTheFirstInterval`, `TestSustainRetriesMergeOverTheDefault` and `TestSustainedRetriesMergeOverTheDefault`.

### BD-Matter-Discovery-CommissionableSearchBounded — a continuous commissionable search keeps no result, remembers at most 8192 instances and prepares at most 16 devices at once

A continuous commissionable DNS-SD search (`client/discovery`, the `IPTransport` of a session) keeps no result and remembers at most `maxSeenInstances` = 8192 instance ids; a forgotten device announced again is delivered again, and a race attempts it again. A search queues at most `maxQueuedDeliveries` = 8192 devices its callback has not taken; past that the oldest is dropped and logged once per drain (`matter.discovery.deliveries_dropped`), and a device delivered on an announcement that the queue drops is the instance the waiter forgets at the same push, so its next announcement is delivered again (owner decision 573). A discovery prepares at most `maxConcurrentPreparations` = 16 devices at once; past it the transport's callback waits while the search runs, and a device still waiting when the search stops is not prepared (owner decisions 563, 565; `client/discovery/session.go` `prepare`). matter.js prepares every device its scanners report, also one reported after the stop (`#prepare` without a stopped check, `Discovery.ts:311-314`); here such a device is prepared only while a slot is free. A device behind N others reaches its kind after about N × Prepare time / 16, and the race's 16 s runs from that hand-over. matter.js keeps `seen = new Set<string>()` unbounded and pushes every device to `result` (`packages/protocol/src/mdns/CommissionableMdnsScanner.ts:177`, `:188-194` at `b25ed960`), and it does not bound preparations: `#preparing = new Set` (`packages/node/src/behavior/system/controller/discovery/Discovery.ts:42`), added without a size check (`:311-313`), the scanner callback never held back (`:287`), `#prepared` waits for all (`:324-328`). These bounds are this module's own (review II, R3-bound-3552); the limits are in `docs/guides/limits.md`. Pinned by `client/discovery:TestScanner_ContinuousSearchRetainsBoundedState`, `TestScanner_FindWithoutKeepReturnsNothing`, `TestSession_ConcurrentPreparationsAreBounded`, `TestSession_PreparationBacklogEndsWithTheSearch`, `TestDeliveryQueue_BoundDropsTheOldest`, `TestDeliveryQueue_DropIsLogged` and `TestDeliveryQueue_DroppedDeviceIsDeliveredAgain`.

### BD-Matter-Subscription-EventMinSaturates — a re-subscription after event number 2^64−1 asks for 2^64−1, not 0

`client/interaction` `requestNewEvents` holds EventMin at 2^64−1 after an event numbered 2^64−1 instead of wrapping to 0, as `controller/client` does for the default subscription's filter since C3 (R2-C2-wire-2351, `a40a0ffa6`). matter.js computes `this.#maxEventNumber + 1n` as a bigint and writes it without a boundary check (`packages/protocol/src/action/client/subscription/SustainedSubscription.ts:379-384`; `packages/types/src/tlv/TlvNumber.ts:118-122`, `:145-156` at `b25ed960`); what it puts on the wire for 2^64 was not read (unverified). This module's own choice (review II, R2-C2-wire-2351 rest). Pinned by `client/interaction:TestSustainedEventMinAtTheTopOfTheRange` and `controller/client:TestEventCursorAtTheTopOfTheRange`.

### BD-Matter-Controller-CameraStringBytes — the camera provider boundary counts a string's bound in UTF-8 bytes, ahead of matterjs-server

The camera provider boundary counts a Matter string field's bound in UTF-8 bytes (`spec.StringLength`, decisions 294, 554): `toBoundedString` (`controller/camera/field_ranges.go`), the Min branch of `stringConverter` (`provider_arguments.go`), and on the typed path `validateICEServers` and `StartRequest`'s `ICETransportPolicy` (`session.go`). This is the same count as the generated decoder, so an over-long string is `ErrInvalidArgument` (matterjs-server's error 8) before the send. It is ahead of matterjs-server `0bd06f2`, which counts UTF-16 code units in `toBoundedString` (`packages/ws-controller/src/camera/wireArgumentChecks.ts:38-43` at `0bd06f2`) and in the Min branch (`webRtcProviderArguments.ts:124-128` at `0bd06f2`) and builds against matter.js 0.18.0 (`packages/ws-controller/package.json:45`). matter.js 0.18.0's `TlvString` counts UTF-16 too (`packages/types/src/tlv/TlvString.ts:82` at `v0.18.0`). matter.js counts bytes from `e4326a175` (#4995; `TlvString.ts:29-31`, `:92-96` at `b25ed960`). The code would be 8 on matterjs-server's path once its matter.js counts bytes (inferred). The refusal text stays matterjs-server's ("… characters") although the count is bytes, because the parity tests pin it verbatim. `client_session_key`, matterjs-server's own WebSocket key and never a Matter TLV string, keeps the UTF-16 count (`cameraCommands.ts:304`, `:309-311` at `0bd06f2`). Review II, R3-err-3651. Pinned by `controller/camera:TestStringBoundsCountBytes`.

### BD-Matter-Node-PartForgetByOwner — a part key is not forgotten on its own while its owner serves it

`Aggregator.Forget` / `Partition.Forget` / `Batch.Forget` of a part key that another endpoint, of any partition, serves is `ErrUnknownKey` and changes nothing: the part is that endpoint's (decision 567; in a `Batch` judged against its end state, decisions 582, 585). Here a part exists only inside its owner's declaration, and a `Replace` of the owner without it drops it. In matter.js at `b25ed960` a part is an `Endpoint` of its own and `delete()` is available on it (`packages/node/src/endpoint/Endpoint.ts:961-966`, `erase()` → `EndpointInitializer.eraseDescendant(this)` at `:953-956`); nothing at those lines refuses a child endpoint. Not read: whether a matter.js parent re-creates or rejects a deleted child afterwards, so "matter.js lets a part be deleted alone and it stays deleted" is inferred, not measured. A difference of the facade's shape (declared trees, `Replace` to drop a part), no gap (fable-diff-g5c, last section). Pinned by `node:TestForgetRefusesAPartKeyAnotherEndpointServes` and `node:TestBatchForgetOfAServedPartKeyIsJudgedAtCommit`.

### BD-Matter-Node-FlatStableKeys — stable keys are one namespace over all partitions and depths, and a Batch judges at its end

Here stable keys are one flat namespace over all partitions and depths (`endpoint/assembler.go:453`), and an `Add` or `Replace` whose own key or a part key another endpoint serves is refused with `ErrDuplicateKey` across it (decision 580). At `b25ed960` an endpoint id must be unique among the children of one parent only: `EndpointContainer.assertIdAvailable` (`packages/node/src/endpoint/properties/EndpointContainer.ts:150-155`, "endpoint IDs must be unique within parent"), called from `EndpointContainer.add` (`:55-57`) before the child is added (`:59`) and from the id setter (`packages/node/src/endpoint/Endpoint.ts:661-663`); the same id under two different owners is allowed there. matter.js judges at the insertion and has no deferred form; the single calls here (`Aggregator` / `Partition` `Add`, `Replace`, `Forget`) still refuse in the same call, and only a multi-call `Batch` judges at its end (decisions 582, 585) — `Batch` has no matter.js counterpart, and the result of a batch is the one the remove-first order gives in both stacks. The number of a key taken by a different device: at `b25ed960` an endpoint's number is read from the endpoint's own store (`packages/node/src/storage/server/ServerEndpointStores.ts:109-110`, `assignNumber` → `storeForEndpoint`), a non-root endpoint's store is its owner's child store (`:205`), and `delete()` erases that store (`eraseStoreForEndpoint`, `:225`, called from `ServerEndpointInitializer.ts:64`); inferred from those lines, not run: a part with the same id under a different owner does not get the deleted part's number. Here decisions 560 and 575 give the different device the forgotten part's number when the take and the Forget are one batch (in two calls the number is fresh here too). The flat namespace predates review II's run 3 and claims no mirror of matter.js (fable-diff-g5d, g5e, g5f, g5g). Pinned by `node:TestAddOrReplaceRefusesAKeyAnotherEndpointServes` and `node/batch_end_state_test.go`.

### BD-Matter-Messages-RemovedFabricTakenDown — a removed fabric's queued messages are taken down at the display, after the removal

Neither reference takes a message down when its fabric goes: matter.js's `MessagesServer` is the empty class (`packages/node/src/behaviors/messages/MessagesServer.ts` at `b25ed960`, no fabric and no cancel in it), and connectedhomeip's Messages server has no fabric-removal handler (`src/app/clusters/messages-server/messages-server.cpp` at `6170af84`; the delegate calls `:392-393`, `:437`). Here `Messages.RemoveFabric` / `MatterDropFabric` calls the host's `MessagePresenter.CancelMessage` once for every queued message of the fabric after the removal, one after the other on a goroutine of the server's, off the removal path (decision 624), and holds each id against another fabric's present until its cancel returned; a refusal is logged (`matter.messages.take_down_refused`, to `Messages.SetLogger`'s logger) and `MatterDropFabric` answers nil (`cluster/core/messages.go`). A cancel that never returns keeps the ids of every later removal held, and a cancel may reach the host after the node's Stop returned. Review II, R4-fsm-4103, owner decisions 598, 624, 628. Pinned by `cluster/core:TestMessagesRemoveFabricTakesItsMessagesDown`, `TestMessagesRemoveFabricHoldsTheIDsUntilTheCancelReturned`, `TestMessagesRemoveFabricDoesNotWaitForThePresenter`. Reason: a message of a fabric that is gone must not stay on the display, and the host's display must not stall the fabric's teardown. Register row above.

### BD-Matter-Camera-LostRequestorEndsSessions — a requestor the node proved lost has its WebRTC sessions ended

When the node proves a requestor lost — an exchange the node opened to it went unanswered: the bridge stack's `closeLostPeer` (`secure/operational` `PeerGoneLost`), or on the client stack `exchange.Config.PeerLost` with a `PeerUnresponsiveError` or `PeerMessageMissingError` on an exchange that received nothing — and no session with the requestor is left in either stack, `Provider.EndLostPeer` (before decision 679 `Provider.PeerGone`, which now wraps it) ends that requestor's sessions through the port's `EndSession` with the generated UnknownReason value and removes them from CurrentSessions whatever the port answers; no End is sent (`node/webrtc_provider_peers.go`, `cluster/camera/provider_gone.go`). The check that no session is left runs under the provider's serialisation: `EndLostPeer` takes a predicate that it evaluates once it holds the provider, so a CASE session the peer establishes while another command holds the provider cancels the end (decision 632). On the bridge stack a CASE responder session still establishing does not count as a session, on the client stack it does; no test pins either side. A loss cancelled by a live session in the other stack is not remembered: when that session later closes without a loss of its own, nothing ends (decision 631). The idle reaper, a closed TCP connection, the peer's CloseSession and a send the network refused (`ErrNetwork`) are no evidence (decisions 611, 634); a fabric's removal ends its sessions by `BD-Matter-Camera-FabricRemovalEndsStreams`. Its reach (decision 630): a silent subscriber never reaches `closeLostPeer` — its report's give-up goes to `noteReportUndelivered` (`bridge/ackpump.go:719-729`) — so the rule covers peers the node opens exchanges to (the camera's own signals, OTA, BDX, the client stack), and a viewer the camera sends nothing to is never detected on the Matter plane; the host's media-plane evidence (`Provider.RemoveSession`, `Provider.End`) stays primary (`docs/guides/camera.md`). The requestor's sessions (`camera.Requestor`) and a push transport's allocations are out of this rule: the requestor's peer is the camera, which `controller/camera` reaches, and a push transport's peer is a TLS endpoint, not a Matter node (owner decision 613). Review II, #590 item 2, owner decisions 605, 611, 612, 630-634. Pinned by `node/camera_peergone_internal_test.go`, `cluster/camera/provider_gone_test.go` and `secure/operational/peer_gone_test.go`. Reason: an exchange the node opened that went unanswered, with no session left, is the only Matter-plane signal that is true when it fires. Register row above.

### BD-Matter-Bridge-ReplaceKeepsKeyScopedState — a same-key Replace keeps what a controller wrote under the key, and the new instance serves it

A same-key `Replace` keeps the controller-written, key-scoped state (NodeLabel, Binding, scenes, Identify) and the new instance serves it; the ConfigurationVersion and the host's name stay with the key too (`endpoint/types.go`, `keyState`). matter.js keys persisted state on the endpoint id (`ServerEndpointStore.ts:66-71`) but erases it on `Endpoint.delete()` (`ServerEndpointStores.ts:225-254`) and, for an endpoint closed and re-added under the same id in one process, starts the new behaviours from defaults because the stored seed was consumed by the first instance (`EndpointStore.ts:36-42`, `BehaviorBacking.ts:215-216`) — inferred from those lines, not run; the values return only after a restart. What matter.js does with `configurationVersion` on a same-id re-add was not read (unverified). The announce follows both references: every cluster of the new instance gets a new random DataVersion (`packages/node/src/behavior/state/managed/Datasource.ts:763`; connectedhomeip `src/app/util/attribute-storage.cpp:384-393` at `6170af84`) and every readable attribute but the changes-omitted ones is reported (`packages/node/src/node/integration/ProtocolService.ts:290-296`). Its shape differs: the announce is decided once per commit from the end state; matter.js announces each cluster of a new endpoint instance as it is added (`ProtocolService.ts:261-296`; a removal announces nothing itself, `:225-229`), matter.js lines at `b25ed960`. Review II, issue #589, owner decisions 592, 594, 595, 604. Pinned by `node:TestReplaceKeepsTheControllerWrittenLabel`, `TestReplaceAnnouncesTheNewInstance` and `endpoint:TestNewInstanceRenewsTheTrackers`. We keep them because the key names the same bridged device to the controller that wrote them.

### BD-chip-Camera-EndRemovesSessionWhenUnreachable — `Provider.End` removes the session before it sends End, the unreachable requestor included

`Provider.End` removes the session from CurrentSessions before it sends the requestor's End and whatever the send's outcome, the unreachable requestor included (`cluster/camera/provider_peer.go`, `End`: `signalTarget`, then `removeSession`, then `send`); the send's error is returned, else the removal's. matter.js at `b25ed960` has no provider logic: `WebRtcTransportProviderServer.ts:14` is the empty subclass (register row above). connectedhomeip's camera app at `6170af84` sends End without waiting for its response (`examples/camera-app/linux/src/clusters/webrtc-provider/webrtc-provider-manager.cpp:1301-1329`: `InvokeCommandRequest` with logging callbacks) and cleans the session up at once, whatever the send returned (`:999-1000`); `CleanupSession` (`:1021-1050`) closes the peer connection (`:1041`; `webrtc-transport.cpp:265-276`, `webrtc-libdatachannel.cpp:359-365`) and leaves CurrentSessions alone — the entry goes when the peer connection reports Failed or Closed (`webrtc-libdatachannel.cpp:342-348` → `OnConnectionStateChanged` `:1157-1187`, `RemoveSession` `:1183`, its only call site in the camera app — the cluster calls it itself only for the requestor's EndSession command, `WebRTCTransportProviderCluster.cpp:1218`; the function is `:332-348`). That libdatachannel's `close()` raises the Closed callback is inferred, not read. So chip's removal does not depend on the requestor's response, which is what the kit mirrors. Two differences remain. The order: chip finds or establishes the CASE session to the requestor (`:892-917`), sends the End, cleans up, and the entry leaves through the peer-connection callback; the kit removes the entry first, then connects and sends — earlier than chip by the connect and the send, never later. The unreachable requestor: the camera app's `OnDeviceConnectionFailure` (`:1014-1019`) only logs — no cleanup, no `RemoveSession`; the session, its transport and its stream references stay until the peer connection itself fails or closes, and the 30 s connection timer (`:40`, `:1408-1420`) is cancelled at the first connection state change (`:1161-1164`). `End` removes the session there too (decision 663), and also on a provider without a `PeerConnector`, which sends nothing and returns `ErrNoPeerConnector` (decision 686). A removal the table refuses is returned with the send's error, or with `ErrNoPeerConnector`, as `errors.Join`; when the removal succeeds that error is returned bare. The CSA case reads CurrentSessions directly after the End arrives, with no wait: `TC_AVSM_2_17.py:327-332` (step 12, `get_remote_end()` without a timeout, session id and reason 11) and `:334-340` (step 13, one read, `len == 0`); the TH raises that End event inside its requestor's command handler, before the handler returns the status (`WebRTCTransportRequestorCluster.cpp:278-281`, `WebRTCTransportRequestorManager.cpp:127-132`). Review II, issue #596 A, owner decisions 654, 663. Pinned by `cluster/camera:TestProviderEndRemovesBeforeTheSendA3`, `TestProviderEndRemovesTheSession`, `TestProviderEndWithoutConnectorRemovesW2B6` and `TestProviderEndReturnsSendAndRemovalErrorsW2B6`. Reason: chip's unreachable-requestor arm is an absence of handling in an example app that relies on its media plane to notice the loss, and without the removal the kit would keep a session the camera has declared ended. Register row above.

### BD-Matter-PeerProbe-ChunkBound — a liveness probe fails at the fourth chunked report

A liveness probe fails at the fourth report with more to come and releases its exchange and network slot (`client/peer/probe.go`, `probeMaxReportChunks = 4`, `errProbeChunks`). matter.js's probe drains `readDataReports` without a count (`packages/protocol/src/action/client/ClientInteraction.ts:405`; `packages/protocol/src/interaction/InteractionMessenger.ts:1019-1054` at `b25ed960`: `while (true)`, left only on the last chunk). Whether a per-message receive timeout bounds each of its waits was not read (unverified). Review II, R2-C2-bound-2159; the bound is listed in `docs/guides/limits.md`. Pinned by `client/peer:TestProbeEndsAPeerThatKeepsChunking`. Reason: a peer that keeps chunking would otherwise hold the probe and its slot for as long as it streams; a read without paths has nothing to report.

### BD-Matter-IpServiceStatus-RestartInCleanup — a status resolution needed again before its cleanup is restarted by that cleanup

A status resolution stopped and needed again before its cleanup ran is restarted by that cleanup (`client/discovery/status.go`, `maybeStartResolving` from the cleanup only when `stopResolving` cancelled the resolution — `statusState.resolveStopped` — and not while the cache closes; a resolution that ended on its own starts nothing there, as matter.js). matter.js clears the handle in the resolution's `.finally` and starts none (`packages/general/src/net/dns-sd/IpServiceStatus.ts:177-185` at `b25ed960`), so an attempt that found the stopped resolution's handle still set (`:153`) gets no resolution until the next `connecting()` or reachable→unreachable change. Review II, R4-conc-4552. Pinned by `client/discovery:TestStatus_ResolutionRestartsWhenNeededAgainBeforeItsCleanup` and `TestStatus_CompletedResolutionStartsNoneW2B5`. Reason: the service would stay unresolved with an attempt outstanding.

### BD-Matter-BLETest-NoHandshakeTimeout — the BLE test peripheral keeps the link after an unanswered handshake request

`controller/ble/bletest` does not model the BTP handshake timeout of matter.js's BLE server. matter.js starts a 15 s timer on the handshake request (`packages/nodejs-ble/src/BlenoBleServer.ts:148-150`, `:258`; `packages/protocol/src/ble/BleConsts.ts:56` at `b25ed960`), stops it on the C2 subscribe (`:297`) and disconnects when it fires (`:413-416`); a subscribe before the request throws (`:288-291`), which the characteristic only logs (`:73-79`) — the central is told nothing, and the request written afterwards runs into the timeout. The kit starts no session for a subscribe before the request and leaves the later request unanswered, but keeps the link: it has no clock, and a central under test ends the attempt by its own handshake timeout (inferred, not run). A test that needs the peripheral's disconnect drops the link itself. Review II, R2-C2-test-2050. Pinned by `controller/ble/bletest:TestSubscribeBeforeTheHandshakeRequestStartsNothing`. Reason: a test kit without a clock stays deterministic.

### BD-Matter-Bridge-AnnounceListsByRead — the announce of a new endpoint lists its attributes by a read, not from the cluster type

The announce of a new endpoint or instance lists the attributes by a read of its servers under a context without the caller's request values (`bridge/bridge.go`, `announceNewEndpoints`, `withoutValues`), and marks the paths that read Success; each subscriber's report is then read again under its own identity and ACL. matter.js lists them from the cluster type without a read: `addCluster` takes the readable, not-changesOmitted attributes of `cluster.type.attributes` and emits `attrsChanged`, with no session or requester (`packages/node/src/node/integration/ProtocolService.ts:290-296` at `b25ed960`; `addCluster(backing)` `:261`). The changes-omitted filter sits in the subscription manager here (`im/subscription/manager.go`, `OnAttributeChanged`), so the two sets agree on that point; a readable attribute whose read does not answer Success is announced there and not here (inferred from the two lists, not run). Review II, R5-par-5106, owner decision 677: the read-free shape needs a new exported enumerator on `endpoint` and is not taken. Pinned by `bridge:TestAnnounceIgnoresTheReassemblyCallersRequest` and `node:TestReplaceUnderARefusingRequestAnnounces`. Reason: no caller's request decides the announced set any more, and every reassembly without a request announces what it announced before.

### BD-Matter-Controller-LeaveLiveAtArrival — a Leave counts only when the subscription was active as its report arrived and is active when the reaction runs

matter.js ignores a BasicInformation Leave while the default subscription is not active, reading `NetworkClient.subscriptionActive` when the reaction runs (`packages/node/src/node/client/Peers.ts:869-880` at `b25ed960`), inside a `Peers.#mutex` task nothing awaits (`:847`; `packages/general/src/util/Mutex.ts:60-72`). The subscription becomes active only after the priming report's `updated` chain ended and the SubscribeResponse arrived (`packages/protocol/src/action/client/ClientInteraction.ts:1097-1100`, `packages/protocol/src/action/client/subscription/SustainedSubscription.ts:224`, `:282`), so the read is false unless the mutex task is delayed behind another mutex task. Here the reaction runs on a goroutine after the report's hooks ran on the node's job queue, with no such ordering (`controller/client/reactions.go` `onEvent`, `onLeave`); it therefore also requires that the subscription was active when the report arrived (`Node.deliveryLive`, read in `node.go` `applyWith`) and keeps matter.js's run-time read. Difference from matter.js: a Leave of a priming report whose reaction is delayed past establishment is ignored here and would delete the node in matter.js. The ShutDown and StartUp reactions and the decommission's leave latch take the same flag; that mirrors matter.js, whose handlers run inside the report's awaited emit, and is no divergence. Reason: it is the rule matter.js states at `Peers.ts:869-873`, made independent of scheduling (issue #628). Pinned by `controller/client:TestLeaveOfPrimingReportReactedLate` and `TestReactionsOfReportBeforeSubscriptionHeldLate`.
